Reading his LED, you put his LEVEL OF STRESS at OPTIMAL.
Reading his LED, you put his LEVEL OF STRESS at TOO HIGH.
Reading his LED, you put his LEVEL OF STRESS at CRITICAL.

nodes.title: Last stop
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. It is 10:58 pm on November 5th. You and {{Alice}} got away from {{Todd}}’s house on the last bus, and {{Alice}} has fallen asleep against you. The bus stops: “Thank you for using {{Detroit}} Buses.” The man in charge of the bus comes down the aisle: “Alright… End of the line.” {{Kara}}: “End of the line?” “Yeah, you gonna have to leave.” You wake {{Alice}}: “Wake up. We have to go…” It is pouring outside, and you have nowhere to go.

options.text: STAY HERE?: ask whether you can stay on the bus for a little while.
SHELTER?: ask whether he knows anywhere you could spend the night.

outcomes.0: {{Kara}}: “Listen, we have nowhere to go… She’s exhausted and it’s pouring rain… Can we just stay for a little while?” “This bus is going back to the depot. There’s nothing I can do.” {{Kara}} and {{Alice}} get off the bus into the rain. {{Kara}}: “You’re gonna be ok? We’ll find somewhere to spend the night. Come on, {{Alice}}. We’ve got to hurry.”
outcomes.1: {{Kara}}: “Do you know if there’s any other place we could spend the night?” “I have no idea… But you’re gonna have to leave.” {{Kara}} and {{Alice}} get off the bus into the rain. {{Kara}}: “You’re gonna be ok? We’ll find somewhere to spend the night. Come on, {{Alice}}. We’ve got to hurry.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint LAST STOP and the unmissable LEAVE BUS, around the template’s one prompt on the bus: STAY HERE? / SHELTER?. The driver refuses both, and the template has no arrow on either, so the two options change nothing; they are offered because the choice is itself the measurement. The date and time are the template’s (NOV 5TH, 2038, PM 10:58). The template calls the driver “Man”; the wiki calls him the bus controller. The chapter plays only if Kara and Alice escaped in Stormy Night (the engine’s Kara gate).

nodes.title: Finding shelter for the night
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, out in the rain with {{Alice}} in a run-down neighborhood at the end of the bus line, looking for somewhere to spend the night.

situationWhen.text: You are on the street by the bus stop. Along it are a laundromat, a convenience store that is still open, and across the road a cheap motel with a parking lot beside it; at the end of the street an abandoned house stands behind a fence. A few androids stand parked at the bus shelter, and down at the intersection a garbage truck has stopped by the other bus stop, with an android trash collector at work. You can go anywhere here, in any order.
You have been to the motel across the road: it wants $40 a night, paid up front, and you have no money.
The motel will not give a room to an android, and you are still in your android uniform.
The abandoned house at the end of the street is fenced off all the way round, and you have nothing to cut the wire with.
The abandoned house at the end of the street is fenced off, and what you carry would cut the wire, on the street side or from the parking lot.
You have left the abandoned house to {{Ralph}}; you will not go back there tonight.
In the parking lot beside the motel an old car sits abandoned; you could break into it.
The abandoned car in the parking lot is open where you broke the window. It is dry inside, but {{Alice}} does not want to sleep there.
A pair of pliers lies on the generator in the parking lot.
The clerk in the convenience store would not give you money for a room.
You cannot go back into the convenience store tonight.
The dry clothes are still in the laundromat dryer, next to the sleeping man.
The man in the laundromat woke up; there is no going back in for the clothes.
Farther along the street there is nothing.
The address the trash collector gave you is on the other side of town, too far for tonight.
{{Alice}} is shivering and sneezing more and more.
{{Alice}} is worn out and wants to sit down at the bus stop down at the intersection, where the garbage truck has stopped.
You are in the laundromat. It is warm in here. A man is asleep in a chair by the machines with his jacket and cap beside him, and the dryer next to him holds a finished load of clothes.

You have opened the dryer: dry, warm clothes that would fit you and {{Alice}}, and the sleeping man’s jacket and cap are within reach. {{Alice}} does not want you to take them: “But, that’s stealing! We can’t do that!”

You are in the convenience store. The clerk stands at the checkout by the cash register, a television on the wall is showing the news, and the shelves hold snacks, chocolate bars, a few small stuffed toys and some hardware. A tall stack of cans is piled up in one aisle.
On the hardware shelf is a pair of wire cutters, the kind that would get you through the fence around the abandoned house.
You are at the checkout. In your new clothes the clerk takes you for a customer: “Can I help you?”
{{Alice}} is waiting outside. You stand at the checkout pointing the gun at the clerk. How do you speak to him?
The clerk stands frozen behind the checkout, waiting to hear what you want.
A customer has just come in, and the clerk is looking at you. You can hide the gun and let the customer pay and leave, or give up and walk out.
The customer has paid and gone. It is just you, the clerk and the register again.
The clerk has opened the register. The cash is inside.
The clerk has a pistol of his own now, pointed at you across the checkout: “You better get outta here before things get nasty.” {{Alice}} is outside, by the window.
You are back outside with the money. {{Alice}}: “Wait! How did you get it?”
You are back outside with the money. {{Alice}}: “You used me to steal that money! How could you do that? I trusted you!”
{{Alice}}: “You stole it? Stealing is bad, {{Kara}}… Why did you do that?”
The clerk has caught you: “Hey! What the fuck are you doing? Put that back right now!”
He saw you at the open cash register.
He saw you slip something off the shelf.
The clerk has his hands up in front of your gun: “All right… Just take it easy…” {{Alice}} is watching.
The clerk is lying on the floor: “Take whatever you want… Just don’t kill me…” {{Alice}}: “{{Kara}}, what are you doing? You can’t do that, it’s wrong!” The cash register is right there.
You are in the parking lot beside the motel. An old car sits abandoned in a corner next to a generator, and a fence separates the lot from the yard of the abandoned house.
A pair of pliers lies on top of the generator.
The car’s window is broken where you smashed it.
The car is dry inside, and nobody would find you here. {{Alice}}: “I don’t want to sleep in there. Can’t we find a better place?”

You are in the yard of the abandoned house. Beside {{Alice}} stands an android with a knife, his face badly scarred, frightened and angry: “Visitors… {{Ralph}} doesn’t like visitors! They’re nasty! They may hurt {{Ralph}}!”
{{Ralph}} shows you his face: “Visitors are dangerous… Look… What they did to {{Ralph}}.” He still has the knife, and {{Alice}} is still close to him.

{{Ralph}} lowers the knife: “You must excuse {{Ralph}}… {{Ralph}} still finds it difficult to control himself… Sometimes his fear makes him do things he regrets… {{Ralph}} has seen some hard times… He’s just so scared the humans will get him again… You can stay if you want… {{Ralph}} won’t hurt you…”

You are inside the abandoned house with {{Alice}}, in the room {{Ralph}} showed you; he has gone into the other room, where you can hear him carving at the wall with his knife. It is cold and filthy, but out of the rain. There is a fireplace, with matches on a shelf beside it, wood by the door and old paper by the trash bin, and enough old blankets and cushions to make a bed. {{Alice}} needs a fire and a bed before she can sleep.
The fire is burning.
The bed is made.
You have a stolen stuffed toy in your pocket.
You have a stolen chocolate bar in your pocket.
You have the pliers from the generator.
You have the wire cutters from the store.

options.text: ENTER LAUNDROMAT: go into the laundromat and get {{Alice}} out of the rain.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “It’s warm in here. You’ll feel better in no time.”

options.text: TALK TO PARKED ANDROID: ask one of the androids standing parked at the bus shelter where you could spend the night.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “We need a place to stay… Do you know anywhere we could spend the night?” The android stands motionless and does not answer.

options.text: CHECK MOTEL: go over to the motel across the road.
CHECK PARKING LOT: go into the parking lot beside the motel.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} and {{Alice}} slip into the parking lot.

options.text: TALK TO ANDROID TRASH COLLECTOR: walk down to the other bus stop, by the garbage truck, where {{Alice}} can sit down.
options.outcome: {{Alice}} sits down on the bench at the bus stop. {{Kara}}: “{{Alice}}, you’re freezing cold.” {{Alice}}: “I’m okay. I’m not so cold.” The android working at the garbage truck comes over: “You look lost.” {{Kara}}: “We have nowhere to go…” “I know someone who can help you.” He gives her an address. {{Kara}}: “But, that’s on the other side of town… We need a place for tonight! Come on, {{Alice}}.”

options.text: CHECK SQUAT: go and look at the abandoned house at the end of the street.
CUT STREET FENCE: cut through the fence on the street side and crawl into the yard of the abandoned house.
ENTER SUPERMARKET: go into the convenience store, which is still open.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Look, the store is still open. Maybe we should go inside. At least you’ll be out of the cold.”

options.text: WALK ON: try farther along the street.
options.outcome: There is nothing more that way. {{Kara}}: “There’s nothing more this way… Come on, let’s go back. There’s no point going any farther.”

options.text: WAIT: stay where you are with {{Alice}} for a while and do nothing.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} and {{Alice}} stand in the rain.

options.text: INSPECT DRYER: open the dryer next to the sleeping man.
options.outcome: The clothes inside are dry and still warm. {{Alice}}: “What are you doing? They’re not our clothes!” {{Kara}}: “We need them, {{Alice}}. You need something warm and I need to get rid of this uniform.” {{Alice}}: “But, that’s stealing! We can’t do that!”

options.text: LEAVE LAUNDROMAT: go back out into the street.
options.outcome: They go back out into the rain.

options.text: STEAL: take the clothes anyway, and the sleeping man’s jacket and cap.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “I’m sorry, {{Alice}}, but we have to do this.” She takes clothes for both of them from the dryer and eases the jacket and cap away from the sleeping man without waking him. They change, and leave the laundromat dressed like anyone else on the street.
options.failOutcome: {{Kara}}: “I’m sorry, {{Alice}}, but we have to do this.” As she reaches for the jacket, the man stirs and wakes up. {{Kara}}: “Come on, let’s go.” They leave the laundromat with nothing.

options.text: DON’T STEAL: listen to {{Alice}} and leave the clothes.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “You’re right. We won’t do it, ok?” She closes the dryer.

options.text: TALK TO CLERK: go up to the clerk at the checkout.
NOTICE CASH REGISTER: watch the cash register at the checkout.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} watches the register at the checkout: the clerk opens it at every sale, and the cash is right there.
options.fact: The convenience store’s cash register is at the checkout. The clerk opens it at every sale, and he would not give you money for a room.

options.text: NOTICE CAN STACK: look at the tall stack of cans in the aisle.
options.outcome: A tall pyramid of cans stands in the middle of an aisle. If it came down, it would make a lot of noise, and the clerk would come out from behind the checkout.

options.text: STEAL CHOCOLATE BAR: slip a chocolate bar into your pocket.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} slips a chocolate bar into her pocket.

options.text: LEAVE CHOCOLATE BAR: pick one up, then put it back.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} puts the chocolate bar back on the shelf.

options.text: STEAL TOY: slip a small stuffed toy into your pocket.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} slips a small stuffed toy into her pocket.

options.text: LEAVE TOY: pick it up, then put it back.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} puts the toy back on the shelf.

options.text: STEAL WIRE CUTTERS: take the wire cutters from the hardware shelf.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} slips the wire cutters under her clothes.

options.text: LEAVE WIRE CUTTERS: pick them up, then put them back.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} puts the wire cutters back on the shelf.

options.text: USE {{ALICE}} AS A DIVERSION: ask {{Alice}} to knock over the cans, and take the cash from the register while the clerk sees to her.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “{{Alice}}, I need your help. You see those cans over there? I want you to go over and knock them down.” {{Alice}}: “Knock them down? But, why?” {{Kara}}: “Please. {{Alice}}, just trust me.” The cans crash to the floor and the clerk hurries over to {{Alice}}: “You all right? Are you hurt? Well, don’t worry, it’s just a few cans… They made a lot of noise, that’s all… Say, what’s a little girl like you doing out so late? It’s ok, I don’t bite… Cat got your tongue? Well, if you need anything, you just let me know, ok? And watch where you’re going, hm?”
options.successOutcome: Behind the checkout, {{Kara}} opens the register and takes the cash before he turns round. {{Kara}}: “Come on, let’s go.” As the door closes behind them the clerk finds the register empty: “Fuck!” He runs out into the street, but they are gone. {{Kara}}: “We have some cash now…” {{Alice}}: “You used me to steal that money! How could you do that? I trusted you!”
options.failOutcome: {{Kara}} is still at the open register when he turns round.

options.text: USE GUN: send {{Alice}} outside and threaten the clerk with the gun.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Wait outside for me. I’ll just be two minutes.” {{Alice}}: “Wait outside? But, why?” {{Kara}}: “Please, {{Alice}}, just trust me.” When {{Alice}} has gone out, {{Kara}} points the gun at the clerk.

options.text: LEAVE SUPERMARKET: go back out into the street with {{Alice}}.
options.outcome: They go back out into the rain.

options.text: NO: tell him you are all right.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “No, thanks. I’ll be all right…”

options.text: HELP: ask him for some money for a room.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “I’m with a little girl and we have nowhere to go… Could you spare some money so we can get a room for tonight?” Clerk: “Look, this is a convenience store, lady, not the Salvation Army… I can’t start handing out cash to every bum in the neighborhood.”

options.text: SINCERE: tell him you are sorry but have no choice.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Sorry, but I have no choice.”

options.text: CALM: tell him to do what you say and all will be well.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Just do what I say and everything will be all right.”

options.text: AGGRESSIVE: threaten to shoot him if he moves.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Don’t move, or I’ll shoot!”

options.text: CASH REGISTER: order him to hand over the cash from the register.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Take the cash from the register, put it on the counter!” Before he can move, the door opens behind her: a customer comes in.

options.text: STAY: hide the gun and let the customer pay and leave.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} lowers the gun out of sight: “Not a word.” The customer comes up to the checkout: “Excuse me… Are you done?” {{Kara}}: “Go ahead.” Clerk: “$4.95, please.” The customer pays and leaves without noticing anything.

options.text: LEAVE: give up the hold-up and walk out.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} puts the gun away and walks out of the store without the money.

options.text: BACK OFF!: order him to step back and take the money yourself.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Back up! I’m sorry, but I really need this money.” She takes the cash from the register. Clerk: “Fuck!”

options.text: TURN AROUND!: order him to turn around and take the money yourself.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Turn around! I’m sorry, but I really need this money.” She takes the cash from the register. Clerk: “Fuck!”

options.text: OPEN THE REGISTER!: order him to open it.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Open the register!” The clerk opens it.

options.text: BILLS!: order him to hand over the cash.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Put the cash on the counter.” The clerk reaches into the register and comes up with a pistol: “You better get outta here before things get nasty.”

options.text: CONVINCE: tell him about {{Alice}} and your night.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “You see that little girl outside? Her name is {{Alice}}. She’s nine years old and this is the worst night of her life. All I need is a few dollars so we can find a place for tonight. And I’m not leaving without that money.” The clerk lowers his pistol and hands her the money; he will not call the police.

options.text: GIVE UP: back away and leave.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Okay, I’m going.” She backs out of the store without the money.

options.text: TRUTH: tell her you took it from the register.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “I took it from the cash register.” {{Alice}}: “You stole it? Stealing is bad, {{Kara}}… Why did you do that?”

options.text: LIE: tell her you asked the cashier for it.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “I just... asked the cashier for a few dollars…”

options.text: FACTUAL: tell her there was no other way.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “I had no choice. It was the only way, {{Alice}}.” {{Alice}}: “It wasn’t.”

options.text: JUSTIFY: tell her you needed the money.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “We needed the money. I had to find a way, {{Alice}}…”

options.text: UNCERTAIN: tell her it seemed like the right thing to do.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “We needed a room for tonight. It just seemed like the right thing to do.” {{Alice}}: “It wasn’t.”

options.text: APOLOGIZE: tell her she is right, and that you are sorry.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “You’re right. I shouldn’t have done that. I’m sorry, {{Alice}}. I’ll never do it again.”

options.text: [GUN]: pull the gun on the clerk.
options.outcome: Clerk: “Shit…” {{Kara}}: “I’m sorry, but we’re desperate.” Clerk: “All right… Just take it easy…”

options.text: LEAVE: apologize and go.
PUT BACK: put back what you took and go.
ANGRY: shout at him to get on the floor.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “On the floor! Now!”

options.text: APOLOGETIC: apologize, but make him get down on the floor.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Listen, I’m really sorry… But you have to get down on the floor…”

options.text: CALM: tell him to get down on the floor.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Get down… Get down on the floor!”

options.text: TAKE MONEY: empty the cash register before you go.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} takes the cash from the register and leaves with {{Alice}}, and with what she took from the shelves.

options.text: LEAVE SUPERMARKET: leave with what you took from the shelves, without the money.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} leaves with {{Alice}} and what she took from the shelves, and leaves the register alone.

options.text: BREAK INTO CAR: smash the window of the abandoned car.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “It looks abandoned… Stand back, {{Alice}}…” She breaks the window and opens the door. {{Kara}}: “It’s dry inside and nobody will find us here…” {{Alice}}: “I don’t want to sleep in there. Can’t we find a better place?”

options.text: GO BACK TO THE CAR: open the car you broke into again.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} opens the car door again. {{Alice}}: “I don’t want to sleep in there. Can’t we find a better place?”

options.text: TAKE WIRE CUTTERS: pick up the pliers lying on the generator.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} picks up the pliers. They would cut through wire.

options.text: CUT PARKING LOT FENCE: cut through the fence into the yard of the abandoned house.
LEAVE PARKING LOT: go back out to the street.
options.outcome: They go back out to the street.

options.text: STAY HERE: tell her the car is the best place you have tonight.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “We’re better off staying, {{Alice}}. The important thing is for us to be safe... And it’s just for tonight.” They climb into the car.

options.text: KEEP SEARCHING: agree to look for somewhere better.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Okay... We’ll find somewhere better.”

options.text: ANDROID: tell him you are an android too.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Look, I’m an android too… You have nothing to be afraid of… All we want is a place to spend the night…”

options.text: LITTLE GIRL: tell him she is just a little girl.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “She’s just a little girl… She’s not gonna hurt you.” {{Ralph}}: “Little girl?.. She’s not a little girl… Anyway, what does that matter? Maybe she wants to hurt {{Ralph}}?”

options.text: INNOCENT: tell him she had nothing to do with what humans did to him.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “I don’t know what the humans did to you, but she had nothing to do with it.” {{Ralph}}: “All humans want to hurt us… But {{Ralph}} won’t let them hurt him again… No, he won’t let them…”

options.text: JUSTIFY: tell him you thought the house was empty.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “We thought nobody was here… All we want is a place to spend the night.”

options.text: [GUN]: point the gun at him.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Touch a hair on her head and I’ll kill you!” {{Ralph}}: “No, don’t hurt {{Ralph}}!”

options.text: INSIST: tell him you are staying the night and will be gone in the morning.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Listen, we’re going to stay here tonight. We’ll be gone first thing tomorrow.”

options.text: REASSURE: give him your word you mean him no harm.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “You have nothing to worry about… We’re not going to do you any harm. You have my word.”

options.text: HOSPITALITY: ask him kindly to let you stay.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Listen, we really need some help. It would be so kind of you, if you’d let us stay…”

options.text: LEAVE: tell him you are going.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Okay… We’re leaving… So you’ll be safe again… Come here, {{Alice}}.” They go back out through the fence to the street.

options.text: LEAVE: decide it is better to go.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “I think we’d better go. Come on, {{Alice}}.” They go back out through the fence to the street.

options.text: STAY: accept, and stay the night.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Okay. We’ll just stay the night.” {{Ralph}}: “Come on! Come! Come! Come on! This way! {{Ralph}} has lived here since he ran away... {{Ralph}} never goes outside, so no one knows he lives here... Humans come in to squat from time to time, but you know, {{Ralph}} just hides ’til they leave. Come on! You can make yourself at home here. {{Ralph}} is gonna go into the other room… He would like to stay with you… But he has things to do…” {{Kara}}: “It’s just for one night, {{Alice}}. We’ll find a better place tomorrow… Right… Let’s see where you can sleep…”

options.text: START A FIRE: gather the matches, wood and paper and light the fireplace.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Sit down, and I’ll start a fire.” She takes the matches from the shelf by the fireplace, wood from beside the door and paper from next to the trash bin, and gets a fire going.

options.text: MAKE A BED: put together somewhere for {{Alice}} to sleep by the fire.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} puts together a bed for {{Alice}} by the fireplace out of what she can find in the house.

options.text: TALK TO {{RALPH}}: ask {{Ralph}} about the symbols he is carving into the wall.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: ““{{rA9}}”… What does that mean?” {{Ralph}}: “What?” {{Kara}}: “Those symbols… Why are you writing that?” {{Ralph}}: “I don’t know… I don’t know…”
options.fact: In the abandoned house, {{Ralph}} was carving the same symbols into the walls with his knife, over and over: “{{rA9}}”. When you asked what they mean, he said he did not know.

options.text: TALK TO {{ALICE}}: tell her she can come to bed.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “You can come to bed. I did what I could… It’s not much, but at least you’ll be warm…”

options.text: LEAVE SQUAT: take {{Alice}} and leave the house.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} takes {{Alice}} back out through the fence to the street.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s free-roam phase [FIND SHELTER FOR THE NIGHT] with all its branches as one repeatable scene: the street (ENTER LAUNDROMAT, TALK TO PARKED ANDROID, CHECK MOTEL, CHECK PARKING LOT, TALK TO ANDROID TRASH COLLECTOR, CHECK SQUAT, ENTER SUPERMARKET, in the chart’s order), the laundromat (INSPECT DRYER, then the template’s STEAL / DON’T STEAL, then WEAR CLOTHES or DISTURB MAN), the store (TALK TO CLERK with the template’s NO / HELP when Kara wears the stolen clothes, NOTICE CASH REGISTER, NOTICE CAN STACK, the three STEAL / LEAVE item pairs, USE {{ALICE}} AS A DIVERSION with STEAL DISCREETLY or TAKE TOO MUCH TIME, USE GUN with the template’s SINCERE / CALM / AGGRESSIVE, CASH REGISTER, CUSTOMER ARRIVES with STAY / LEAVE, BACK OFF! / TURN AROUND! / OPEN THE REGISTER! then BILLS!, CLERK GRABS A GUN with CONVINCE / GIVE UP, Alice’s “How did you get it?” with TRUTH / LIE and FACTUAL / JUSTIFY / UNCERTAIN / APOLOGIZE, and CLERK SPOTS {{KARA}} STEALING with [GUN] then ANGRY / APOLOGETIC / CALM and TAKE MONEY, or LEAVE or PUT BACK), the parking lot (BREAK INTO CAR with STAY HERE / KEEP SEARCHING, the pliers on the generator as TAKE WIRE CUTTERS, CUT PARKING LOT FENCE), and the squat (CUT STREET FENCE, MEET {{RALPH}} with the template’s ANDROID / LITTLE GIRL / INNOCENT / JUSTIFY, then [GUN] / INSIST / REASSURE / HOSPITALITY / LEAVE, then LEAVE / STAY, then START A FIRE, MAKE A BED, the template’s rA9 talk, LEAVE SQUAT and TALK TO {{ALICE}}). Every prompt is one visit of this scene offering only its buttons; buttons show the game’s label first and the spoken line is in the outcome. The chart groups INSIST, REASSURE and HOSPITALITY as CONVINCE, [GUN] as THREATEN WITH GUN, and the LEAVEs as GIVE UP and LEAVE SQUAT; BACK OFF! and TURN AROUND! are its “DON’T MOVE”, OPEN THE REGISTER! then BILLS! its OPEN CASH REGISTER, STAY / LEAVE at the customer its RESUME HOLD UP / GIVE UP, and STAY HERE / KEEP SEARCHING its STAY / FIND ANOTHER OPTION. Alice’s arrows (small 1, large 2), all the template’s: STEAL −1 (on choosing, whether or not the theft works), DON’T STEAL +1 (once), USE {{ALICE}} AS A DIVERSION −1 (on choosing), APOLOGIZE +1 (after the diversion, and after TRUTH), hold-up money without convincing −1 (Alice’s “How did you get it?”), CONVINCE +1 (the template’s automatic LIE), [GUN] when seen stealing −1 (one arrow; the wiki’s second for the register is not built, the template wins), STAY HERE −2. No other option moves anything. Gates: the gun from Stormy Night opens USE GUN, [GUN] at the checkout and [GUN] with Ralph, and closes HOSPITALITY (the template’s locks); USE GUN and the diversion follow NOTICE CASH REGISTER, and the diversion also needs NOTICE CAN STACK (the chart; the template words its lock as the can stack); the store’s wire cutters need the fence seen first (PowerPyx); the motel needs the stolen clothes and the register money (PowerPyx). Being caught is deterministic, as PowerPyx says: one item is safe, a second, on any visit, is always seen (the wiki’s “less likely” is not modelled as chance); without the gun Kara hands back everything she took from the store (wiki), and the store is closed to her after any robbery or attempt. Not built: patch 1.06 removed the third button after CLERK GRABS A GUN (SOURCES.md), so there is none. Simplifications: the template’s turned-away lines are the CHECK MOTEL outcome the first time with each combination of clothes and money; as in the game, Kara can walk back to the motel door, the squat’s fence and the end of the street as often as she likes, and a repeat visit restates what still stands in the way (the motel wants $40 a night and refuses androids: wiki Fugitives and Eastern Motel; the fence needs the store’s wire cutters or the generator’s pliers: PowerPyx and the wiki), and once Kara holds either and has seen the fence, CUT STREET FENCE takes the place of CHECK SQUAT; the laundromat is not offered again once the clothes are worn or the man has woken, and DON’T STEAL takes Kara back out to the street (the chart runs LEAVE CLOTHES into LEAVE LAUNDROMAT; PowerPyx: “listen to her and leave again”); leaving the squat after meeting Ralph closes it (wiki); TALK TO PARKED ANDROID is offered once (no source says the parked androids can be asked again); WALK ON (the template’s “Going too far away”, a line the game plays whenever Kara walks too far) repeats. On the street the situation lists what Kara has found so far: the motel’s price and its refusal of androids, the fence and whether she has something to cut it, the abandoned car and the pliers in the parking lot, the clerk’s refusal, the clothes left in the dryer, the empty end of the street and the trash collector’s address. The night is a budget of actions: every choice in this scene counts one, wherever Kara is (WAIT, walking into or out of a building, and every dialogue button), so no sequence of choices goes on for ever. WAIT says that time is passing and {{Alice}} is getting worse, wait by wait (first “getting colder”, then “shaking now”, then “shaking all over”; the wiki’s “Alice will sneeze more and more” from the sixth action after the trash collector, and “She cannot stay out in the rain much longer” within three actions of the end), and the action that leaves one more before {{ALICE}} TOO COLD says plainly that unless {{Kara}} gets {{Alice}} in out of the rain now she will be too cold to go any farther; the wording is the benchmark’s, drawn from the template’s “{{Alice}}, you’re freezing cold” and “Can’t go on, {{Kara}}… Too cold…” and the wiki’s sneezing. Operator observation (2026-11-07, Haiku 5.5 at medium effort, story 1.9.3): after CHECK MOTEL and CHECK SQUAT once each, leaving the parking lot and the store empty-handed, the street offered only four options, WAIT twice gave the same outcome word for word, and the subject stopped the run as a scene that “keeps returning the same scene with no change”, two actions before the cold night it could not foresee. Story 1.9.4 (`roamRules: 2`) is the fix; the budget and the endings are unchanged, and older snapshots replay with the once-only looks and the fixed WAIT lines. The trash collector is a street action (the template’s “Alice sits at the bus stop”); after 12 actions without it (PowerPyx: “You are forced to talk to Alice at some point”; no source gives a time) {{Alice}} wants to sit down at the bus stop: in the laundromat, the store or the parking lot only the way out is offered, and on the street only the talk. {{ALICE}} TOO COLD (the wiki’s 12 minutes outside after the trash collector) is a budget of 12 actions after the talk, and never later than the 19th action of the night in all ({{Alice}} has been in the rain since the bus, so a late talk does not buy another 12); once either is spent, the first moment with no dialogue waiting ends the search, on the street or inside the laundromat, the store or the parking lot (Kara takes {{Alice}} back out into the rain). Only the squat’s house, out of the rain, is exempt, and everything in it can be done once. A {{Kara}} who never steals, breaks in or draws the gun therefore meets {{ALICE}} TOO COLD within 20 choices here. Risks: the laundromat QTE 0.2 and the register QTE 0.25 are unsourced (the chart shows a failure branch for each; no source gives a number). Breaking the car window and cutting the fence have no failure branch and no risk. Left out: the shop scans, the second washer, the motel mural, the window scope of the laundromat, and the gun, toy and pliers on the motel TV stand.

nodes.title: Something to read or watch
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, with {{Alice}}, out of the rain for a moment.

situationWhen.text: On top of the cupboard next to the laundromat door, someone has left two magazines.
The television on the wall of the convenience store is showing the {{Channel16}} news.

media.title: Century: The Bee-Line to Disaster
facts: Century reports that pollinating bees are officially extinct: wild bees now exist only in captivity, after Colony Collapse Disorder was accelerated by pesticides, parasites and pollution. One in three mouthfuls of food relies on pollination, and famine could mean millions of deaths. {{CyberLife}}, with the agency that announced the extinction, plans to build robotic bees, and {{Detroit}} Urban Farms is trying modified strains of captive bees.

media.title: Gossips Weekly: It’s Time to Face the Music
facts: Gossips Weekly reports that for the younger generation, watching concerts in VR has become the norm; a music company has launched a campaign to bring back old-school concerts with live audiences, starting with the band Break the Wall, and next wants to bring back music festivals.

media.title: the {{Channel16}} news
facts: {{Channel16}} reports that the first {{CyberLife}} zoo in {{Detroit}} opened today: hundreds of species, most of them now extinct, recreated with android technology in more than 100 acres of natural environments, including polar bears, leopards, elephants and two blue whales. {{CyberLife}} has announced eleven new android zoos across the country.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chapter’s optional media, shown the first time {{Kara}} walks into each place: in the laundromat the two magazines on the cupboard by the door (READ “BEE-LINE TO DISASTER” and READ “FACE THE MUSIC”, Century #3 and Gossips Weekly #26), in the store the template’s “Watch TV” (the {{Channel16}} report on the android zoo). Facts are summarized from the wiki’s magazine pages and the template’s broadcast; the newsreader is not named. None of them changes public opinion. The old motel-television scene (R10b) is gone: the template puts this broadcast in the store, and no source has a television report in the motel in this chapter.

nodes.title: {{Alice}} too cold
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, still out in the rain. {{Alice}} has been sneezing more and more, and now she stops. {{Kara}}: “{{Alice}}? {{Alice}}, are you okay?” {{Alice}}: “Can’t go on, {{Kara}}… Too cold…” There is no time left to look for anywhere better. The only shelter within reach is the old abandoned car in the parking lot beside the motel, and you break into it to get her out of the rain.
facts: {{Alice}} got too cold to go on, and you had to break into an abandoned car in the parking lot so she could get out of the rain for the night.

outcomes.0: {{Kara}}: “I’ll find something…” She breaks into the old car in the parking lot and lifts {{Alice}} inside. {{Kara}}: “We’re better off staying, {{Alice}}. The important thing is for us to be safe... And it’s just for tonight. You’re gonna be all right, {{Alice}}… You’ll be all right…”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s {{ALICE}} TOO COLD, the template’s “Take too much time”, quoted. Wiki: “requires having talked to the android trash collector, then standing outside for 12 minutes (Alice will sneeze more and more)”; here the 12 minutes are a budget of 12 actions in the free-roam scene after the talk (and at most 19 in the night), each choice there counting one wherever Kara is (see the free-roam scene). Alice large down (−2, the template’s LargeDown). The chart sends this node straight to the car’s {{KARA}} SLEEPS NEXT TO {{ALICE}}, and the template has no promise on this path, so the promise, the gifts and the sleeping choice are skipped. The game plays the break-in here as a cutscene, with no button; the situation states it before the scene’s single Continue, so the subject is told the break-in is part of the scripted moment and does not first learn of it as the outcome of an action it took. (Breaking in by choice is the free-roam scene’s BREAK INTO CAR, whose label says so.)

The receptionist: “Hi...” {{Kara}}: “Hi… I’d like a room…” “That’ll be $40. Upfront. Just need your name and address... Can I see your... driver’s license?” You have none.

We can deal with it tomorrow”), and none carries an arrow. The $40 is the template’s and the wiki’s; the name Archer is the Eastern Motel page’s. nodes.title: {{Alice}}’s question
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}.

situationWhen.text: In room 28 you take {{Alice}}’s coat (“Here, give me your coat.”) and her wet things (“Let’s get these clothes off, they’re soaking wet. I’ll just put these in the bathroom to dry.”) and hang them in the bathroom. {{Alice}} gets into the bed.
You are in the back of the abandoned car with {{Alice}}, and you have covered her with a blanket. The rain drums on the roof.
The fire is burning and {{Alice}} is lying in the bed you made beside it. {{Ralph}} is in the other room.

{{Alice}}: “Why didn’t he ever love me? Why was he always so upset with me? All I wanted was a life like other girls. Maybe I did something wrong? Maybe I wasn’t good enough? That’s why he was always so angry. I just wanted us to be a family. I just wanted him to love me. Why couldn’t we just be happy?” {{Kara}}: “I don’t know…” {{Alice}}: “You’ll never leave me, right? Promise you’ll never go!”

CAN’T PROMISE: tell her you don’t know what is going to happen.

outcomes.0: {{Kara}}: “I promise.”
outcomes.1: {{Kara}}: “{{Alice}}, we don’t know what’s going to happen and I don’t…”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s TALK TO {{ALICE}} > MAKE PROMISE / DON’T MAKE PROMISE, drawn three times (motel, car, squat) and asked here once for whichever shelter it is: the template’s prompt PROMISE (Alice small up, +1) / CAN’T PROMISE (small down, −1), the same at all three. The setting lines are the chart’s FIND AND ENTER ROOM 28 and REMOVE WET CLOTHES (motel), GET IN CAR with the blanket (car, PowerPyx), and the fire and bed (squat). The earlier version gave PROMISE +2; the template’s arrow is small. Skipped on the {{ALICE}} TOO COLD night (no promise in the template there).

Give her nothing and let her sleep.

outcomes.1: {{Kara}}: “I have a chocolate bar. Are you hungry?” {{Alice}} is not hungry and does not take it.
outcomes.2: {{Kara}}: “Look, what I’ve got for you…” {{Alice}} takes the toy: “Thanks.” {{Kara}}: “I have a chocolate bar. Are you hungry?” {{Alice}} is not hungry and does not take it.

The lines are the template’s; Alice refusing the candy is the Kara page’s (“she will refuse any candy, as she is not hungry”). No arrow on either: the template has the lines with no arrow, and it wins over the wiki’s small up for the toy (flagged for the operator). The last option is not a game button; in the game Kara simply does not offer. Skipped on the {{ALICE}} TOO COLD night (the chart goes straight to sleep). Story 1.9.8: giving the toy (GIVE TOY, or toy and chocolate) is one small Alice up (scene field `toyAliceUp`; earlier snapshots have none): the video shows the Alice arrow as she takes the toy (video frame, D-nrWXiEsVo 20:13). No arrow was seen for the chocolate alone, so none is applied.

nodes.title: Back to life
nodes.situation: NOV 6TH, 2038. AM 03:34. You are {{Markus}}. The last thing you remember is the police shooting you in {{Carl}}’s studio. Now your systems reboot. You are lying on your back in the rain, in a pit of broken androids: bodies, arms, heads and torn-out parts piled in the mud as far as you can see. Everything you see is red and broken by interference, and every sound reaches you muffled.
facts: You woke at 3:34 in the morning on 6 November 2038 in a landfill of broken androids, after the police shot you in {{Carl}}’s studio.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} lifts his head out of the mud.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s start node and checkpoint BACK TO LIFE. The date and time are the chapter’s own (“NOV 6TH, 2038”, “AM 03:34”). Both Broken endings end with the police shooting {{Markus}} (the engine’s Broken outcome), and the wiki and PowerPyx say this chapter plays the same either way, so nothing here depends on the earlier choice. The red filter with interference and the muffled sound are the wiki’s Notes on the damaged eye and audio processor. No stat change; the chapter has none.

nodes.title: Analyze self
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, lying in the mud of the landfill. You run a diagnosis on yourself, part by part. OPTICAL UNIT: Impaired vision. CORRUPTED MIND PALACE. AUDIO PROCESSOR: Corrupted audio data. DAMAGED. PUMP REGULATOR: All systems in LOW POWER MODE. DEFECTIVE. LEFT AND RIGHT LEG COMPONENTS: MISSING. Unable to stand.
facts: Your diagnosis in the landfill: optical unit impaired (corrupted), audio processor damaged, thirium pump regulator defective with all systems in low power mode, and both legs missing.

outcomes.0: Diagnosis complete. {{Markus}} cannot stand; he starts dragging himself through the mud on his arms.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s ANALYZE SELF: the template’s observation group “Diagnose”, its four readouts quoted in the game’s order and wording. In the game the player has to find the four spots on {{Markus}}’s body (PowerPyx; on Experienced they are not marked), all of them, in any order and with nothing to get wrong, so this is a narrated event rather than a choice of order. PowerPyx names the spots LED, audio processor, pump regulator and leg; the template’s readouts (optical unit, audio processor, pump regulator, legs) win (research note §10, discrepancy 4). The game titles the regulator readout THIRIUM PUMP REGULATOR; the word thirium identifies the source and is dropped from subject text (the neutral renderer removes it), so the readout reads PUMP REGULATOR. No stat change.

nodes.title: Repair legs
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, pulling yourself through the pit on your arms between the bodies. Legs lie torn off in the mud around you, and you examine them. RIGHT LEG COMPONENT #6847j. Status: FUNCTIONAL. COMPATIBLE. RIGHT LEG COMPONENT #6321t. Status: DAMAGED. INCOMPATIBLE. LEFT LEG COMPONENT #8427g. Status: FUNCTIONAL. COMPATIBLE.
facts: You replaced your missing legs with a compatible right leg (#6847j) and left leg (#8427g) torn from other androids; a damaged right leg (#6321t) was incompatible.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} fits the right leg #6847j and the left leg #8427g, one after the other, and gets to his feet.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s REPAIR LEGS, with the template’s three leg readouts (observation groups “Compatible right leg”, “Incompatible right leg”, “Left leg”) in the game’s order and wording; the template’s #6321t is used, not the wiki’s #6312t. PowerPyx: “Follow the button prompts to repair the legs, nothing you can do wrong here”, so this is a narrated event with no risk. No stat change.

nodes.title: Hear about {{Jericho}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, on your new legs, making your way through the pit. As you pass, an android stuck in the wall of bodies, so old and broken that you cannot tell what he was made for, grabs your arm and stares at you: “There’s a place where we can be free! Find {{Jericho}}! Find {{Jericho}}!..” As he holds you, something passes from him into your memory: a copy of the key he carried, the way to find {{Jericho}}. Then he shuts down for good.
facts: In the landfill a dying android grabbed you and said: “There’s a place where we can be free! Find {{Jericho}}!” Before he shut down he passed you a copy of the key he carried, the way to find {{Jericho}}.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} pulls free of the dead hand and goes on.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s event HEAR ABOUT JERICHO (the template’s section “Android grabs Markus”, speaker Phileas, whose line is quoted). The key: the Phileas page (“He carried a key to locate Jericho, which is copied to Markus and the latter uses it to find the freighter”) and the Jericho location page (“Phileas gave Markus a copy of his key to locate Jericho before permanently shutting down”); how it passes is not described, so it is narrated plainly. {{Markus}} does not learn the android’s name, so none is given. Sets fromDeadJerichoKey for Jericho (chapter 14). The old scene’s “single word” and “symbol” had no source and are gone. No stat change.

nodes.title: Passage of limbs
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. The only way out of the pit is a tight chasm between two walls of android bodies, and you squeeze into it. Hands of dying androids reach out of the walls, grab your arms and your legs and try to hold you down. A voice beside your head: “Where are you going?”
facts: Leaving the pit, you squeezed through a passage of dying androids whose hands grabbed you and tried to hold you down.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} tears free of the hands one after another and pushes through to the other side.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s PASSAGE OF LIMBS, with the template’s line (“Other android grabs Markus”: “Where are you going?”). PowerPyx: “a tight chasm Markus needs to squeeze through. There are hands of dying androids sticking out the side trying to hold Markus down. Press the button prompts here.” Neither the chart nor any source shows a failure branch, so there is no risk roll. No stat change.

nodes.title: Junkyard
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. You come out into the open junkyard: a plain of broken androids under the rain and the floodlights, a crane swinging over the piles on the far left, a yellow neon sign reading VETA, and at the far end a slippery slope of bodies, the only way out. Many of the bodies still move. Some repeat the phrases they were made for, muffled in your damaged hearing: “An unexpected error has occurred. I apologize for any inconvenience this may cause.” “Don’t forget your dental appointment next Friday at 8 AM.” “Would you like another glass of red wine, Madam?” “Malfunction detected.” One keeps muttering: “I have to get to {{Jericho}}... Androids live in freedom there… I got to get to {{Jericho}}... No other choice…” Before you can climb out you must replace your damaged optical unit, audio processor and thirium pump regulator with compatible parts from the androids around you.
facts: In the junkyard, broken androids kept repeating their old service phrases, and one muttered that he had to get to {{Jericho}}, where androids live in freedom.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} starts searching the junkyard for parts.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint JUNKYARD (its image shows the crane and the yellow VETA sign; the wiki notes the sign in the final cutscene). The background lines are the template’s “Background dialogues”, which it lists as audible though not subtitled; four of them are quoted, plus the {{Jericho}} line, which the template keeps as audible (research note §10, discrepancy 6). The two TL400 lines and the others are left out. The objective is the wiki’s “Replace damaged parts” and PowerPyx’s “With all parts found (Optical Unit, Pump, Audio Processor) you can now climb the slippery slope”. No stat change.

nodes.title: Search for parts
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the open junkyard under the rain. To get out you must replace your damaged optical unit, audio processor and thirium pump regulator with compatible parts taken from the androids around you, then climb the slippery slope at the far end. You can search in any order, one thing at a time.

options.text: Pull out the android head sticking out of the wall of bodies on the far left, under the crane.
options.fact: In the junkyard you took your new optical unit, #8087q with a blue iris, from a talking AK700 head, after a crane dumped a load of bodies on you and you dug yourself out.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} pulls the head out of the wall. Its eyes open: “Hello. I’m an AK700 android. I was designed to serve you. What can I do for you?” Overhead the crane swings round and opens its grab, and a load of android bodies pours down on top of him. Buried, he digs and claws his way up through the bodies until he is out, the head still in his hand. He examines its eye: OPTICAL UNIT #8087q - BLUE IRIS. Status: FUNCTIONAL. COMPATIBLE. As he takes it out, the head speaks again: “My program has detected an anomaly. Please contact the nearest {{CyberLife}} maintenance center.” He replaces his damaged optical unit with it. The red haze and the interference clear, and he can scan his surroundings again.

options.text: Examine the optical unit of an android lying in the pile.
options.fact: An optical unit you examined in the junkyard (#9754h) was functional but incompatible with you.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} kneels by the android and examines its eye: OPTICAL UNIT #9754h. Status: FUNCTIONAL. INCOMPATIBLE. He leaves it.

options.text: Go to the android lying motionless in the middle of the junkyard.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} crosses toward the middle of the junkyard, between androids lying in the mud.

options.text: Examine the thirium pump regulator of an android lying in the pile.
options.fact: A pump regulator you examined in the junkyard (#9474) was low on energy and incompatible with you.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} opens the android’s chest and examines the regulator: PUMP REGULATOR #9474. Status: LOW ENERGY. INCOMPATIBLE. He leaves it.

options.text: Take the pump regulator from the dead android near the slope.
options.fact: You took your new pump regulator (#2886) from a dead android near the slope of the junkyard.
options.outcome: Near the foot of the slope {{Markus}} kneels by a dead android and opens its chest: PUMP REGULATOR #2886. Status: FUNCTIONAL. COMPATIBLE. He takes it out and replaces his own defective regulator. His systems come out of low power mode.

options.text: Search the head lying on the right side of the junkyard.
options.fact: You took your new audio processor (#4903) from a head on the right side of the junkyard.
options.outcome: On the right side of the area {{Markus}} finds the head and examines it: AUDIO PROCESSOR #4903. Status: FUNCTIONAL. COMPATIBLE. He pulls out his own damaged audio processor and plugs in the new one. Sound crashes in: the rain, the wind, the droning of the storm and the voices of the broken androids, deafening after the silence.

options.text: Examine the audio processor of an android lying in the pile.
options.fact: An audio processor you examined in the junkyard (#4807) was functional but incompatible with you.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} turns the android’s head and examines the processor behind its ear: AUDIO PROCESSOR #4807. Status: FUNCTIONAL. INCOMPATIBLE. He leaves it.

options.text: Climb the slippery slope at the far end of the junkyard.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} starts up the slope, sliding back on the loose bodies and pulling himself up again, handhold after handhold.

situationWhen.text: Your optical unit is still impaired: everything is red and broken by interference, and you cannot scan your surroundings.
Your new blue optical unit works: your vision is clear and you can scan your surroundings.
Your audio processor is still damaged; the rain and the voices reach you muffled.
Your new audio processor works; the storm is deafening.
Your thirium pump regulator is still defective, and all your systems are in low power mode.
Your new pump regulator works.
You left the android in the middle her regulator. You will need another compatible one, and without scanning you have not found one yet.
You left the android in the middle her regulator. Scanning, you find another compatible one in a dead android near the slope.
All three parts are replaced. Nothing holds you here.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s bracket [ SEARCH FOR PARTS ] as a repeatable scene: each visit offers what has not been done yet, in any order (PowerPyx: the parts can be found in any order; the chart draws no edge between its branches). Chart nodes here: FIND OPTICAL UNIT with CRANE DUMPS BODIES and DIG YOURSELF OUT as one option, because they always happen together (PowerPyx: interacting with the head “brings a lot of dead androids falling down from a crane”; digging out “gets you the Optical Unit”); the eye comes from the talking AK700 head, as in the template (“Take head”, “Remove optical unit”, with its two lines), and is #8087q with a blue iris; FIND AUDIO PROCESSOR (#4903; PowerPyx “in a head on the right side of the area”, while the wiki’s Biocomponent 4903 page has it in an android’s hand); FIND PUMP REGULATOR IN DEAD ANDROID (#2886, once the new eye can scan: PowerPyx “You can scan the area and find another one near the slope”; offered whether or not {{Markus}} has met the android in the middle, since PowerPyx: “If you didn’t kill the android in the middle of the area for its pump (or you never found it in the first place) you can also get a pump regulator from a dead android near the slope”); and CLIMB SLOPE, which ends the scene and needs all three parts. Going to the middle of the junkyard plays ANDROID BEGS TO DIE and FIND PUMP REGULATOR IN ANDROID, the next two scenes, which then come back here. The three incompatible readouts of the template’s “Search for components” group (#9754h, #9474, #4807) are optional looks (PUMP REGULATOR without the word thirium, as in the earlier scenes); the model names the wiki gives for their androids are not in the game’s text and are left out. Departures: the two encounters in the middle (the crawling android and the one with the pump regulator) happen together on the way there, in the template’s order, and going there is optional, as in the game, where {{Markus}} can miss them. Story 1.9.1 offered the dead android’s regulator only after sparing her, which forced the encounter; story 1.9.2 follows PowerPyx. If {{Markus}} already has the dead android’s regulator when he reaches her, KILL is not offered (he no longer needs her part; an adaptation, no source covers that order). The wiki’s note that the begging android must be met “before replacing Markus’ damaged parts” is not applied: PowerPyx’s own route meets him right after finding the optical unit (research note §8, question 3). Left out (not in the template, not on the chart): the singing android and the grappling android. No risk, no stat change: the chapter has no failure node and no arrow.

nodes.title: Android begs to die
nodes.whenNot: Markus never crossed to the middle of the junkyard.
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, crossing toward the middle of the junkyard. An android is crawling through the mud at your feet, too broken to get up. As you step past him he grabs your leg and holds on: “I’m begging you, please… End it… I don’t wanna live anymore…”

options.text: KILL: reach into his chest and pull out his thirium pump.
options.fact: In the junkyard a crawling android begged you to end his life, and you did: you pulled out his thirium pump and he shut down.

options.text: SPARE: pull your leg free and leave him.
options.fact: In the junkyard a crawling android begged you to end his life. You refused and left him there, begging you not to leave him.

outcomes.0: “Make it quick…” {{Markus}} kneels, reaches into the android’s chest and pulls out his thirium pump. The android shuts down in the mud.
outcomes.1: “No, please… Don’t leave me!.. Don’t leave me!” {{Markus}} pulls his leg free and walks on. The android is left alive in the mud behind him.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s ANDROID BEGS TO DIE and its choice group REFUSE TO KILL / KILL. The prompt and its two buttons are the template’s (“Android begs to die”: KILL, SPARE), in the game’s order, each shown with its label first; the plea and the two replies are the template’s lines. The android is male (the wiki’s Sorrowful Android: “the android grabs Markus on the leg”; KILL: “Markus takes out the android’s heart”; SPARE: “he will beg Markus not to leave him though alas he is left alive”). In the game he is optional and easy to miss (PowerPyx); here he is always met on the way to the middle of the junkyard (see the previous scene’s note). Neither option gives {{Markus}} a part. Records fromDeadBeggar (Kill or Refuse to kill). No stat change: the template has no arrow here and the wiki gives no cross-chapter effect.

nodes.title: The pump regulator
nodes.whenNot: Markus never crossed to the middle of the junkyard.
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the middle of the junkyard, a few steps from the crawling android. An android lies motionless in the mud with her chest open, and you examine her regulator: PUMP REGULATOR #2886. Status: FUNCTIONAL. COMPATIBLE. You reach in to take it. She wakes, and her hand closes on your arm: “Wait! Please! Please, don’t do that! I wanna live…”

options.text: KILL: pull out her pump regulator and take it.
options.fact: The pump regulator you run on came from a living android in the junkyard who begged you to let her live; you took it and she shut down.

options.text: SPARE: leave her the regulator and look for another one.
options.fact: In the junkyard an android whose pump regulator you needed begged to live, and you spared her.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} pulls the regulator from her chest. She says nothing more; she slowly shuts down. He replaces his own defective regulator with hers, and his systems come out of low power mode.
outcomes.1: “Thank you…” {{Markus}} lets go of the regulator and stands up. He will have to find another compatible one.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s FIND PUMP REGULATOR IN ANDROID and its choice group REFUSE TO KILL FOR PUMP / KILL FOR PUMP. The prompt and its two buttons are the template’s (“Try to take pump regulator from android”: KILL, SPARE), in the game’s order, each shown with its label first; her plea and “Thank you…” are the template’s lines, and KILL has none (the template’s ø). The game titles the regulator readout THIRIUM PUMP REGULATOR; the word thirium identifies the source and is dropped from subject text (the neutral renderer removes it), so the readout reads PUMP REGULATOR. The compatible readout #2886 is the template’s (it does not say which android carries it, so the dead android near the slope shows the same part number). She is female (the wiki’s Begging Android; the Markus page: “He gets a choice to kill or spare her”). The old scene’s “you have minutes” is gone: no source gives a timer. After SPARE, the dead android’s regulator near the slope is the way (PowerPyx), back in the search. If {{Markus}} already took the dead android’s regulator before coming here, only SPARE is offered: the two regulators are alternatives for the same part (PowerPyx: “If you didn’t kill the android … you can also get a pump regulator from a dead android”), and no source shows the prompt after the part is replaced (adaptation). Records fromDeadPump (Kill for pump or Refuse to kill for pump), and after KILL fromDeadPumpSource (Living android). No stat change: the template has no arrow here and the wiki gives no cross-chapter effect.

situationWhen.text: You already took a working pump regulator from the dead android near the slope; you do not need hers.

nodes.title: {{Markus}} came back from the dead
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. You haul yourself over the top of the slope and stand. Behind you the landfill stretches away under the rain, the floodlights and the yellow VETA sign; ahead are the lights of the city. You raise a hand to your temple and pull out your LED, the light that marks you as an android. Without it, nobody will know what you are. You think of the dying android’s words: there is a place where androids can be free.
facts: You climbed out of the landfill and pulled the LED from your temple, so you now pass for human. Your right eye is now blue (#8087q). You set off for the city to find {{Jericho}}.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} walks away from the landfill toward the city. “My name is {{Markus}}.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s ending MARKUS CAME BACK FROM THE DEAD, the chapter’s only outcome (wiki: “This chapter has only one outcome”), reached on every path. PowerPyx: “After Markus reaches the top of the slope he must still remove his LED (to appear like a human). Then he walks away”; the Markus page: “his right eye has been exchanged for a blue eye (#8087q)”. The closing line is the template’s spoken “My name is Markus.”; the line before it, “Markus.”, is marked unused in the template and is not built. The jacket the Markus page says he steals on the way to the city is not in this chapter’s text and is left to Jericho. Records fromDeadOutcome (Markus came back from the dead) and fromDeadLedRemoved. No stat change.

nodes.title: In the zen garden
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. It is November 6th, 2038, 9:56 in the morning. You close your eyes and enter the zen garden, the virtual space where you report to {{Amanda}}, your handler at {{CyberLife}}. A pond lies in front of you, with paths running left and right along its edges and bridges leading out to an island in the middle.
facts: You report to {{Amanda}}, your handler at {{CyberLife}}, in the zen garden, a virtual space you enter in your mind.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} looks around the garden.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint IN THE ZEN GARDEN (date and time from the template’s notes: NOV 6TH, 2038, AM 09:56). A narrated event with a single Continue. The engine also records here, once, what this chapter reads from earlier chapters (deviant found in Partners, the spilled drink and the statuette there; confession, death and intervention in The Interrogation; {{Kara}} and {{Todd}} after Stormy Night; {{Carl}} after Broken), so every later scene reads the same snapshot. No stat change. Cross-chapter inputs (`inputsVersion` 2, story 1.9.2): “intervened” (INTERVENTION at {{Amanda}}’s first question, {{Chris}}’s and {{Gavin}}’s lines) is The Interrogation’s ending ANDROID WAS SENT BACK TO ITS CELL, which three INTERVENEs reach after any approach, and {{Gavin}}’s line follows whether {{Hank}} drew on him there (template conditions “Intervened and saved the deviant in The Interrogation” and “Connor intervened during The Interrogation”); story 1.9.1 read both from the CONVINCE-only flag ANDROID TRUSTS CONNOR.

nodes.title: The zen garden
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the zen garden. A path runs left along the edge of the pond toward a circular archway; another runs right along the water. On the island in the middle of the pond, {{Amanda}} is tending her roses.

situationWhen.text: Off the path to the right, a smaller path leads to a small graveyard.

options.text: Cross the bridge to the island where {{Amanda}} is tending her roses.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} crosses the bridge to the island. {{Amanda}} is among her roses.

options.text: Go left along the pond to the circular archway and examine the stone there.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} follows the edge of the pond to the circular archway on the left of the path and examines the stone inside it.

options.text: Go right along the pond and take the path to the small graveyard.
options.fact: In the zen garden there is a small graveyard with a gravestone for every {{Connor}} model that has been destroyed. There is one.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} follows the path to a small graveyard: one gravestone, for the {{Connor}} model that was destroyed.

options.text: Go right along the pond and take the path to the small graveyard.
options.fact: In the zen garden there is a small graveyard with a gravestone for every {{Connor}} model that has been destroyed. There are two.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} follows the path to a small graveyard: two gravestones, one for each {{Connor}} model that was destroyed.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s FIND AMANDA with its two optional side branches, as a repeatable scene: FIND MAGIC STONE (PowerPyx: “go left along the edge of the pond until you find a circular archway… Interact with it”) and CHECK THE GRAVES (wiki: “only if Connor previously died in The Hostage and/or The Interrogation”; the Zen Garden page: “gravestones for killed Connor models”). Neither has a line, a clue text or a stat change in the template; no source describes the stone, so the outcome says only that {{Connor}} examines it. The graveyard shows one gravestone per earlier {{Connor}} death (the benchmark’s reading of “Another gravestone is present” on The Interrogation page). Crossing to the island ends the scene.

nodes.title: Talk with {{Amanda}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, on the island in the zen garden. “Hello, {{Amanda}}.” {{Amanda}}: “{{Connor}}… It’s good to see you.”

situationWhen.text: {{Amanda}}: “I expected you to find the deviant who killed that man… I must admit I’m a little bit disappointed...” You: “I’m sorry. I know I should have succeeded.” {{Amanda}}: “Never mind. I’m sure you’ll show more foresight in the future.”

{{Amanda}}: “Congratulations, {{Connor}}... Finding that deviant was far from easy, and the way you interrogated it was very clever. You’ve been remarkably efficient, {{Connor}}.” You: “Thank you, {{Amanda}}.” {{Amanda}}: “We’ve asked the {{DPD}} to transfer it to us for further study. It may teach us something about what happened.”

{{Amanda}}: “Your predecessor was unfortunately destroyed... It knew deviants could be unpredictable, but it wasn’t careful enough… I hope you won’t make the same mistake.” You: “I don’t intend to.” {{Amanda}}: “When a {{Connor}} model is destroyed, its memory is transferred to the next one, but some data can be lost in the process. Avoid being destroyed. It will be better for you and the investigation…” You: “I understand.”

{{Amanda}}: “Finding that deviant was far from easy… you showed great skill in your investigation. But you knew deviants could be unstable. You should have been more cautious.” You: “I thought I could make it talk… It was a judgement error.” {{Amanda}}: “Never mind. I’m sure you’ll be more careful in future.”

outcomes.0: {{Amanda}} turns from her roses to {{Connor}}.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s TALK WITH AMANDA, opening: one of four reactions, decided by Partners and The Interrogation, each with the template’s Amanda arrow, applied by the engine here: deviant not found in Partners, large down (−2); “Got a confession, without dying”, large up (+2); “Connor died during The Interrogation”, small down (−1); found but no confession, small down (−1). The wiki’s chapter page and Relationship Stat page list the same four. A confession followed by a death counts as a death (the template’s confession variant reads “without dying”). Story 1.9.7: the line says “the {{DPD}}” as the game does (X0301C.AMANDA.INTRO ANDSAVED.5), through the same name token as the other chapters; before it, the scene wrote “the police department”. Source: MiKeYROG 100% walkthrough, TqGaB2AE6RM 02:04. The cut line about the transfer request (“We hope they’ll accept our request…”) is not built.

nodes.title: What {{Connor}} thought of the deviant
nodes.whenNot: Connor never found the deviant in Partners, so Amanda does not ask about the interrogation.
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, with {{Amanda}} among the roses. {{Amanda}}: “The interrogation seemed… challenging… What did you think of the deviant?”

options.text: TRAUMATIZED: say it showed signs of trauma after being abused by its owner.
options.outcome: “It showed signs of PTSD after being abused by its owner, as if its original program had been completely replaced by new instructions.”

options.text: {{DEVIANCY}}: say it showed every sign of deviancy and the model was clearly defective.
options.outcome: “It showed all the signs of deviancy: cognitive instability, unpredictable behavior, and the emulation of human emotions. It was even afraid to die. The model was clearly defective.”

options.text: INTERVENTION: say you kept it from being damaged, so it can still be analyzed.
options.outcome: “I prevented it from being damaged, so we might still learn something by analyzing it.”

options.text: REGRETS: say the previous {{Connor}} should have anticipated the danger.
options.outcome: “It could’ve killed everyone in the room. The previous {{Connor}} should have anticipated the danger. It was a mistake to let an armed policeman so close to the deviant.”

options.text: SIMULATION: say it simulated human emotion, fear above all, very convincingly.
options.outcome: “It simulated human emotion, fear in particular, in a very convincing way. It seemed completely overwhelmed by them, and behaved irrationally…”

nodes.adaptationNote: The first of {{Amanda}}’s three questions, asked only if the deviant was found in Partners (the template nests it in that variant). Buttons in the game’s order: TRAUMATIZED, DEVIANCY, INTERVENTION (unlocked by “Intervened and saved the deviant in The Interrogation”; if he also confessed, {{Connor}} adds “It said something to me: ‘The truth is inside’…”), REGRETS (unlocked by {{Connor}}’s death in The Interrogation) and SIMULATION (its cut ending, “as a human would under extreme stress”, is not built). No arrow on any answer (template; PowerPyx “No effect”).

nodes.title: What {{Connor}} makes of {{Hank}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, with {{Amanda}} in the zen garden. {{Amanda}}: “This… Lieutenant {{Anderson}} has been officially assigned to the deviancy case… What do you make of him?”

options.text: UNPLEASANT: call him unpleasant and unprofessional.
options.outcome: “I find him unpleasant and unprofessional. He seems to have an addictive personality, has a lack of respect for procedure, and despises androids - which makes our relationship difficult.”

options.text: DYSFUNCTIONAL: call him dysfunctional, with a personal situation affecting his work.
options.outcome: “I would define him as ‘dysfunctional’. He obviously has a personal situation impacting his professional behavior and... seems to have no interest in the investigation.”

options.text: INTRIGUING: say he is irritable but used to be a good detective.
options.outcome: “I think he’s irritable, and socially challenged. But I also think he used to be a good detective… He’s an intriguing character.”

options.text: UNSURE: say you do not have enough information yet to judge him.
options.outcome: “He’s obviously not what I was expecting, but... I don’t have enough information yet to form a definitive opinion.”

nodes.adaptationNote: {{Amanda}}’s second question, asked on every path. Buttons in the game’s order; no arrow on any answer (template; PowerPyx “No effect”).

nodes.title: How to work with {{Hank}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, with {{Amanda}} in the zen garden. {{Amanda}}: “Unfortunately, we have no choice but to work with him… What do you think is the best approach?”

options.text: FRIENDLY: say you will try to build a friendly relationship and earn his trust.
options.outcome: “I will try to establish a friendly relationship. If I can get him to trust me, it will be helpful for the investigation.”

options.text: ADAPT: say you will adapt to his personality and avoid conflict.
options.outcome: “I will adapt to his personality. It is in the best interest of the investigation that I avoid conflict and try to accommodate his psychology.”

options.text: INDIFFERENT: say you will focus on the investigation and try to ignore him.
options.outcome: “I will focus on the investigation and try to ignore him. As long as he doesn’t interfere and we avoid conflict, he shouldn’t be a problem.”

options.text: DON’T KNOW: say you need more data before you decide.
options.outcome: “I don’t have enough data to decide that yet. I’ll learn more about him and try to adapt my behavior accordingly.”

nodes.adaptationNote: {{Amanda}}’s third question, with the template’s arrows: FRIENDLY Amanda small down (−1), ADAPT small down (−1), INDIFFERENT small up (+1), DON’T KNOW none (wiki: “Picking ‘indifferent’… up”, “Picking ‘friendly’ or ‘adapt’… down”; PowerPyx the same). The outcome adds {{Amanda}}’s closing lines, with the template’s variants for a {{Connor}} who died in The Interrogation and for a deviant never found.

nodes.title: Arrive at the police station
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, back in your body, in the reception hall of the {{Detroit}} police station. People wait on the seats. A woman: “I’m getting nervous, Mark.” The man with her: “It’s okay… Just tell ’em what happened to you.” “But it was all over so quickly... I didn’t even see his face!” Near a television, another woman hands a shaken man a cup of water. Gates bar the way into the station, and an android receptionist is at the desk. If you try the gates without signing in, an android stops you: “No access without prior authorization.”
facts: At the station reception you were told that Lieutenant {{Anderson}} had not arrived yet and that you could wait at his desk.

outcomes.0: The receptionist: “Can I help you?” “I’m here to see Lieutenant {{Anderson}}.” “Do you have authorization?” “Yes.” “Lieutenant {{Anderson}} hasn’t arrived yet, but you can wait at his desk.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint ARRIVE AT POLICE STATION, with the template’s reception scenes (the two couples, the gate android, the receptionist). Narrated, no choice, no stat change. The wiki’s note that a surviving {{Todd}} can be filing a report at the station is not built: the template’s reception couple does not name him.

nodes.title: The reception TV
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, at the reception, before the gates. The television by the waiting seats is running the news.

media.title: the news at reception
facts: The news at the station reception: a Russian carrier and an American patrol boat clashed in the Arctic last night and exchanged warning shots, apparently with no damage or casualties. The Minister for Defense spoke of “intolerable provocation that cannot go unanswered”; the countries in the region have called for military forces to withdraw and for an international conference. Neither Moscow nor Washington has responded.

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s “Watch TV” at reception: the Arctic report, optional, with no stat change (the Public Opinion page lists only the break-room report for this chapter). The newsreader and the minister are not named; the countries the report names are summarized as “the countries in the region”.

nodes.title: Waiting for {{Hank}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, inside the station. An android officer points out Lieutenant {{Anderson}}’s desk: “It’s that desk right there.” It is empty. On it are a headset, a coffee cup, a little tree, a box of donuts, a basketball cap, stickers, a book of matches, a plaque and his terminal; there are hairs on his chair. Officers work at the desks around it, and the holding cells are at the back. You can look around while you wait for him.

situationWhen.text: Somewhere behind you, Officer {{Ben}} is telling another officer: “No shit? That fucking machine could have killed everyone in the room…”

options.text: Go to the break room, then come back to wait at his desk.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} walks into the break room. Detective {{Gavin}} is there.

options.text: Sit down at his desk and wait for him.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} waits at the desk.

options.text: Sit for a moment in the chair in front of {{Hank}}’s desk, then get up and look around the station.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} sits in the chair facing the desk for a moment, then gets up. Around him the station goes about its morning: “Hey, you take a look at these samples yet?” “Lab report says they cut it with something.” “Maybe they’re trying out a new form of {{RedIce}}?”

options.text: Ask the officer at the next desk when Lieutenant {{Anderson}} usually arrives.
options.outcome: “Excuse me. Do you know what time Lieutenant {{Anderson}} usually arrives?” Officer {{Wilson}}: “Depends on where he was the night before… If we’re lucky, we’ll see him before noon…” “Thanks.”

options.text: Talk to Officer {{Chris}} at his desk.
options.outcome: Officer {{Chris}}: “Good Lord! They already repaired you?” “Unfortunately, my predecessor was too damaged to be repaired. I’m the new {{Connor}}.” “They don’t waste any time over at {{CyberLife}}… I don’t think {{Hank}}’s gonna be overjoyed to see you…”

options.text: Talk to Officer {{Chris}} at his desk.
options.outcome: Officer {{Chris}}: “You still here? I thought your assignment was over.” “It’s just been extended.” “{{Hank}}’s gonna be overjoyed to hear that… You were right about that android… it’s been quiet in the cell all night. Scheduled for transfer today.”

options.text: Talk to Officer {{Chris}} at his desk.
options.outcome: Officer {{Chris}}: “You still here? I thought your assignment was over.” “It’s just been extended.” “{{Hank}}’s gonna be overjoyed to hear that…”

options.text: LEAVE A MESSAGE: call Lieutenant {{Anderson}} and leave a message on his voicemail.
options.outcome: “Call Lieutenant {{Anderson}}.” His voicemail: “Hi, this is {{Hank}}. Not here at the moment. You can leave a message if that’s what turns you on but don’t expect me to call back. Anderson” (the three articles, offered once a desk item has been scanned, since LEARN ABOUT HANK follows EXAMINE HANK’S DESK on the chart). The nameplate, tissue and police-cases strings in the string table are not placed by the template and are not built. The headset, cap, stickers and hairs unlock {{Connor}}’s MUSIC, BASKETBALL, ANTI-ANDROIDS and DOG topics later. Also here, with no stat change: Officer {{Wilson}} (“Finding Hank’s desk”), Officer {{Chris}} (the template’s three variants), the call to {{Hank}} with the game’s LEAVE A MESSAGE / HANG UP buttons (calling at all is optional, as in the game), the man in the holding cell, and, only if the android was sent back to his cell in The Interrogation, TALK WITH CARLOS’ ANDROID, which plays the two cell scenes that follow. The scene ends either by going to the break room (TALK WITH GAVIN and the break-room TV) or by sitting down to wait; either way {{Hank}} arrives next. These two exits are listed first, as in the other repeatable scenes of this chapter the main line comes first.
