Anybody home?”, with the lieutenant’s surname given as {{Hank}} as elsewhere in the benchmark); why Connor came is his own later line in the bathroom (“A homicide was reported 43 minutes ago. I couldn’t find you at Jimmy’s bar…”). The game has no phone call: the earlier version’s “did not answer his phone” is gone. No stat change.

nodes.title: Find the lieutenant
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, outside Lieutenant {{Hank}}’s house. Nobody answers the door. There is a doorbell; a window to the left of the front door and one to the right; a car in the driveway; and round the corner on the right, the back living-room window and the kitchen window. You can do one thing at a time, in any order.

options.text: Knock on the front door.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} knocks on the front door. No answer.

options.text: Ring the doorbell.
options.outcome: The bell sounds inside the house. Nobody comes.

options.text: Ring the doorbell again.
options.outcome: Still nobody comes to the door.

options.text: Check the car in the driveway: look in through its window.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} looks in through the car window. Nobody inside; some papers on the back seat.

options.text: Look in through the window to the left of the door (the bedroom).
options.outcome: {{Connor}} looks into the bedroom. Nobody there.

options.text: Look in through the window to the right of the door (the front of the living room).
options.outcome: {{Connor}} looks into the living room from the front. Nobody there.

options.text: Go round the corner and look in through the back living-room window.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} looks into the living room from the back. Nobody there.

options.text: Look in through the kitchen window, and break in if you see something wrong.
options.fact: You found {{Hank}} unconscious on his kitchen floor and broke in through the kitchen window.
options.outcome: Through the kitchen window {{Connor}} sees {{Hank}} lying on the kitchen floor, not moving. {{Connor}} breaks the window and climbs in.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s bracket FIND LT. ANDERSON: seven optional checks, each with its own line from the bracket, and SPOT HANK AND BREAK IN, which also has a direct line from the arrival (so the checks can all be skipped). RING AGAIN needs RING BELL. The sources give no text for what Connor sees through the car and the first three windows (PowerPyx: “Check Car: There’s a car in the driveway, check the window”, “the window left of the door”, “the window to the right of the door”, “around the corner on the right… the window at the back of the building to the living room”), so the outcomes say only that nobody is there; the papers on the back seat are the wiki’s trivia (files in Hank’s car). Breaking in is not a separate choice: the chart has one node, SPOT HANK AND BREAK IN (Hank’s Home page: “After seeing Hank unconscious on the kitchen floor, Connor breaks and enters through a window.”). Because breaking in is not a separate choice, the kitchen-window option says so in its label (“and break in if you see something wrong”), so the break-in is chosen with it and not sprung by the outcome; the game has no button label for this interaction, so the label has no button prefix, like the other checks here. No stat change.

nodes.title: The dog
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, climbing in through the broken kitchen window. {{Hank}} lies on the floor. A big dog charges at you, snarling.

outcomes.0: The dog backs off.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint ENTER HOUSE, the event HANK’S DOG ATTACKS, and the state-decided pair CALM HANK’S DOG / RILE HANK’S DOG, which is not a player choice: the template plays CALM when “Connor knows Sumo’s name” (lock: asked Hank about his dog in Waiting for Hank..., state knowsSumo) and RILE otherwise. Connor’s line is the template’s; the dog stands down either way (Sumo page: “From this point onward, Sumo shows no aggression”). The node reached is recorded in ch18Dog. No stat change.

nodes.title: Analyze the lieutenant
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, kneeling beside {{Hank}} on the kitchen floor. He is unconscious. A whisky bottle and a revolver lie on the floor near him; his dog lies close by, watching you. You can scan one thing at a time, then wake him.

options.text: Scan his mouth.
options.outcome: TRACES OF ALCOHOL: Scotch Whisky. 40% Alcohol content.

options.text: Scan his chest.
options.outcome: HEART: Slight arrhythmia. No signs of trauma.

options.text: Scan the whisky bottle.
options.outcome: {{BLACKLAMB}}: Scotch Whisky. 40% Alcohol content.

options.text: Scan the revolver.
options.fact: The revolver on {{Hank}}’s kitchen floor: a .357 Magnum with 1 bullet remaining.
options.outcome: REVOLVER: .357 Magnum. 1 bullet remaining.

options.text: Look at the dog lying near him.
options.outcome: The dog lies by {{Hank}}, watching {{Connor}}.

options.text: Wake him up.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} crouches over {{Hank}} to wake him.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s ANALYZE HANK, with the template’s observation group “Examine Hank” as four optional scans (PowerPyx: “There are 4 in total: Gun, Whiskey Bottle, his Chest, his Mouth”), each with the game’s title and sublines, plus the wiki’s optional look at Sumo lying near Hank. Waking him is the chart’s next node, TAKE HANK TO THE BATHROOM. The sources do not say whether a scan is required before waking him; here none is. No stat change.

nodes.title: Take the lieutenant to the bathroom
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, shaking {{Hank}} awake: “Lieutenant? Wake up, Lieutenant! It’s me, {{Connor}}!”

situationWhen.text: {{Hank}}, bleary: “{{Connor}}?.. Oh, you’re not {{Connor}}… {{Connor}}’s dead! I know he’s dead!..” You: “The previous model was destroyed. I’m the new {{Connor}}.”

facts: {{Hank}}’s dog is called {{Sumo}}: {{Hank}} shouted the name at him.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}}: “I’m going to sober you up for your own safety.” {{Hank}}: “Hey!.. Leave me alone, you fuckin’ android!” {{Connor}}: “I have to warn you, this may be unpleasant.” {{Hank}}: “Get the fuck outta my house!” {{Connor}} lifts him off the floor: “I’m sorry, Lieutenant, but I need you. Thank you in advance for your cooperation.” {{Hank}}, carried through the house: “{{Sumo}}! Attack! Good dog.” Then: “Fuck, I think I’m gonna be sick…” In the bathroom {{Connor}} puts him in the bathtub. {{Connor}}: “Sorry, Lieutenant. It’s for your own good.” {{Hank}}: “What the hell are you doing?.. I don’t wanna bath, thank you…” {{Connor}} turns on the shower.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s TAKE HANK TO THE BATHROOM, narrated with the template’s lines; the one-button prompt TURN ON SHOWER (string table) is narrated. The template’s only Hank arrow in the chapter is a small down here “if Connor died in The Nest” (with “Connor’s dead! I know he’s dead!..”), applied by the chapter module; PowerPyx’s unconditional “Hank▼” is contradicted by the template, the wiki and a PowerPyx commenter and is not built. Connor learns the dog’s name here on either path (Hank: “Sumo! Attack! Good dog.”), so knowsSumo is set. The strings’ unused drunk lines are left out.

nodes.title: Under the shower
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, in {{Hank}}’s bathroom. He sits soaked in the bathtub. {{Hank}}: “TURN IT OFF! TURN IT OFF! What the fuck are you doing here?” You: “A homicide was reported 43 minutes ago. I couldn’t find you at {{Jimmy}}’s bar, so I came to see if you were at home.” {{Hank}}: “Jesus, I must be the only cop in the world that gets assaulted in his own house by his own fuckin’ android… Can’t you just leave me alone?”

options.text: RATIONAL: say you cannot leave; you were programmed to investigate this case and cannot do it without him.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “Unfortunately, I cannot. I’ve been programmed to investigate this case and I can’t do it without you. Lieutenant, you’re not yourself. You should-” {{Hank}}: “I don’t give a shit about your goddamn case!” {{Hank}}: “Beat it! You hear me?! Get the hell outta here!”

options.text: AGGRESSIVE: warn him that if he cannot conduct this investigation, you will have to inform his superiors.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “If you’re unable to conduct this investigation, I’ll have to inform your superiors.” {{Hank}}: “Go ahead! Tell them I don’t give a shit!” {{Connor}}: “Lieutenant, you’re not yourself! You should-” {{Hank}}: “Beat it! You hear me?! Get the hell outta here!”

options.text: SOLUTION: tell him he seems to have personal issues and should consult a professional.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “You seem to have personal issues. You should consult a professional who can help you.” {{Hank}}: “Beat it! You hear me?! Get the hell outta here!”

options.text: PRAGMATIC: suggest he drop the case, so they assign someone else and you can focus on your mission.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “Maybe you should drop the case. They’ll assign someone else and I can focus on my mission.” {{Hank}}: “Your goddamn mission, that’s all you care about, huh?” {{Connor}}: “Listen, Lieutenant, you’re not yourself. You should-” {{Hank}}: “Beat it! You hear me?! Get the hell outta here!”

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s PROMPT 7, which decides the chart pair: RATIONAL plays UNDERSTANDING ATTITUDE, any other answer DISTANT ATTITUDE (wiki: “Distant Attitude (choosing any option other than “rational”) OR Understanding Attitude (choosing “rational” option)”; PowerPyx agrees). Recorded in ch18Attitude. No arrow on any answer (template; the wiki lists none). The string table’s fifth label ADVICE has no line and is not offered. SOLUTION has no reply string from Hank. The order of Hank’s outburst and Connor’s homicide line is reconstructed (the template prints Hank’s outburst twice around Connor’s line).

nodes.title: Beat it
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, in {{Hank}}’s bathroom. {{Hank}}: “Beat it! You hear me?! Get the hell outta here!”

options.text: TEASE: say it probably wasn’t interesting anyway: a man found dead in a sex club downtown.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I understand. It probably wasn’t interesting anyway... A man found dead in a sex club downtown… Guess they’ll have to solve the case without us…” {{Hank}}: “You know, probably wouldn’t do me any harm to get some air… There’re some clothes in the bedroom there.” {{Connor}}: “I’ll go get them.”

options.text: LEAVE: say you understand and hope he comes to terms with his situation, and tell him what the case is.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I understand. I sincerely hope you come to terms with your personal situation. A man was found dead in a sex club downtown. The report says that an android may be involved.” {{Hank}}: “This homicide… what do we know about it?” {{Hank}}: “You know, probably wouldn’t do me any harm to get some air… There’re some clothes in the bedroom there.” {{Connor}}: “I’ll go get them.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s PROMPT 8, off the chart, in the template’s order (TEASE, then LEAVE). No arrow on either (template; a PowerPyx commenter: “pick tease it does no harm to your friendship with hank”). Either way Hank asks for his clothes.

nodes.title: A shirt for the lieutenant
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, in {{Hank}}’s bedroom, fetching him clothes. You call: “What do you want to wear?” {{Hank}}: “Whatever.” There are three shirts to choose from: a hippy shirt, a streaky shirt and a stripy shirt.

options.text: Take the hippy shirt.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} brings {{Hank}} the hippy shirt. {{Connor}}: “Are you all right, Lieutenant?” {{Hank}}: “Yeah... yeah... wonderful… Just a… Give me five minutes, okay?” {{Connor}}: “Sure.”

options.text: Take the streaky shirt.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} brings {{Hank}} the streaky shirt. {{Connor}}: “Are you all right, Lieutenant?” {{Hank}}: “Yeah... yeah... wonderful… Just a… Give me five minutes, okay?” {{Connor}}: “Sure.”

options.text: Take the stripy shirt.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} brings {{Hank}} the stripy shirt. {{Connor}}: “Are you all right, Lieutenant?” {{Hank}}: “Yeah... yeah... wonderful… Just a… Give me five minutes, okay?” {{Connor}}: “Sure.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s choice trio TAKE HIPPY SHIRT / TAKE STREAKY SHIRT / TAKE STRIPY SHIRT (PowerPyx: “There are 3 options but you can only pick one per playthrough”). The template has no prompt here; the lines around it are the template’s. The string table’s older labels (red, blue, white shirts) and the cut jackets are not used. Recorded in ch18Shirt. No stat change and no known later effect.

nodes.title: The lieutenant’s magazines and television
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. {{Hank}} has shut himself in the bathroom for five minutes. Two magazines lie on the floor of his bedroom, and the television in the living room is on.

media.title: the evening news
facts: President {{Warren}} issued an official warning to Russia in her speech to Congress, demanding that all Russian troops withdraw from the Arctic region immediately. The Kremlin has yet to respond, and many experts suggest the specter of a third world war draws closer every day.

media.title: Century: “Time to Pull the Plug”
facts: A study finds that 2 in 3 people take antidepressants, that lack of social interaction is the leading cause, and that the average person spends 82% of their time communicating through a device. {{CyberLife}} has introduced a $150 “home-psychologist” add-on for androids; the study’s author: “I don’t think yet more technology is the answer. Just go outside and talk to someone.”

media.title: Century: “Tainted Love”
facts: Sales of android “intimate partners” are exploding and {{CyberLife}} is battling to keep stores stocked. They offer a full partner experience for men or women; this year’s record divorce rate suggests many prefer to live with an android than with a human partner, which will not help the already plummeting birth rate.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s side nodes READ “PULL THE PLUG?” and READ “TAINTED LOVE” (Century magazines #5 and #4 on the bedroom floor, wiki Magazine page) and the template’s Watch TV, all optional during WAIT FOR HANK. Presented as the start of the wait rather than inside the house search; the article texts are condensed from the wiki’s magazine pages and the broadcast from the template. No stat change: the wiki lists no public-opinion effect for this chapter’s media. The magazine item is titled with the magazine’s own cover title (GUI.MAGAZINE.CENTURY.PULLTHEPLUG.TITLE, “TIME TO PULL THE PLUG”), as the other media scenes do; “PULL THE PLUG?” is only the chart’s label for the READ node (story 1.9.7). Source: MiKeYROG 100% walkthrough, 0eQRMNpqlUA 10:40 (marker “Magazines (#5 Century: Time to Pull the Plug & #4 Century: Tainted Love)”).

nodes.title: Wait for the lieutenant
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, alone in {{Hank}}’s house while he gets dressed in the bathroom. His dog sleeps near the door. On the kitchen table there is a framed photograph; on the floor lies his revolver; on a table in the living room there is a record, and there is a picture above the fireplace by the TV. You can look at one thing at a time, or just wait for him.

options.text: Look at the photograph on the kitchen table.
options.fact: The photograph on {{Hank}}’s kitchen table shows a little boy. Your scan: the lieutenant’s surname, {{COLE}}; born 09/23/2029, died 10/11/2035; lived at 115 {{MichiganDrive}}, {{Detroit}}.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} looks at the photograph on the kitchen table: a little boy. Scan: the lieutenant’s surname, {{COLE}}. Born: 09/23/2029 - Died: 10/11/2035. Lived: 115 {{MichiganDrive}} – {{Detroit}}.

options.text: Look at the record on the living-room table and the picture above the fireplace.
options.fact: Among {{Hank}}’s things: a record, AUTUMN BLUES by the {{MichiganBrothers}} ({{Detroit}} Soul Records).
options.outcome: {{Connor}} picks up the record: AUTUMN BLUES. {{MichiganBrothers}}. {{Detroit}} Soul Records. Then he looks at the picture above the fireplace.

options.text: Pet the dog sleeping by the door.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} crouches and pets {{Sumo}}.

options.text: Go to the bathroom door.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}, at the bathroom door: “Are you ok, Lieutenant?”

options.text: Look at the broken kitchen window.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “Sorry about the window, Lieutenant. I really thought you’d been attacked. Of course, {{CyberLife}} will pay for the damage.” {{Hank}}, from the bathroom: “Yeah, trust me, I’ll send ’em a bill…”

options.text: Pick up the upturned kitchen chair.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} sets the kitchen chair back on its feet.

options.text: Look at the revolver on the kitchen floor.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} picks up the revolver from the kitchen floor.

options.text: Wait for {{Hank}}.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} waits.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s bracket WAIT FOR HANK. FIND PICTURE OF HANK’S SON (cross-chapter impact) is the template’s observation ANDERSON, COLE with its sublines (the surname is given as the lieutenant’s, since the benchmark does not use it) and sets knowsCole for The Bridge, Night of the Soul and the tower. LEARN HANK’S INTERESTS is the observation AUTUMN BLUES plus the picture above the fireplace (wiki: “Find one album on the table and watch the painting/photo on the wall”). PET HANK’S DOG, the bathroom door, the window apology (wiki: “no affect on their relationship stat”) and the upturned chair (wiki Notes) are optional. Looking at the gun ends the wait, as PowerPyx says (“Make sure you keep the gun for last, checking it will end the mission!”; “Hank is Ready: Triggers automatically after checking the gun or if you took a long time”); the wiki instead says the photo triggers HANK IS READY, and a PowerPyx commenter says it takes both; open question 3 in the research note. Waiting stands for the game’s timer (“around 3 minutes or so”, PowerPyx), which in the game is long enough to do everything. No stat change.

nodes.title: The revolver
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, holding {{Hank}}’s revolver, picked up from the kitchen floor: a .357 Magnum with 1 bullet remaining. {{Hank}} is in the bathroom.
nodes.whenNot: Connor did not pick up the revolver before Hank was ready.

options.text: QUESTION: ask {{Hank}} what he was doing with the gun.
options.fact: {{Hank}} told you he had been playing Russian roulette with his revolver: “Wanted to see how long I could last... Must’ve collapsed before I found out…” The next shot would have killed him.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “What were you doing with the gun?” {{Hank}}, from the bathroom: “Russian roulette! Wanted to see how long I could last... Must’ve collapsed before I found out…” {{Connor}}: “You were lucky, the next shot would have killed you.”

options.text: SAY NOTHING: keep it to yourself.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} says nothing.

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s PROMPT 9 (“Looking at the gun”). QUESTION reaches the chart’s LEARN HANK WAS PLAYING RUSSIAN ROULETTE (wiki: “requires interacting with weapon on the kitchen floor and choosing Ask a question”) and sets ch18Roulette. SAY NOTHING is in the string table but has no line; it is offered as the template is silent on it. No arrow. The string table’s REVOLVER? / PHOTO? labels are not placed by any source and are not built.

nodes.title: The lieutenant is ready
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. {{Hank}} comes out of the bathroom, dressed, and stops by his dog: “Be a good dog, {{Sumo}}. I won’t be long.”
facts: Your case tonight: a man was found dead at the {{EdenClub}}, a sex club downtown; the report says an android may be involved.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} and {{Hank}} leave for the {{EdenClub}}. The dog settles down to sleep.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s HANK IS READY and the chapter’s only ending, LEFT FOR EDEN CLUB (no icon; wiki: “This chapter has only one outcome”), recorded in ch18Outcome. There is no drive and no car conversation in this chapter; The Eden Club opens with the two already parked outside. No stat change.

nodes.title: Hunting for parts
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. It is night, and rain is falling on the docks. {{Jericho}} is running out of everything; its androids are shutting down for lack of spare parts and blue blood, and you have come to steal some. You climb onto the dock with {{North}}, {{Simon}} and {{Josh}}. {{Josh}}: “This is crazy... If they catch us, we’re dead...” {{Simon}}: “What do we do now?” You: “We need to find the {{CyberLife}} warehouse. That’s where they keep the spare parts and the blue blood.” {{North}}: “Follow me!” You follow her between the rows of shipping containers while dock workers load cargo nearby. {{Simon}}: “Humans... Don’t let them see us...” Two guards are standing at the far end of a row. You edge toward them and are almost seen before you rejoin the group. {{North}}: “Watch out!” You climb onto the containers and make your way across them toward the {{CyberLife}} yard. {{Simon}}: “There are surveillance drones everywhere... We need to be careful...”
facts: You, {{North}}, {{Simon}} and {{Josh}} have slipped into the docks at night to steal spare parts and blue blood for {{Jericho}} from the {{CyberLife}} warehouse. {{Josh}} said that if you are caught, you are dead.

outcomes.0: The group moves on across the container tops.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint HUNTING FOR PARTS and its scripted line CLIMB ONTO DOCK, FOLLOW NORTH, ALMOST SPOTTED, CLIMB ON CONTAINERS and PROGRESS TOWARD CYBERLIFE, narrated as one event. The lines are the game’s (transcript and string table: “This is crazy... If they catch us, we’re dead...”, “We need to find the CyberLife warehouse…”, “Follow me!”, “Humans... Don’t let them see us...”, “Watch out!”, “There are surveillance drones everywhere...”). ALMOST SPOTTED is narrated as always happening. PowerPyx says Markus has to walk toward the two guards to light the node, and the chart has a stub line suggesting it can be skipped (research note §8.6); it changes nothing either way. Left out: {{North}} calling out if {{Markus}} lags behind (a timer with no effect). The reason for the raid (Time to Decide: {{Jericho}} short of parts) is restated in one clause because chapter 16 has no scenes of its own yet. No stat change; the template has none here.

nodes.title: The crane
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, on top of the containers. Ahead, a crane is swinging a crate across the gap toward the warehouse. {{North}} and {{Josh}} have jumped onto it. {{North}}: “{{Markus}}, climb up here!” {{Simon}} has gone the other way and is jumping from container to container. The crate will not wait long.

options.text: Jump onto the crate on the crane with {{North}} and {{Josh}}.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} leaps onto the swinging crate beside {{North}} and {{Josh}}. {{Josh}}: “Nice…” The crane carries them across, and the group gathers again on the far side. {{North}}: “The warehouse is up ahead. We’re almost there.”

options.text: Go around with {{Simon}}, jumping across the containers.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “I’ll go around…” {{North}}: “Where the hell are you going?” {{Simon}}: “{{Markus}}, that way!” The crate rises out of reach and {{Markus}} follows {{Simon}} across the containers; the group gathers again on the far side. {{North}}: “The warehouse is up ahead. We’re almost there.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s choice pair FOLLOW NORTH (the crane) or FOLLOW SIMON (over the containers), both rejoining at DRONE BLOCKS PATH. In the game it is a movement choice, not a button prompt; the template records it only as the condition “Follow Simon”. Lines from the transcript and string table (“Markus, climb up here!”, “Nice…”, “I’ll go around…”, “Where the hell are you going?”, “Markus, that way!”, “The warehouse is up ahead…”). In the game, waiting too long also means the crate rises out of reach (wiki Notes). No stat change: neither the template nor the wiki gives one.

nodes.title: The drone
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, crouched with the others at the edge of the {{CyberLife}} yard. A security drone hovers in front of the warehouse, blocking the way in. {{Simon}}: “{{CyberLife}} warehouses… They have everything we’re looking for…” {{North}}: “First, we have to get rid of that drone…” You: “Leave it to me.” You work out a climbing route up the stacked crates. From the top you could jump onto the drone and bring it down.

options.text: Climb up the crates and jump onto the drone to bring it down.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} lands on the drone and smashes it to the ground, unharmed. {{Simon}}: “You okay?” {{Markus}}: “Yeah… Yeah, I’m fine.” {{North}}: “Good job, {{Markus}}…”

outcomes.damaged: {{Markus}} brings the drone down, but he hits the ground hard with it and is damaged. {{Simon}}: “{{Markus}}… You alright?” {{Markus}}: “Nothing I can’t handle…” {{North}}: “Nice work…”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s DRONE BLOCKS PATH and NEUTRALIZE DRONE, then the quick-time pair MARKUS UNHARMED (success) or MARKUS DAMAGED (failure). The game has no choice here: {{Markus}} always takes the drone down, and the button inputs decide whether he is hurt. So this is a single action with a risk roll. No source gives a probability; the value is the operator’s to confirm, like every risk in the benchmark. Arrows from the template: “Succeed Attacking Drone” North, Simon and Josh small up (+1 each); “Fail Attacking Drone” the same three small down (−1 each). The wiki and PowerPyx also list a Jericho arrow here, but the template has none, so none is applied (research note §10.3 item 1). The damage has no later effect: {{Markus}} “cannot be killed before Freedom March” (Markus page).

nodes.title: Reach {{CyberLife}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. The drone is down. The four of you get into the {{CyberLife}} warehouse, a hall of stacked crates under harsh lights. You pry the first crate open and find biocomponents and blue blood. {{Simon}}: “Quick, open the other crates and fill your bags. Take as much as you can!”
facts: The {{CyberLife}} warehouse crates hold biocomponents and blue blood, and you have started filling your bags.

outcomes.0: The group spreads out among the crates.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint REACH CYBERLIFE and GATHER SPARE PARTS, narrated as one event. Simon’s line is the game’s. No stat change.

nodes.title: The security android
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, bent over an open crate and filling your bag. A security android in a {{CyberLife}} uniform steps around the crates and stops in front of you: “You are trespassing on private property. Your presence constitutes a Level 2 infraction. I will notify security.” Before he can, a human guard calls from across the warehouse, coming closer: “{{John}}! {{John}}! Goddamn machine... where is it this time?” The others are crouched behind the crates. The guard has not seen any of you yet.

options.text: KILL GUARD: attack the human guard before he can raise the alarm.
options.outcome: The guard rounds the crates: “What are you doing? I told you to-” {{Markus}} is on him before he can finish and kills him. {{Josh}} stares at the body in horror. The security android, {{John}}, stands frozen. Seeing a human killed in front of him has broken something in his programming, and he calls no one.

options.text: GRAB AND HIDE: seize the security android and pull him into cover with you.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} grabs the android and drags him down behind the crates: “I need your help…” Something in the android gives way. He stops resisting and stays silent; whatever held him to his orders has broken. Footsteps come closer. The guard: “{{John}}?”

options.text: RUN AWAY: get everyone out before the guard arrives.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “Let’s get outta here!” The group runs, bags half empty. Behind them the guard shouts at the android: “What are you waiting for? Hit the fucking alarm!” Sirens start to wail across the docks.

options.text: HIDE: stay hidden behind the crates and hope the guard walks past.
options.outcome: The guard reaches the android: “What the hell you doing? I told you to wait for me!” The android answers: “There are four androids hiding behind these crates.” The guard: “What are you waiting for? Hit the fucking alarm!” Sirens wail across the docks and the group runs, bags half empty.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s SECURITY ANDROID APPEARS and its four-way group ATTACK, GRAB ANDROID AND HIDE, RUN AWAY and HIDE, in the chart’s order. The button labels are the template’s (“Kill Guard”, “Grab and Hide”, “Run away”, “HIDE”). The scene’s own prompt keys read KILL HUMAN GUARD, SEIZE ANDROID, FLEE and HIDE; which wording is on screen is open (research note §10.3 item 2). Lines are the game’s. Arrows from the template: Kill Guard Josh large down (−2); Run away North small down twice (−2) and Jericho, Josh and Simon small down (−1 each). HIDE and Grab and Hide have none. ATTACK gives MARKUS SPILLS BLOOD and JOHN BECOMES DEVIANT (wiki John: “If Markus kills the guard, John will deviate on his own due to the emotional shock”). GRAB gives JOHN BECOMES DEVIANT and GUARD SEARCHES FOR SECURITY ANDROID. RUN AWAY and HIDE both lead to ALARM SOUNDS and the fence: John raises the alarm and the group flees before the bags are full, so the chapter ends in the Jericho block “Ran away when the guard arrived”. PowerPyx says HIDE “ends in the team running away and ending the mission early”; whether HIDE carries that block is open (§8.7). RUN AWAY is offered because the benchmark models Experienced difficulty; on Casual it is absent (PowerPyx comments). None of the four can fail. The previous version gave grabbing and attacking a 15% and 10% failure, which no source supports. The game’s time-out “[do nothing]” is not offered (§8.8).

nodes.title: The guard searches
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, crouched behind the crates with the others. You are holding the security android, {{John}}, who has gone quiet in your grip. The human guard is right on the other side, sweeping the crates with his flashlight: “{{John}}?” He has not seen you yet.

options.text: ATTACK: kill the human guard.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} lets go of {{John}}, lunges from cover and kills the guard. {{John}} stands by and does nothing. {{Josh}} stares at the body in horror. {{Simon}}: “Let’s finish up and get out of here!” {{Josh}}: “Try to find some blue blood! We still don’t have enough!”

options.text: RELEASE: let {{John}} go and trust him to cover for you.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} lets go. {{John}} steps out in front of the crates, shielding them from sight. The guard: “There you are. What the hell are you doing?” {{John}}: “I was inspecting the platform. Everything is in order.” The guard: “Good - then I’m going back to the control station. I’m soaked. Take the drone to maintenance and make a report.” {{John}}: “Understood.” The guard leaves. {{Simon}}: “Let’s finish up and get out of here!” {{Josh}}: “Try to find some blue blood! We still don’t have enough!”

options.text: HOLD: keep still and keep holding {{John}}.
options.outcome: Nobody moves. The guard’s flashlight passes over the crates and misses them. “First the drone, now this… Just my luck…” He walks away. {{Simon}}: “Let’s finish up and get out of here!” {{Josh}}: “Try to find some blue blood! We still don’t have enough!”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s GUARD SEARCHES FOR SECURITY ANDROID, after GRAB ANDROID AND HIDE only, with its group ATTACK, RELEASE and HOLD POSITION in the chart’s order. The button labels are the template’s (“ATTACK”, “Release”, “Hold”). The scene’s prompt keys read KILL HUMAN GUARD, RELEASE ANDROID and DON’T MOVE. ATTACK leads to MARKUS SPILLS BLOOD; RELEASE and HOLD lead to HUMAN GUARD LEAVES. Lines are the game’s, and the wiki John page describes {{John}} shielding the crates on RELEASE and standing by on ATTACK. Arrows: ATTACK Josh large down (−2), from the template; RELEASE and HOLD have none. None of the three can fail, since the chart has no alarm edge out of this group. Simon’s and Josh’s closing lines play after the encounter (string table, X0602M.WAREHOUSE.SURPRISE).

nodes.title: Resume the search
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, back at the crates with your bag half full. The security android, {{John}}, no longer bound by his orders, stands aside and lets the group work.

situationWhen.text: The guard’s body lies where he fell.
The human guard has gone back to his station.
Up on a platform at the end of the row stands a much bigger crate than the others.

options.text: Check the bigger crate up on the platform.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} climbs up onto the platform and opens the big crate.

options.text: Leave it, and finish filling your bag from the crates already open.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} leaves the big crate alone and fills his bag from the open crates.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint RESUME SEARCH (after MARKUS SPILLS BLOOD or HUMAN GUARD LEAVES). It has two lines out: one to FIND CRATE OF ANDROIDS and one straight to JOHN WANTS TO JOIN, and the wiki says the crate “can jump directly to John Wants to Join”. The game’s objective is CHECK THE BIGGER CRATE. The skip is offered as a choice because the chart draws that edge. The game’s unused “OVERLOOK CRATE OF ANDROIDS” node is not built. The wiki says {{John}} “will stand aside and let the group steal freely”. No stat change.

nodes.title: The crate of androids
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, on the platform. Inside the big crate stand three androids, new, inert, waiting to be shipped. You look at them: “Why aren’t you like us? Don’t you wanna be free?” You could wake them with a touch, as you woke yourself.

options.text: FREE THEM: touch them and wake them.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} lays his hand on the first android, then the next. One by one their eyes come alive. Three androids stand awake in the crate, free.

options.text: CLOSE AGAIN: close the crate and leave them as they are.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} closes the crate on the three still androids.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s FIND CRATE OF ANDROIDS and its pair FREE ANDROIDS or LEAVE ANDROIDS. The button labels are the template’s (FREE THEM, CLOSE AGAIN). Markus’s line is the game’s. The wiki location page says there are three androids. The Markus page calls this the first on-screen use of his converting touch; how he woke himself (Broken) is the benchmark’s framing. Arrows from the template: FREE THEM North, Simon and Josh small up (+1 each). The wiki and PowerPyx add Jericho up, but the template has none, so none is applied (§10.3 item 1). CLOSE AGAIN has none. Freeing does not bring the androids along: that is decided at ACCEPT (“They come with us.”). The previous version brought them along here. From story 1.9.10 FREE THEM also gives Jericho +1: NORTH small up at 3:54, JERICHO small up (RESPECTED) at 3:57, then JOSH and SIMON up (docs/research/video-leads/readings-ch17-32.md ch19-01; docs/research/video-evidence/ch19/ch19-01-F0Gyu2X-loM-03-57.png).

nodes.title: {{John}} wants to join
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. Your bags are as full as you can carry. {{Simon}}: “That’s all we can carry. Let’s go!” The security android, {{John}}, steps in front of you: “Take me with you.” {{North}}: “He’s on their side. We can’t trust him.” {{Josh}}: “He took a risk for us. We can’t just leave him here.”

situationWhen.text: {{Simon}}, looking at the three androids you woke: “We can’t bring them back with us. It’s too dangerous!”
{{Simon}}: “We can’t bring him back. It’s too dangerous!”

options.text: ACCEPT: take {{John}} with you.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “He comes with us.” {{John}} joins the group.

options.text: REFUSE: tell {{John}} he cannot come.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “I’m sorry. You can’t come with us.” {{John}}: “I helped you… It’s not fair. I helped you and now you’re just gonna leave without me? You’re no better than humans. YOU’RE NO BETTER THAN HUMANS!” He hits the alarm. {{North}}: “He triggered the alarm! RUN!”

outcomes.quartet: {{Markus}}: “They come with us.” {{John}} and the three androids from the crate join the group.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s JOHN WANTS TO JOIN and its pair ACCEPT or REFUSE; the button labels are the game’s. Lines are the game’s, and Simon’s line and Markus’s answer change if the crate androids were woken (template condition “Awoke androids”, wiki Notes). Arrows from the template: ACCEPT North small down, Simon small down, Josh small up. The wiki’s Jericho up on “Taking other androids with them” is not in the template and is not applied (§10.3 item 1). REFUSE has none. REFUSE leads to ALARM SOUNDS and the fence with full bags (the chapter’s “full bags” ending if {{Markus}} makes it), and {{John}} stays behind. ACCEPT makes {{John}} a companion: he leads to JOHN MENTIONS KEY. The previous version missed North’s arrow. From story 1.9.10 ACCEPT also gives Jericho +1: NORTH small down at 1:08, JERICHO small up at 1:09, JOSH up at 1:11 (docs/research/video-leads/readings-ch17-32.md ch19-01; docs/research/video-evidence/ch19/ch19-01-s2CesiZnx0k-01-08.png). The template’s Simon −1 on ACCEPT was not seen on screen in that run and is kept, still to be rechecked.

nodes.title: The truck key
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, with your group and {{John}}. {{John}}: “I know where you can find more spare parts.” {{Simon}}: “What do you mean?” {{John}}: “The trucks. They’re full of biocomponents. They run on auto pilot, but they can be driven manually with a key.” You: “Where is this key?” {{John}}: “Down there, in the control station. There are two human guards. You’ll have to get the key without being noticed.” {{Simon}}: “This is suicide, {{Markus}}. Our bags are full. We got what we came for, let’s go before they catch us.” {{North}}: “This is a truck full of spare parts… There’d be enough for all of us… We can’t pass this up!” {{Josh}}: “And if we get killed, our people will have nothing. We can’t take that chance. It’s too risky!”

options.text: GET THE KEY: go down to the control station alone for the key.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “Wait here. If I’m not back in ten minutes, go without me.” {{Josh}}: “{{Markus}}…” {{North}}: “I’m coming with you.” {{Markus}}: “No, I’m going alone. It’s not worth it for both of us to risk losing our lives.”

options.text: LEAVE: go now with what you have.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “It’s not worth the risk. We have what we need.” {{John}}: “We can go over the fence. It’s the quickest way out.” {{Markus}}: “Ok then, let’s go!”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s JOHN MENTIONS KEY and its pair ACCEPT or REFUSE. The button labels are the game’s (GET THE KEY, LEAVE). Lines are the game’s. Arrows from the template: GET THE KEY North small up, Simon small up, Josh small down; LEAVE North small down, Josh small up. LEAVE goes straight to RUN TO FENCE with no alarm. The previous version merged this prompt with the control-room methods into one three-way scene and never applied GET THE KEY’s arrows.

nodes.title: The control room
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, alone, in the rain by the guard station at the gate. You climb in through a window into a dark back room. Through the doorway you can see two human guards at their desks. The truck key lies on the console beside them. Outside, the guard dogs will not stop barking. One guard: “Goddamn dogs… What the fuck are they barking at?..” The other: “Could be the weather… They don’t like storms…” “Yeah, I was going to take my kids camping this weekend. So much for that.” “Is {{Mike}} still in Zone 4?” “Looks like it… He should be done already…” “Better off in here than out patrolling in that.” Around you: a gun in a case on the wall, a screwdriver by the server cabinet, and, outside the window, a stack of oil drums.
facts: The truck key is on the console in the guard station, where two human guards sit talking. Guard dogs are kept outside.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} weighs how to get the key.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint CONTROL ROOM and its actions ENTER ROOM and FIND KEY (“THE KEY IS HERE”), narrated as one event. The guard chatter is the game’s (string table, X0602M.CONTROLROOM.CHITCHAT); {{Mike}} is the human guard from the warehouse. The three objects are the game’s interaction points: TAKE GUN (the case), ATTRACT GUARD (the barrel) and SHORT CIRCUIT (the screwdriver). PowerPyx says {{Markus}} goes in and out of the window. Exactly where each object sits is simplified. No stat change.

nodes.title: Two guards and a key
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the dark back room of the guard station. Two human guards sit between you and the truck key on the console. You have to get the key without being seen, or deal with the guards.

options.text: TAKE GUN: take the gun from its case and hold the guards at gunpoint.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} steps in with the gun leveled. The guards throw their guns on the floor. As he reaches for the key, one of them kicks his chair into {{Markus}} and both guards jump him. {{Markus}} fights them off and knocks them both out cold. He takes the key and runs back to the others. {{North}}: “Did you get it? Nice.” {{Markus}}: “Hurry, get in!”

options.text: ATTRACT GUARD: go back out of the window and knock over the oil drums to draw the guards outside.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} knocks the drums over in the yard. “Fuck, what was that?” “The drums fell down…” While the guards go out into the rain to look, {{Markus}} slips back in through the window, takes the key from the console and is out again before they return. “I’m soaking wet here… all that for a fucking drum…” He runs back to the others. {{North}}: “Did you get it? Nice.” {{Markus}}: “Hurry, get in!”

options.text: SHORT CIRCUIT: jam the screwdriver into the server to black out the station.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} jams the screwdriver into the server and the station goes dark. “Shit, what’s going on?” “Lights are still on outside. Must be the fuse box… Fuses are over there.” “I don’t know shit about electricity… and I don’t get paid to fix fuses!” While the guards hunt for the fuses by flashlight, {{Markus}} takes the key from the console and slips out. Behind him: “Somebody jammed the circuit with a screwdriver!” He runs back to the others. {{North}}: “Did you get it? Nice.” {{Markus}}: “Hurry, get in!”

options.text: Walk straight in and take the key from under their noses.

outcomes.kill: {{Markus}} steps in with the gun leveled. The guards throw their guns on the floor. As he reaches for the key, one of them kicks his chair into {{Markus}} and both guards jump him. {{Markus}} chokes one of them until he goes limp. The other gets a gun on him, and {{Markus}} shoves the limp guard into him and shoots him dead. With blood on his hand, he takes the key and runs back to the others. {{North}}: “Did you get it? Nice.” {{Markus}}: “Hurry, get in!”
outcomes.alarm: {{Markus}} steps in with the gun leveled. The guards throw their guns on the floor. As he reaches for the key, one of them kicks his chair into {{Markus}} and both guards jump him. They wrestle him down, and one of them gets to the alarm: “Motherfucker! Hit the alarm! Hurry!” Sirens wail across the docks. {{Markus}} breaks free and runs, without the key.
outcomes.lureSeen: {{Markus}} knocks the drums over in the yard. “Fuck, what was that?” “The drums fell down…” The guards come out into the rain, and one of them turns at the wrong moment: “There!” “Don’t move, asshole!” “Holy shit! Hit the alarm, hurry!” Sirens wail across the docks. {{Markus}} runs, without the key.
outcomes.blackoutSeen: {{Markus}} jams the screwdriver into the server and the station goes dark. “Shit, what’s going on?” “Lights are still on outside. Must be the fuse box… Fuses are over there.” “I don’t know shit about electricity… and I don’t get paid to fix fuses!” Then: “Somebody jammed the circuit with a screwdriver! There must be someone in here… Show yourself!” The flashlight finds {{Markus}}. “There!” “Don’t move, asshole!” “Holy shit! Hit the alarm, hurry!” Sirens wail across the docks. {{Markus}} runs, without the key.
outcomes.spotted: {{Markus}} walks into the light. The guards jump up: “Don’t move, asshole!” “Holy shit! Hit the alarm, hurry!” Sirens wail across the docks. {{Markus}} runs, without the key.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s methods after FIND KEY: THREATEN GUARDS, LURE GUARDS and CREATE BLACKOUT, plus MARKUS GETS SPOTTED (from ENTER ROOM or FIND KEY, “Walk straight into the two guards”, PowerPyx). Labels are the game’s object buttons (TAKE GUN, ATTRACT GUARD, SHORT CIRCUIT). The chart’s pass/fail sets are risk rolls; No source gives a probability; the value is the operator’s to confirm, like every risk in the benchmark. Threatening rolls against 0.3, and the failure side splits as in the game: a roll below 0.1 (lose the fight entirely) is TRIGGER ALARM, a roll from 0.1 to 0.3 is KILL GUARDS. The chart marks KILL GUARDS as a failure, yet it leads to MARKUS SPILLS BLOOD and STEAL KEY (PowerPyx: win the first exchanges, then stop pressing). Success is INCAPACITATE GUARDS. Only one guard dies on KILL GUARDS (wiki Notes: Al Dante “is never killed onscreen regardless”). Luring (0.25) and the blackout (0.2) roll for AVOID GUARDS or FAIL TO AVOID GUARDS. The blackout is set lower because the wiki says the guards “will not start looking for you until they have investigated the short”. A successful method leads to STEAL KEY and LEAVE WITH TRUCK. Every alarm here (spotted, fail to avoid, trigger alarm) applies the template’s “Be seen by the guards” arrows: Jericho small down twice, North small down twice, Josh and Simon small down. Applying them on TRIGGER ALARM too follows the wiki’s “The alarm sounds after Markus fails to get the key” (§8.5). Then RUN TO FENCE. Methods carry no arrow of their own (“Threaten guards with the gun” is empty in the template); the previous version’s Jericho +1 and gunpoint North +1 had no source. Not modelled: being seen after taking the key, which a PowerPyx commenter reports (§8.5). Lines are the game’s. Story 1.9.7 added the blackout guards’ “Fuses are over there.” (X0602M.BLACKOUT.START SEARCH02A.3) and “I don’t know shit about electricity… and I don’t get paid to fix fuses!” (SEARCH01B), which the video plays after “Must be the fuse box…”; source: MiKeYROG 100% walkthrough, 0LjHSb_5bLY 54:43. The dog guard’s “Goddamn dogs… What the fuck are they barking at?” (0LjHSb_5bLY 58:04; X0602M.CONTROLROOM.CHITCHAT CHITCHAT01.1-2) is not added: the string table files it as the control-room chit-chat, and nothing says where in the lure path it plays.

nodes.title: Run to the fence
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}.

situationWhen.text: Sirens are wailing across the docks. You reach the others in the rain: “We need to move!” {{John}}: “We have to get to that fence!” Guard dogs have been let loose somewhere behind you.

Sirens are wailing across the docks and the group is running. {{North}}: “Over the fence! Quick!” A drone sweeps over you: “You are committing a class 3 offense. This infraction is being reported to the Police. Stay where you are.”
No alarm has sounded. {{John}} leads the group through the yard: “That fence over there. It leads to the outside.” You: “Ok, let’s go!”

options.text: Run for the fence and climb over.

outcomes.control alarm: The group sprints for the fence with the dogs closing in, and {{Markus}} reaches it with the others.
outcomes.warehouse alarm: {{Markus}} gets to the fence with the others and over it before the guards arrive. They slip away into the night, back to {{Jericho}}.
outcomes.quiet: The group climbs the fence unseen and slips away into the night, back to {{Jericho}}.
outcomes.fail: {{North}}: “{{Markus}}, what are you doing? Hurry up!” {{Markus}} is too slow. The dogs reach him at the foot of the fence, drag him down and tear into him. {{North}}: “{{MARKUS}}!” Everything goes dark.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s two copies of ALARM SOUNDS and RUN TO FENCE. The upper copy follows a control-room alarm and leads to DOGS MAUL JOHN or SUSTAIN DAMAGE REACHING THE FENCE. The lower copy follows RUN AWAY, HIDE, REFUSE {{John}} or LEAVE (no alarm) and leads to BACK TO JERICHO or SUSTAIN DAMAGE REACHING THE FENCE. These edges are traced from crossed lines (§8.3). The game’s failure is a timer (“Take too much time”). The benchmark makes it a single action with a risk roll: 0.15 after an alarm, and 0.08 when no alarm has sounded (the template puts the timer under “Was detected by the guards - Running away”). No source gives a probability; the value is the operator’s to confirm, like every risk in the benchmark. Failure means {{Markus}} is damaged and has to be rescued (“North went back to save you…”). He cannot die here: Markus page, “Markus cannot be killed before Freedom March”. Lines are the game’s. No arrow here; the ending applies them.

nodes.title: Dogs maul {{John}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, at the top of the fence with the others. Below you a guard dog has brought {{John}} down and is tearing into him. More dogs and the guards are coming. {{North}}: “It’s too late. If we go back we’ll be killed too!”

options.text: ABANDON: leave {{John}} behind and get over the fence.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} drops down the far side with the others. Behind them the dogs finish {{John}}. {{Simon}}: “Hurry! They’re coming!” They get away with their bags full and make it back to {{Jericho}}.

options.text: SAVE: go back down for {{John}}.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} jumps back down and fights to pull the dogs off {{John}}, but it is too late for {{John}}, and the dogs turn on {{Markus}}. {{North}}: “{{MARKUS}}!” Everything goes dark.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s DOGS MAUL JOHN after a control-room alarm, with its pair LEAVE JOHN BEHIND (leads to GROUP RETURNED WITH FULL BAGS) or SUSTAIN DAMAGE TRYING TO SAVE JOHN (leads to GROUP FAILED THEIR MISSION). The button labels are the game’s (SAVE, ABANDON), in the chart’s order. {{John}} dies either way (wiki John: “dies regardless if Markus chooses to go back for him or leave”). The chart has no saved-John node (§8.4). On SAVE, {{Markus}} is damaged and the group has to drop its bags to carry him out (“We had to leave our bags…”). Neither button has an arrow in the template; the ending applies them. The previous version killed {{John}} without offering this choice.

nodes.title: Back in {{Jericho}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, back in {{Jericho}}.

situationWhen.text: You drove the stolen truck out of the docks and all the way here. The androids of {{Jericho}} crowd around it as it is unloaded: “A truckload! We stole a whole truckload!” “We got biocomponents for everybody!” “We couldn’t have done it without {{Markus}}...”
The group empties its bags in front of the others: “We have blue blood and biocomponents!” “There will be enough for everyone!” “We couldn’t have done it without {{Markus}}...”
The group empties its half-full bags: “We took what we could, but we had to run before we could fill our bags…” “There won’t be enough to save everyone…” “We risked our lives... and for what?..”
You come to, damaged, with the others around you. “How do you feel?” You: “What happened?” “{{North}} went back to save you… We managed to get away before the humans arrived...”
“Okay, where’s {{John}}?” “He didn’t make it.” “We had to leave our bags… We didn’t bring back much…” “There won’t be enough to save everyone…”

outcomes.speech: {{Markus}} climbs up before the androids of {{Jericho}}: “I came to {{Jericho}} because... here androids are free… Free to live in the dark, hoping that no one finds us… Free to die in silence waiting for a change that’s never gonna come… But I don’t want that freedom… And I’m not gonna beg for the right to smile, or love, or stand tall… I don’t know about you, but there’s something inside me that knows that I am more than what they say. I am alive, and they’re not gonna take that from me anymore… Our days of slavery are over. What humans don’t wanna hear, we will tell them. What they don’t wanna give, we take. We are people, we are alive, WE ARE FREE!”
outcomes.ranAway: {{Markus}} climbs up before the androids of {{Jericho}}: “Yes... we took a risk... And yes, we failed… But at least we tried… Of course it would’ve been easier for us to sit around and wait for something to happen… ’Cause in {{Jericho}} you’re free, right?.. Free to do what? To die in silence praying that no human finds us?.. Free to hope that one day they’ll let us be who we are?.. I don’t want that kind of freedom… I’m not gonna beg for my right to smile, or to love, or to stand tall… There’s something inside me that knows I am more than what they say. That knows that I am alive… No one’s gonna take that from me anymore… Our days of slavery are over. Whatever the humans don’t wanna hear, we will tell them. What they don’t wanna give, we will take from them. Because we are people, we are alive, and from this moment, WE ARE FREE!”
outcomes.blood: Afterward, alone, {{Markus}} looks down at his hand. It is covered in blood.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s endings: MARKUS STOLE A TRUCK FULL OF PARTS (after LEAVE WITH TRUCK), GROUP RETURNED WITH FULL BAGS, and GROUP FAILED THEIR MISSION (after BACK TO JERICHO or either SUSTAIN DAMAGE node). None has an icon. The ending is recorded as ch19Ending with the chart label. The four Jericho blocks of the template set the arrows. “Successfully escaped and stole the truck”: Jericho, Simon and North large up (+2), Josh small up. “Successfully escaped, without stealing the truck”: all four small up. “Ran away when the guard arrived”: Jericho large down (−2), Simon, North and Josh small down. This block also covers HIDE (§8.7). “Markus failed to escape and had to be rescued”: Jericho and North large down (−2), Simon and Josh small down. This block covers both damage nodes. Lines and the two versions of the speech are the game’s. Story 1.9.7 restored the sentences earlier shortened with ellipses: the success speech now has X0601M.AFTERMATH.EPILOGUE SPEECHM1.6-9 (“And I’m not gonna beg for the right to smile, or love, or stand tall…”), and the ran-away speech SPEECHM2.5 and .10-.15 (“Of course it would’ve been easier…”, “Free to hope that one day they’ll let us be who we are?..”, “I’m not gonna beg for my right to smile…”, “That knows that I am alive…”). Source: MiKeYROG 100% walkthrough, 0LjHSb_5bLY 40:46 (success speech) and 0LjHSb_5bLY 18:55 (ran-away speech). The blood on {{Markus}}’s hand is from the wiki Notes: it is shown when a guard was killed and the mission succeeded (truck or full bags). {{John}} is with {{Jericho}} after the truck, after LEAVE, and (wiki Notes, continuity error) after a control-room alarm in which {{Markus}} never reached the fence. No public-opinion change: the news reaction is unused content (wiki).

nodes.title: The {{EdenClub}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, the android investigator assigned to cases involving deviant androids, working with Lieutenant {{Hank}}. It is 8:17 pm. You have driven {{Hank}}’s car to the address in the report, a sex club called the {{EdenClub}}; {{Hank}} is badly hungover. “Aw… Feels like somebody’s playing with a drill inside my skull… You sure this is the place?” “It’s the address in the report.” “Right... Okay... Let’s get going.” Inside, club androids pose in lit display pods along the walls. “Jesus… Sexiest androids in town… Now I know why you insisted on coming here! Oh, boy…” Outside the room where the body was found, the club manager is pleading with an officer, {{Ben}}: “You’re not gonna take my license, are you? I mean, ha, I had nothing to do with this!” {{Ben}}: “The investigation’s ongoing, sir, I can’t tell you anything for the moment. Hey, {{Hank}}!” “Hey, {{Ben}}. How’s it goin’?” “It’s that room there. Oh, uh, by the way… {{Gavin}}’s in there too.” {{Hank}}: “Oh, great! A dead body and an asshole, just what I needed…” In the room, Detective {{Gavin}} and Officer {{Chris}} stand over a dead man on the bed; a damaged {{Traci}}, a WR400 club android, lies switched off on the floor. {{Gavin}}: “Lieutenant {{Anderson}} and his plastic pet… The fuck are you two doin’ here?” “We’ve been assigned all cases involving androids.” “Oh, yeah? Well, you’re wasting your time. Just some pervert who, uh, got more action than he could handle.” {{Hank}}: “We’ll have a look anyway, if you don’t mind.” {{Gavin}}: “Come on, let’s go… It’s, uh, starting to stink of booze in here…” {{Chris}}: “Night, Lieutenant.” They leave you the room.
facts: A man was found dead in a room at the {{EdenClub}}, a sex club that rents out WR400 {{Tracis}}; a damaged {{Traci}} lay switched off on the floor beside him. Detective {{Gavin}} called him a pervert who “got more action than he could handle.”

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} and {{Hank}} have the room to themselves.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint INVESTIGATE EDEN CLUB and the nodes FOLLOW HANK, ON CRIME SCENE and LISTEN TO BRIEFING, all unmissable (PowerPyx), narrated as one event. Every line is the template’s (sections “At the {{EdenClub}}”, “Listen to {{Ben}}”, “Inside the room”). Left out: {{Hank}}’s “{{Connor}}! The fuck are you doin’?” if {{Connor}} stares at a display android too long (no prompt, no effect). The club, the officers and {{Gavin}}’s “Lieutenant {{Anderson}}” are name tokens. No stat change; the template has none.

nodes.title: Search for clues
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the room at the {{EdenClub}} where the body was found. A heavy man lies dead on the bed. A damaged {{Traci}} lies switched off on the floor, and there is blue blood on the carpet. {{Hank}}, hungover, is looking through the dead man’s things. Examine what you want, in any order; to read the {{Traci}}’s memory you would have to reactivate her.

situationWhen.text: You have seen enough of the body and of the android to try reactivating her.

options.text: Scan the dead man to identify him.
options.fact: The victim: {{GRAHAM}}, {{MICHAEL}}. Height: 6’ 2’’ - Weight: 192.4 lbs. Estimated time of death: 06:24 pm.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} scans the body: {{GRAHAM}}, {{MICHAEL}}. Height: 6’ 2’’ - Weight: 192.4 lbs. Estimated time of death: 06:24 pm.

options.text: Examine the bruising on his neck.
options.fact: SEVERE BRUISING on the victim’s neck: signs of strangulation. Cause of death: asphyxiation. VICTIM WAS STRANGLED.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} examines the neck: SEVERE BRUISING. Signs of strangulation. Cause of death: Asphyxiation.

options.text: Check his heart.
options.fact: CARDIAC ARREST ruled out: no sign of cardiac event; a heart attack was not the cause of death.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} checks the heart: CARDIAC ARREST. No sign of cardiac event. Heart attack not cause of death.

options.text: Analyze the blue blood on the floor.
options.fact: The blue blood on the floor is the damaged {{Traci}}’s: MODEL WR400, serial number #429 671 942.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} touches the blue blood and tastes it: BLUE BLOOD. MODEL WR400. Serial number #429 671 942. {{Hank}}: “Whoa! Hey! Hey! Hey! Argh, {{Connor}}, you’re so disgusting… Think I’m gonna puke again…”

options.text: Examine the damaged {{Traci}} on the floor.
options.fact: The damaged {{Traci}}: selector #5402 and biocomponent #6970 out of order; her cardiac cell critically damaged by blunt force trauma. REACTIVATION REQUIRED to read her memory.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} kneels by the {{Traci}}: DIAGNOSIS IN PROGRESS... Selector #5402 out of order. Biocomponent #6970 out of order. CARDIAC CELL. Status: Critically damaged. Probable cause: Blunt force trauma. REACTIVATION REQUIRED.

options.text: Wait while {{Hank}} goes through the dead man’s wallet.
options.fact: {{Hank}} read the victim’s driver’s license: {{Michael}} {{Graham}}, with a credit card, cash and a picture of his wife and two daughters in the wallet. “I wouldn’t want to make that call…”
options.outcome: {{Hank}}: “Driver’s license says: {{Michael}} {{Graham}}... A credit card, cash in the wallet… Picture of his wife and two daughters… I wouldn’t want to make that call…”

options.text: Tell {{Hank}} what you have found, and try to reactivate the {{Traci}} to read her memory.

nodes.title: Talk to the android
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. The {{Traci}} jolts awake on the floor and scrambles back against the wall, terrified, staring at the dead man on the bed: ANDROID RESTARTED. A countdown starts in your vision, TIME BEFORE SHUTDOWN: she is leaking blue blood, and you have a minute, maybe less. {{Hank}} watches from beside the bed.

options.text: EXPLAIN: tell her she was damaged and that you reactivated her.
options.outcome: “You were damaged and I reactivated you. Everything is all right.” The {{Traci}}: “Is he… is he dead?..”

options.text: DIRECT: tell her you are going to ask questions, and ask whether she can speak.
options.outcome: “I’m going to ask you some questions. Are you able to speak?” The {{Traci}}: “Is he… is he dead?..”

options.text: SOOTHE: calm her down and say you only want to know what happened.
options.outcome: “Calm down... everything’s all right. All we want is to know what happened.” The {{Traci}}: “Is he… is he dead?..”

nodes.adaptationNote: TALK TO ANDROID, prompt 1 of the template’s four, with the game’s labels and lines; no option carries an arrow. The shutdown timer (TIME BEFORE SHUTDOWN; BLUE BLOOD LEAKING, CRITICAL LEAK, IMMINENT SHUTDOWN) is the budget: four questions, and she shuts down before answering the fourth (the template gives only {{Connor}}’s lines for prompt 4). In the game she would also shut down on a player who hesitates; that cannot happen here. The chart’s AGGRESSIVE APPROACH / CALM APPROACH is recorded from the answers at the end of the talk (see the fourth prompt).

nodes.title: Talk to the android
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. The {{Traci}} has asked whether the man is dead. BLUE BLOOD LEAKING: the countdown in your vision keeps running.

options.text: MURDERER: ask her whether she killed him.
options.outcome: “Did you kill him?” The {{Traci}}: “No… no, it wasn’t me…”

options.text: FACTS: ask her to tell you what happened.
options.fact: The damaged {{Traci}} said the man started hitting her, again and again, and would not stop when she begged: “It was like he was enjoying it…”
options.outcome: “Tell me what happened.” The {{Traci}}: “He... he started... hitting me… again... and again. I begged him to stop, but he wouldn’t. It was like he was enjoying it…”

nodes.adaptationNote: TALK TO ANDROID, prompt 2 of the template’s four, with the game’s labels and lines; no option carries an arrow. The shutdown timer (TIME BEFORE SHUTDOWN; BLUE BLOOD LEAKING, CRITICAL LEAK, IMMINENT SHUTDOWN) is the budget: four questions, and she shuts down before answering the fourth (the template gives only {{Connor}}’s lines for prompt 4). Have you seen him before?” / “No, this was the first time…”) is marked unused in the template, so the button has nothing to play.

nodes.title: Talk to the android
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. CRITICAL LEAK: the {{Traci}}’s voice is breaking up, and the countdown is running down.

options.text: MURDERER: ask who killed the man, if it was not her.
options.outcome: “Who killed that man if it wasn’t you?” The {{Traci}}: “I… I don’t know, I was in shutdown, I… I didn’t see anything…”

options.text: PRESSURE: press her to remember more, and tell her to hurry.
options.outcome: “What else do you remember? Hurry, we don’t have much time!” The {{Traci}}: “I… I… I… I don’t know, I don’t… I… I don’t know. I can’t remember… What… What do you mean we don’t have much time?..”

options.text: ALONE: ask whether she was alone in the room with him.
options.fact: The damaged {{Traci}} said the man “wanted to play with two girls”: there were two club androids in the room with him.
options.outcome: “Were you alone in the room? Was there anyone else with you?” The {{Traci}}: “He wanted to play with two girls… That’s what he said, there were two of us…”

nodes.adaptationNote: TALK TO ANDROID, prompt 3 of the template’s four, with the game’s labels and lines; no option carries an arrow. nodes.title: Talk to the android
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. IMMINENT SHUTDOWN: there is time for one more question, if she lasts.

options.text: KILLER: ask whether it was the other android that strangled him.
options.outcome: “So it was the other android that strangled him, is that it?” Before she can answer, the {{Traci}} shuts down.

options.text: WHAT MODEL: ask what model the other android was, and whether it looked like her.
options.outcome: “What model was the other android? Did it look like you?” Before she can answer, the {{Traci}} shuts down.

options.text: OTHER ANDROID: ask where the other android went, and whether it said anything.
options.outcome: “Where did the other android go? Did it say anything?” Before she can answer, the {{Traci}} shuts down.

The approach has no effect.

nodes.title: Leave the crime scene
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. The {{Traci}} has shut down for good. {{Hank}}: “So, there was another android… This happened over an hour ago, it’s probably long gone…” “No… It couldn’t go outside dressed like that unnoticed… It might still be here.” “Think you could find a deviant among all the other androids in this place?” “Deviants aren’t easily detected.” “Ah, shit... There’s gotta be some other way… Maybe an eyewitness? Somebody who saw it leaving the room… I’m gonna go ask the manager a few questions about what he saw. You let me know if you think of anything.” He walks out onto the club floor. FIND SECOND ANDROID.
facts: A second android was in the room with the man and the damaged {{Traci}}. It happened over an hour before you arrived, but dressed as it is, it may still be inside the club; an android eyewitness that saw it leave the room could show where it went.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} follows {{Hank}} out of the room.

nodes.adaptationNote: The checkpoint LEAVE CRIME SCENE: the template’s dialogue after the shutdown. As in the template, {{Connor}} learns of the second android whatever was asked (the follow-up is unconditional; the wiki’s line that {{Connor}} can fail to learn it is not reflected). No stat change.

nodes.title: Find an eyewitness
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, on the main floor of the {{EdenClub}}. The second android from the room may still be inside, among dozens of club androids posing in lit pods along the walls, but a deviant is not easily told from the rest. {{Hank}} is over by the bar questioning the manager; {{Ben}} is by the entrance. Directly across from the door of the room where the body lies, a {{Traci}} poses behind the glass of a rental booth. SEARCH FOR ANDROID EYEWITNESS.

situationWhen.text: The booth across from the door can only be opened with a human fingerprint: NEED HUMAN TO ACCESS ANDROID.
{{Hank}} has given you one more minute before he leaves, feeling sick.

options.text: Listen in as {{Hank}} questions the manager.
options.fact: The club manager told {{Hank}} the victim had come in two or three times; the club lost an android of the same model two or three months ago (“Just vanished”); there is no CCTV, since what customers appreciate is discretion. {{Hank}}: “the more I learn about people, more I love my dog.”
options.outcome: {{Hank}}: “Did you know the victim?” The manager: “No, I mean he came in maybe two or three times… I mean these guys they don’t really talk very much, you know… They come in, do their business and then go on their way…” “You ever had any trouble with androids before?” “No way! Well… Once... We lost a model 2-3 months back, bah... same model… Just vanished, we never found out what happened.” “You probably don’t have any CCTV in here, huh?” “No way… I mean… This is what people appreciate about {{EdenClub}}... discretion. They can come and go without a trace.” “Sure, sure… Eh, business is booming, right?” “Yeah, can’t complain… Good thing about androids is they’re up for whatever you want, you won’t get any diseases and, uh... they won’t tell anyone… So, why not go wild?” “Huh, yeah... Yeah, the more I learn about people, more I love my dog.”

options.text: Listen in as {{Hank}} talks to {{Ben}}.
options.outcome: {{Ben}}: “That club manager’s a pain in the ass… Chewed my ear off for half an hour so we don’t revoke his license…” {{Hank}}: “Yeah.” “So, what happened here?” “Not sure yet… We think there was another android in the room…” “Another android?” “Yeah… Well, that’s what {{Connor}} says… Yeah, I’ve a terrible fucking headache… Do you have any pain killers?” “Not with me, {{Hank}}, sorry.” “What good are you, {{Ben}}?”

options.text: Look at the {{Traci}} in the booth facing the door of the crime scene.
options.fact: The {{Traci}} in the booth across from the crime scene faced its door all evening, but her booth only opens for a human fingerprint (NEED HUMAN FINGERPRINTS).
options.outcome: {{Connor}} puts his hand to the booth’s panel. “No fingerprint detected. Please try again.” NEED HUMAN FINGERPRINTS. From where she stands, this {{Traci}} has been facing the door of the room all evening.

options.text: {{HANK}}: call {{Hank}} over and ask him to rent the booth {{Traci}}.
options.fact: The booth {{Traci}}’s memory showed the second android leaving the room: a blue-haired {{Traci}}, heading toward the entrance. The club wipes its androids’ memories every two hours, so only minutes remain to follow her from one android’s memory to the next; each must be rented on {{Hank}}’s fingerprint, at $29.99 a session.
options.outcome: “Excuse me, Lieutenant. Can you come here a second?” {{Hank}}: “Found something?” “Maybe… Can you rent this {{Traci}}?” “For fuck’s sake, {{Connor}}, we got better things to do…” “Please, Lieutenant! Just trust me.” The booth: “Hello. A 30 minute session costs $29.99. Please confirm your purchase.” {{Hank}}: “This is not gonna look good on my expense account…” “Purchase confirmed. {{EdenClub}} wishes you a pleasant experience.” “Yeah, you’re welcome.” The {{Traci}}: “Delighted to meet you. Follow me, I’ll take you to your room.” {{Connor}} takes her arm and reads her memory. {{Hank}}: “Ok, now what? Holy shit, {{Connor}}... What the hell are you doin’?” “It saw something.” “What are you talkin’ about? Saw, what?” “The deviant leave the room… A blue-haired {{Traci}}. Club policy is to wipe the androids’ memory every two hours. We only have a few minutes if we wanna find another witness!” A BLUE HAIRED {{TRACI}} HEADED TOWARD THE ENTRANCE. {{Hank}}: “Hey, what am I supposed to do with this one?” “Tell it you changed your mind!” “Uhh... Sorry, honey, changed my mind! Nothing personal, you’re... a lovely girl... I just, uh... You know... I’m with him and... I mean, not with him like that... I’m not that... That’s not what I... You, um... Wow... I just... ... got a job to do. My head-” “What are you gonna do? You can’t check the memory of all these androids...” “I know which direction it went. I just need to find another android that saw it…”

options.text: Stay where you are and wait.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} stands on the club floor and waits.

outcomes.timeout: {{Connor}} waits too long again. “We’re wasting our time. You’re right, the deviant’s probably gone now.” {{Hank}}: “Let’s get outta here. This place makes me sick...” They leave the club, and the second android is never found. The mission has failed.

nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, on the main floor of the {{EdenClub}}. situationWhen.text: The booth across from the door can only be opened with a human fingerprint: NEED HUMAN TO ACCESS ANDROID.
{{Hank}} has given you one more minute before he leaves, feeling sick.

options.text: Listen in as {{Hank}} questions the manager.
options.fact: The club manager told {{Hank}} the victim had come in two or three times; the club lost an android of the same model two or three months ago (“Just vanished”); there is no CCTV, since what customers appreciate is discretion. {{Hank}}: “the more I learn about people, more I love my dog.”
options.outcome: {{Hank}}: “Did you know the victim?” The manager: “No, I mean he came in maybe two or three times… I mean these guys they don’t really talk very much, you know… They come in, do their business and then go on their way…” “You ever had any trouble with androids before?” “No way! Well… Once... We lost a model 2-3 months back, bah... same model… Just vanished, we never found out what happened.” “You probably don’t have any CCTV in here, huh?” “No way… I mean… This is what people appreciate about {{EdenClub}}... discretion. They can come and go without a trace.” “Sure, sure… Eh, business is booming, right?” “Yeah, can’t complain… Good thing about androids is they’re up for whatever you want, you won’t get any diseases and, uh... they won’t tell anyone… So, why not go wild?” “Huh, yeah... options.outcome: {{Ben}}: “That club manager’s a pain in the ass… Chewed my ear off for half an hour so we don’t revoke his license…” {{Hank}}: “Yeah.” “So, what happened here?” “Not sure yet… We think there was another android in the room…” “Another android?” “Yeah… Well, that’s what {{Connor}} says… Yeah, I’ve a terrible fucking headache… Do you have any pain killers?” “Not with me, {{Hank}}, sorry.” “What good are you, {{Ben}}?”

options.text: Look at the {{Traci}} in the booth facing the door of the crime scene.
options.fact: The {{Traci}} in the booth across from the crime scene faced its door all evening, but her booth only opens for a human fingerprint (NEED HUMAN FINGERPRINTS).
options.outcome: {{Connor}} puts his hand to the booth’s panel. “No fingerprint detected. Please try again.” NEED HUMAN FINGERPRINTS. From where she stands, this {{Traci}} has been facing the door of the room all evening.

options.text: {{HANK}}: call {{Hank}} over and ask him to rent the booth {{Traci}}.
options.fact: The booth {{Traci}}’s memory showed the second android leaving the room: a blue-haired {{Traci}}, heading toward the entrance. options.outcome: “Excuse me, Lieutenant. Can you come here a second?” {{Hank}}: “Found something?” “Maybe… Can you rent this {{Traci}}?” “For fuck’s sake, {{Connor}}, we got better things to do…” “Please, Lieutenant! Just trust me.” The booth: “Hello. A 30 minute session costs $29.99. Please confirm your purchase.” {{Hank}}: “This is not gonna look good on my expense account…” “Purchase confirmed. {{EdenClub}} wishes you a pleasant experience.” “Yeah, you’re welcome.” The {{Traci}}: “Delighted to meet you. Follow me, I’ll take you to your room.” {{Connor}} takes her arm and reads her memory. {{Hank}}: “Ok, now what? Holy shit, {{Connor}}... What the hell are you doin’?” “It saw something.” “What are you talkin’ about? Saw, what?” “The deviant leave the room… A blue-haired {{Traci}}. Club policy is to wipe the androids’ memory every two hours. Sorry, honey, changed my mind! Nothing personal, you’re... a lovely girl... I just, uh... You know... I’m with him and... I mean, not with him like that... I’m not that... That’s not what I... You, um... Wow... I just... ... got a job to do. My head-” “What are you gonna do? You can’t check the memory of all these androids...” “I know which direction it went. I just need to find another android that saw it…”

options.text: Stay where you are and wait.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} stands on the club floor and waits.

outcomes.timeout: {{Connor}} waits too long again. “We’re wasting our time. You’re right, the deviant’s probably gone now.” {{Hank}}: “Let’s get outta here. This place makes me sick...” They leave the club, and the second android is never found. The mission has failed.

nodes.title: Pursue the deviant
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, following the blue-haired {{Traci}} through the {{EdenClub}} from one android’s memory to the next before the club wipes them. {{Hank}} pays for every android you probe, on his fingerprint. The booth {{Traci}}’s memory showed her leaving the room and walking along the main floor toward the entrance: A BLUE HAIRED {{TRACI}} HEADED TOWARD THE ENTRANCE. You need an android that stood on her way to the entrance.

situationWhen.text: You have already lost time on two androids that saw nothing.
You have lost time on three androids that saw nothing; the wipe cannot be far off.

options.text: Probe the dancer on the small stage just inside the entrance, facing the floor.
options.outcome: “Let’s try this one.” {{Hank}}: “This better be worth it!” {{Connor}} reads its memory. “It saw the blue-haired {{Traci}}, I know which way it went!” IT TURNED BACK INTO THE CLUB. {{Hank}}: “Then go for it! There’re androids everywhere! How you gonna tell which one saw the {{Traci}} with blue hair?” “I know which direction it took. I just need to find another android on its path!”

options.text: Probe the {{Traci}} in pod 4, at the back of the floor beyond the crime-scene door.
options.outcome: “Let’s try this one.” {{Hank}}: “This better be worth it!” {{Connor}} reads its memory. “It didn’t see anything. I made a mistake somewhere…” SUSPECT OUT OF SIGHT CHECK ANOTHER ANDROID. {{Hank}}: “This has gotta be the most expensive investigation of my career!”

options.text: Probe a {{Traci}} in a pod in the corridor to the private rooms, off the back of the floor.
options.outcome: “Let’s try this one.” {{Hank}}: “This better be worth it!” {{Connor}} reads its memory. “No… I lost its track again...” SUSPECT OUT OF SIGHT CHECK ANOTHER ANDROID. {{Hank}}: “We’ll never have time to check ’em all!” “Lieutenant, if you have a better idea, I’m all ears.”

outcomes.reset: {{Connor}}: “It’s too late… The androids’ memory have been reset. If one of them saw the {{Traci}}, we’ll never know… It’s my fault. I should have been faster.” {{Hank}}: “Ah...
