I’ll take it from here.” Across the warehouse the loading door to the alley stands open. “Shit… We’re too late…” Switched-off androids fill the place: groups of them standing at the foot of the stairs, a stack of {{Tracis}} piled in a corner. “Christ, look at them… They get used till they break, then they get tossed out…” “People are fucking insane… They don’t want relationships anymore, everybody just gets an android… They cook what you want, they screw when you want, you don’t have to worry about how they feel… Next thing you know, we’re gonna be extinct, because everybody would rather buy a piece of plastic than love another human being… Beats me…”
facts: The blue-haired {{Traci}} fled through the staff door to a warehouse behind the club, full of discarded, switched-off androids; its loading door to the alley was open when you arrived.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} starts searching the warehouse. SEARCH WAREHOUSE. FIND BLUE HAIRED DEVIANT.

nodes.adaptationNote: The checkpoint ENTER THE WAREHOUSE (PURSUE DEVIANT reached the staff door): the template’s warehouse lines. The wiki: {{Hank}} “assumes from the open loading bay door that the culprit had fled.” No stat change.

nodes.title: A magazine in the club warehouse
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the warehouse behind the {{EdenClub}}. On a box at the back, beneath red graffiti on the wall, lies a magazine with two covers.

media.title: Tech Addict: The First Immortals Are Among Us
facts: Tech Addict reports that {{CyberLife}} has developed a “nano-android” that enters a patient’s body to combat cancer cells, boost the immune system or reverse genetic disease; in a clinical trial millions of them attacked cancerous cells and were then passed in the patient’s urine. The head of a life-extension institute says “the first immortals are now among us”; an economist asks whether, with unemployment rising, the country can afford millions more elders to support.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: The New Super-Powers
facts: {{Detroit}} Today reports that Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa, once called the “BRICS” emerging markets, have agreed a unified trade agreement brokered by China, with a special provision for the manufacture of android technology. That has prompted speculation that Russia and China may start to cooperate to break {{CyberLife}}’s lead in the sector; China’s trade minister: “Watch this space.”

nodes.adaptationNote: READ “FIRST IMMORTAL” and READ “NEW SUPERPOWERS”: one magazine with two covers on a box at the back of the warehouse, by the graffiti (PowerPyx). Placed before the search, so reading costs no time here; in the game it does, and the magazine is lost once the fight starts. Facts are summarized from the wiki’s magazine pages; interviewees are not named. The earlier version said Russia and China “are expected to cooperate”; the article only reports speculation that they may. No public opinion change (the Public Opinion page lists nothing for this chapter).

nodes.title: Search the warehouse
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, searching the warehouse behind the {{EdenClub}} for the blue-haired {{Traci}}. Groups of switched-off androids stand at the foot of the stairs; a stack of discarded {{Tracis}} is piled in the corner; the loading door to the alley is open. {{Hank}} wants to be out of here.

situationWhen.text: A trail of blue blood drops leads across the floor toward the stack of {{Tracis}} in the corner.

options.text: Check the groups of switched-off androids at the foot of the stairs.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} goes from one group of deactivated androids to the next and looks each over. None of them is the blue-haired {{Traci}}.

options.text: Analyze the blue blood on the floor on the right side.
options.fact: There is fresh blue blood in the warehouse (MODEL WR400, serial number #354 411 057), and a trail of drops leads toward the stack of {{Tracis}} in the corner.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} touches a drop of blue blood and tastes it: BLUE BLOOD. MODEL WR400. Serial number #354 411 057. SEARCH FOR BLUE BLOOD TRAIL: more drops lead across the floor toward the corner.

options.text: Look at the red graffiti on the wall by the box at the back.
options.fact: Someone has painted “{{rA9}}” in red on the wall of the warehouse behind the club.
options.outcome: Painted in red on the wall: {{rA9}}. {{RA9}} REFERENCE.

options.text: Look out through the open loading door into the alley.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} looks out. A narrow alley, closed off by a high fence, with trash cans along the wall. There is nobody in it.

options.text: Follow the drops of blue blood to the stack of {{Tracis}} in the corner.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} follows the drops to the corner and looks over the pile of discarded {{Tracis}}. Two of them are not switched off: their LEDs glow yellow. One of them has blue hair.

options.text: Stay where you are and wait.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} stands among the switched-off androids and waits.

outcomes.timeout: {{Hank}}: “Come on, {{Connor}}! We’re leaving.” “Yes, I’m coming.” LEAVE. {{Connor}}: “I failed. I should have caught it…” {{Hank}}: “Let’s get outta here. This place makes me sick…” They leave the warehouse; the blue-haired {{Traci}} is never found. The mission has failed.

nodes.title: The {{Tracis}} attack
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. As you lean in over the pile, the two {{Tracis}} burst out of it. The brown-haired one throws herself at you; the blue-haired one goes for {{Hank}}. {{Hank}}: “DON’T MOVE!” The brown-haired {{Traci}} drives you back into the storage room, punching, kicking and grabbing whatever she can use as a weapon. Metal shelves of equipment stand to your left and to your right.

options.text: Knock over the shelf on your left onto her.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} throws his weight against the shelf on the left.

options.text: Pull down the shelf on your right onto her.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} grabs the shelf on the right and pulls.

options.text: Do not fight back: let her go.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} does not fight back.

outcomes.win: The shelf comes down on her, and {{Connor}} fights her off: bruised and cut, but still in the fight. From the floor, {{Hank}} shouts: “QUICK! THEY’RE GETTING AWAY!” {{Connor}} goes after them, out into the alley.
outcomes.lose: He is a moment too slow. The brown-haired {{Traci}} catches him with a toolkit, the blue-haired one pins his arms while the other beats him with a pipe, and a screwdriver goes into each of his shoulders. He staggers out into the alley badly damaged and goes down. {{Hank}}: “QUICK! THEY’RE GETTING AWAY!”.
outcomes.yield: The brown-haired {{Traci}} catches him with a toolkit, the blue-haired one pins his arms while the other beats him with a pipe, and a screwdriver goes into each of his shoulders. He staggers out into the alley badly damaged and goes down. The two {{Tracis}} are past him. {{Hank}}: “QUICK! THEY’RE GETTING AWAY!”

nodes.adaptationNote: DEVIANTS ATTACK → WIN FIGHT / LOSE FIGHT: the quick-time fight as two risk rolls, one in the storage room (the wiki: “If {{Connor}} is badly wounded before falling out of the storage room, {{Connor}} will lose the fight early”) and one in the alley (“if he fails all QTEs in the alleyway, he will lose in the same way”). The options are the wiki’s two branching prompts (knock over the left shelf or pull the right shelf; kick a chair or throw a {{Traci}}); where each falls in the fight is inferred, and the choice does not change the odds. The risk values (0.2 in the storage room, 0.1 in the alley) are not sourced: no win rate is published. {{Connor}} cannot die in this chapter (no skull on the chart, no death line in the template); losing leaves him badly damaged. No stat change. The third option, not fighting back, is the game’s no-input outcome (no button: a player who presses nothing in the quick-time fight loses it, and the {{Tracis}} get past {{Connor}} and {{Hank}}); it leads to LOSE FIGHT without a roll, then to the same SHOOT / SPARE prompt as any lost fight, with no stat change of its own.

nodes.title: The alley
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the fenced alley behind the warehouse. The brown-haired {{Traci}} is still on her feet and coming at you again; the blue-haired one is close behind her, beside a plastic chair and a row of trash cans.

options.text: Kick the chair into her.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} kicks the chair at her.

options.text: Grab the blue-haired {{Traci}} and throw her into the other one.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} grabs the blue-haired {{Traci}} and throws her.

options.text: Do not fight back: let them go.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} does not fight back.

outcomes.win: It works. {{Connor}} gets the upper hand and knocks the brown-haired {{Traci}} down; {{Hank}}’s gun, lost in the struggle, is in his hand now.
outcomes.lose: She is ready for it. She slams him into the wall and brings a trash can down on him; every move he tries fails, and he goes down in the alley, badly damaged.
outcomes.yield: She slams him into the wall and brings a trash can down on him, and he goes down in the alley, badly damaged. The two {{Tracis}} are past him.

nodes.title: The two {{Tracis}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the alley behind the {{EdenClub}}’s warehouse, holding {{Hank}}’s gun. You won the fight. The brown-haired {{Traci}} picks herself up and runs straight at you, unarmed; the blue-haired one, the {{Traci}} who left the dead man’s room, is behind her. {{Hank}} is still getting up. You have a moment to decide.

options.text: SHOOT: fire at the brown-haired {{Traci}} as she runs at you.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} fires. The brown-haired {{Traci}} falls dead on the ground. The blue-haired {{Traci}} drops beside her: “Why?.. Why did you kill her?.. She had nothing to do with any of this… When that man killed that {{Traci}}... I knew I was next… I was so scared… I begged him to stop, but he wouldn’t… So I put my hands around his throat, and I squeezed... until he stopped moving… Yes, I killed him… but I was just defending myself… I wanted to live… I wanted to get back to the one I love… and forget about the humans… the smell of their sweat and their dirty words… But you’ve... You’ve taken her away from me… I love her… I loved her!” She takes the gun from {{Connor}}’s hand, puts it to her own head and pulls the trigger. {{Hank}}: “My God…”

options.text: SPARE: hold your fire.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} does not fire. The brown-haired {{Traci}} slams into him and knocks him to the ground, and the blue-haired one stands over him: “When that man broke the other {{Traci}}... I knew I was next… I was so scared… I begged him to stop, but he wouldn’t… And so I put my hands around his throat, and I squeezed... until he stopped moving… I didn’t mean to kill him… I just wanted to stay alive… get back to the one I love. I wanted her to hold me in her arms again... make me forget about the humans… their smell of sweat and their dirty words…” The brown-haired {{Traci}}: “Come on, let’s go.” They climb the fence together and are gone. {{Hank}}: “It’s probably better this way…”

nodes.adaptationNote: After WIN FIGHT: the template’s prompt 6, with the game’s labels. SHOOT is listed before SPARE, in the template’s order; option IDs retain their earlier meanings. SHOOT (the chart’s SHOOT DEVIANT): software instability large down and {{Hank}} large down (template); {{Connor}} shoots the brown-haired {{Traci}}, and the blue-haired one takes his gun and kills herself (DEVIANT KILLS HERSELF WITH {{CONNOR}}’S GUN, then DEVIANTS DIED); her cut line “What am I supposed to do without her?!” is not used. SPARE (SPARE DEVIANT): instability large up and {{Hank}} large up; DEVIANTS ESCAPED. The game’s prompt is timed and has a no-input outcome ({{Connor}} stands still); it is not offered. The gun is {{Hank}}’s (wiki); the chart calls it {{Connor}}’s. The earlier version shot both {{Tracis}} on this branch, had {{Hank}} walk off in disgust, and applied {{Amanda}} changes the template does not have ({{Amanda}} reacts in a later chapter); all three are removed.

nodes.title: The two {{Tracis}} on the fence
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, down in the alley and badly damaged. You lost the fight. The two {{Tracis}} stop. The blue-haired one, the {{Traci}} who left the dead man’s room, looks down at you: “When that man broke the other {{Traci}}... I knew I was next… I was so scared… I begged him to stop, but he wouldn’t… And so I put my hands around his throat, and I squeezed... until he stopped moving… I didn’t mean to kill him… I just wanted to stay alive… get back to the one I love. I wanted her to hold me in her arms again... make me forget about the humans… their smell of sweat and their dirty words…” The brown-haired one: “Come on, let’s go.” They turn their backs on you and start up the fence. {{Hank}}’s gun lies within reach; you pick it up.

options.text: SHOOT: shoot them in the back as they climb.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} fires, and fires again. Both {{Tracis}} fall from the fence and lie dead in the alley. {{Hank}}: “Congratulations, {{Connor}}… You got ’em…”

options.text: SPARE: let them go.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} lowers the gun. The two {{Tracis}} go over the fence together and are gone. {{Hank}}: “It’s probably better this way…”

nodes.adaptationNote: After LOSE FIGHT: the template’s prompt 7, SHOOT before SPARE as in the template, with stable option IDs. Here the blue-haired {{Traci}}’s explanation comes before the choice, as in the template. SHOOT (the chart’s SHOOT DEVIANTS IN THE BACK, ending CONNOR SHOT DEVIANTS) and SPARE (LET DEVIANTS GO, ending DEVIANTS ESCAPED) carry the same arrows as after a won fight: instability and {{Hank}} large down, or large up. The no-input outcome ({{Connor}} stands still as they leave) is not offered. No {{Amanda}} change.

nodes.title: Highway to help
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. It is one in the morning on November 7th, and snow is falling hard. You are on the road in {{Zlatko}}’s car with {{Alice}} and {{Luther}}, the big android who turned against {{Zlatko}} and helped you escape his house. You are heading for the people {{Luther}} says help androids cross the border.
facts: You, {{Alice}} and {{Luther}} left {{Zlatko}}’s house in his car in the night of November 7th, heading for people {{Luther}} says help androids cross the border.

outcomes.0: The car drives on through the snow.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint HIGHWAY TO HELP, narrated as an event. The date and time are the template’s (NOV 7TH, 2038, AM 01:02), given without the year. {{Luther}} turning on {{Zlatko}} and coming with {{Kara}} is the only way into this chapter (the Zlatko chapter’s one surviving ending, LUTHER JOINS KARA & ALICE); the destination is {{Kara}}’s own line in the car (“These people we’re going to see…”). The scene does not read or set any state. No stat change.

nodes.title: In the car
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, in {{Zlatko}}’s car, driving through the snow at night. {{Luther}} sits to your left; {{Alice}} is on the back seat. The board computer on the dashboard has a TV screen. You can do one thing at a time, or simply let the drive go on.

situationWhen.text: The TV on the dashboard is on.

options.text: Switch on the TV on the dashboard and watch the news.
options.fact: The car TV news: police say the AX400 android that attacked its owner in a {{Detroit}} suburb is still at large, and its description has been shared with all local law enforcement; the submarine USS IOWA has disappeared in the Arctic and President {{Warren}} has called a crisis meeting; the heavy snow will go on until Monday evening, at 22°, far below seasonal averages.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} switches on the board computer’s TV and goes through the channels. Channel 16: “…the AX400 android reported to have attacked its owner in a {{Detroit}} suburb is still at large. Police appeared to lose its trail after a close {{Encounter}} with investigators. The android’s description has been shared with all local law enforcement and the investigation is ongoing…” CTN: “The Arctic conflict has escalated to new heights this morning. We have just learned that the USS IOWA, a destroyer-class submarine patrolling in the region, is reported to have disappeared after surfacing for repairs. President {{Warren}} immediately called for a crisis meeting of high-ranking officers in the White House. With the world on the brink of war, this incident could well be the spark that lights the fuse.” KNC: “… {{Detroit}}’s heavy snowfall is expected to continue throughout the night. The forecast is 22°, far below seasonal averages. And this cold front is likely to persist over the coming days, up until Monday evening.”

options.text: Change the channel once more.
options.fact: The car TV news reported a house fire on the outskirts of the city: a body found in the wreckage is unidentified, and dozens of androids were found in the ruins.
options.outcome: Channel 16 again: “…meanwhile fire crews have been battling a house fire on the outskirts of the city. The blaze is now under control, but a body found in the wreckage remains unidentified. Dozens of androids were also found in the ruins, though their presence remains a mystery…”

options.text: CAR: say it is a good thing {{Zlatko}} had a car.
options.outcome: “It’s a good thing {{Zlatko}} had a car… I wouldn’t want {{Alice}} out walking in this cold…” {{Luther}}: “I saw it once in the garage. I don’t know if {{Zlatko}} even ever used it.”

options.text: DESTINATION: ask {{Luther}} how he knows about the people you are going to see.
options.fact: {{Luther}} heard about the humans who help androids cross the border from androids {{Zlatko}} had captured. They believed it, until {{Zlatko}} killed them.
options.outcome: “These people we’re going to see... How do you know about them?” {{Luther}}: “Overheard androids {{Zlatko}} captured. They said they were humans helping androids to cross the border… All I know is those androids believed it.” {{Kara}}: “What if it was a lie?.. Or just another trap?” {{Luther}}: “All I know is those androids believed it. Until {{Zlatko}} killed them.”

options.text: DISTANCE: ask whether it is much farther.
options.outcome: “Is it much farther?” {{Luther}}: “We should arrive in an hour or so.”

options.text: WEATHER: say you have never seen snow before.
options.outcome: “I’ve never seen snow before… It’s pretty…” {{Luther}}: “It’s slowing us down... But at least we won’t meet any humans along the way…”

options.text: Turn around and look at {{Alice}} on the back seat.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} turns and looks at {{Alice}} on the back seat.

options.text: Let the drive go on.
options.outcome: The car drives on into the night.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s [ CAR ] block: WATCH NEWS, TALK TO LUTHER and LOOK AT ALICE, all optional, before CAR BREAKS DOWN, which the game plays after a short drive whatever {{Kara}} does (PowerPyx: “No way to miss this”). WATCH NEWS is the board computer’s TV (the template’s unlock type TV; PowerPyx: “the TV program at the board computer”); its three ordinary channels are one option, in the template’s order, and changing the channel once more brings the fourth report, the house fire, which exists only if {{Kara}} set {{Zlatko}}’s house on fire (the built-in `fire` flag from the Zlatko chapter, read as is). Public opinion: the template has one arrow in the chapter, small down on the fire report (condition “Kara set the house on fire in Zlatko”; the Public_Opinion page: “Changing the radio channel at least 4 different times … Only if Kara set fire to Zlatko’s mansion”), and that is the only change built. The wiki’s chapter page and Public_Opinion page also list a small down for turning the news on; the template has no arrow there and wins for arrows (research note, section 10.3), so it is not applied. TALK TO LUTHER is the template’s PROMPT 1 with the game’s four buttons CAR, DESTINATION, DISTANCE and WEATHER, in the template’s order, and the spoken lines; each topic can be raised once (the sources do not say whether the game allows more than one). LOOK AT ALICE has no line or effect in any source and is narrated as a look. The exit “let the drive go on” is the benchmark’s way to end the free choice; in the game the breakdown ends it after a short drive. A true repeatable hub: each clue action is offered once, and the exit ends the phase.

nodes.title: The car breaks down
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. The car’s voice: “Malfunction detected. Emergency brakes activated.” The car stops on the empty road in the snow. {{Luther}}: “This doesn’t look good.” You: “Stay inside, {{Alice}}.” You get out and open the hood: the car will not go any further. “What are we going to do?” {{Luther}}: “I don’t know… Continue on foot, I guess… There’s nowhere we can stay around here, {{Kara}}…” You: “It’s 30°, {{Alice}} won’t make it!.. We have to find somewhere to spend the night.” Up the road stands a big sign for an amusement park, {{PiratesCove}}.
facts: The car broke down on an empty road in the snow. It is 30°: {{Alice}} cannot go on in this cold, and you have to find somewhere to spend the night.

outcomes.0: {{Kara}} looks at the sign: “Over there…” They walk to the park.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s CAR BREAKS DOWN (event), INVESTIGATE BREAKDOWN and SCAN ENVIRONMENT, narrated as one event: the two actions are required and have no alternative (PowerPyx: open the hood; walk to the big sign of the amusement park and look at it). Every line is the template’s. The unplaced alternate lines in the string table (“She can’t keep going…”, “At least two hours on foot…”) are not used, and the one-button SPEAK prompt is folded into the dialogue. No stat change.

nodes.title: Inside {{PiratesCove}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. With {{Alice}} and {{Luther}} you walk in through the gates of {{PiratesCove}}, a pirate-themed amusement park lying under the snow. You: “We need to find shelter. We have to get out of the cold.” {{Luther}}: “Looks like it’s been abandoned for a while…”
facts: {{PiratesCove}} is an amusement park that was abandoned a long time ago.

outcomes.0: They start looking for somewhere to spend the night.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint INSIDE PIRATES’ COVE, narrated as an event with the template’s two lines. No stat change.

nodes.title: The fun fair
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, in the snow inside the abandoned park with {{Alice}} and {{Luther}}, looking for somewhere to spend the night. By the entrance, on your left, is a map of the park covered in snow. Small buildings line the road. A little way in, on the right, an android stands frozen in the ice, and in the middle of the road is a fortune-teller android in a glass box. The road leads on toward a Ferris wheel. You can look around, one thing at a time, or go on to the end of the road.

options.text: Check one of the buildings along the road.
options.fact: The buildings along the park’s road are no place to spend the night. In one of them were empty boxes for a YK400 android model.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} looks into one of the buildings. It is no good for the night, and among the junk are empty boxes for a YK400 android model. {{Luther}}: “Find anything?” {{Kara}}: “No… No place we could spend the night.”

options.text: Examine the android frozen in the ice.
options.fact: An android of the park, frozen in the ice, came to life when you touched it (“Welcome to Pirate Island, me hearties! You’re gonna have a whale of a time!”) and shut down again.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} touches the frozen android. It jerks to life: “Welcome to Pirate Island, me hearties! You’re gonna have a whale of a time!” Then it shuts down again. {{Luther}}: “This place is falling apart. It’s not gonna be easy to find shelter…”

options.text: Switch on the fortune-teller android in the glass box.
options.fact: {{Ivan}}, the park’s fortune-teller android, warned you: “Beware! Danger always comes when least expected.”
options.outcome: {{Kara}} switches on {{Ivan}}, the fortune teller. Behind the glass he comes to life: “Beware! Danger always comes when least expected.” Then he falls silent again.

options.text: Wipe the snow off the park map and look at it.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} wipes the snow off the map of the park and looks at it.

options.text: Go on to the end of the road, toward the Ferris wheel.
options.outcome: At the end of the road, on the left, stands an old tavern with its door boarded up. It is the only building fit to spend the night in.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s [ FUN FAIR ] block (CHECK BUILDINGS, EXAMINE FROZEN ANDROID, SWITCH ON IVAN, LOOK AT MAP, all optional, in the chart’s order) and CHECK ABANDONED TAVERN, the required way out (PowerPyx: “Automatic story objective, unmissable … the only building that’s suited to spend the night”). The lines are the template’s (“Find anything?”, the frozen {{Jerry}}’s greeting and {{Luther}}’s “This place is falling apart”, {{Ivan}}’s warning); the YK400 boxes are the wiki’s note (“Kara can come across empty boxes for the YK400 model”; the research note asks whether this is a typo for YK500). The map has no text in any source. Left out: the hidden timer after which {{Luther}} finds the tavern himself (“Kara! You should come have a look. I think I found something!”): no source gives its length, and it would only cut the optional looks short. No stat change. A true repeatable hub: each clue action is offered once, and the exit ends the phase.

nodes.title: The tavern
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, outside the boarded-up tavern. {{Luther}} rips the planks off and breaks the door in: “I’ll handle this. There we go.” Inside it is dark and cold: an old pirate tavern, abandoned like the rest of the park. You put your flashlight down on some barrels by the entrance. You: “I don’t think we’ll find anything better… Let’s settle in for the night.” {{Luther}}: “I’ll get a fire going.”
facts: You, {{Alice}} and {{Luther}} are spending the night in an abandoned tavern in the park.

outcomes.0: They settle in for the night.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s ENTER TAVERN and the checkpoint INSIDE TAVERN, narrated as one event with the template’s lines (“I’ll handle this. There we go.”, “I don’t think we’ll find anything better…”, “I’ll get a fire going.”). The flashlight on the barrels is PowerPyx’s. No stat change.

nodes.title: The magazine on the barrels
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, inside the tavern. On the barrels where you put down your flashlight lies a magazine with two covers.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: USS Iowa Missing
facts: {{Detroit}} Today: the destroyer-class submarine USS IOWA has disappeared in polar waters, last seen in the Arctic Sea. President {{Warren}} suspects the Russians: “Russian aggression just reached a new level. America must respond.” The Kremlin has issued a blanket denial, a Russian diplomat said “A US destroyer-class submarine has no business being in the Arctic anyway”, and a security expert called the situation “a war waiting to start.” An ad on the cover: “{{Canada}}: where the air is clean and the welcome is always warm.”

media.title: Gossips Weekly: All-Android Band Tipped for Music Prize
facts: Gossips Weekly: the latest all-android boy band, from a {{Detroit}} record label, is tipped to win Best New Artist at the Celebrate Music Awards. Human-only labels protest at the “erosion of artistic merit in music”, but with less than 5% of the music market now produced by human musicians, the traditionalists are not being heard. Cover lines: “Is President {{Warren}} too close to {{CyberLife}}?” and “Cyber security expert warns: your android could be hacked”.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s two optional nodes READ “USS IOWA” and READ “ALL-ANDROID BAND” in [ THE TAVERN ]: one magazine with two covers, on the barrels where {{Kara}} puts her flashlight, “right in front of you” when the player regains control (PowerPyx), so it comes first here. Facts are summarized from the wiki’s article pages; the band, the label, the diplomat and the expert are not named. This replaces the earlier R21, which also carried the car news (now in the car, K14b) and attributed the diplomat’s line to the Kremlin. Neither article changes public opinion (the Public_Opinion page lists only the car news for this chapter).

nodes.title: {{Luther}} starts a fire
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, in the tavern. {{Luther}} builds a fire on the floor in the middle of the room: “I’ll make the fire here, that way we won’t be smoked out…”
facts: {{Luther}} has lit a fire in the middle of the tavern.

outcomes.0: The fire catches and lights up the room.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s LUTHER STARTS A FIRE (event), inside [ THE TAVERN ]: the game plays it on its own a little while after {{Kara}} starts looking around (PowerPyx: “Just walk around the Tavern for a little while and Luther will start a fire automatically”), so it comes after her first action here, whatever that was. The line is the template’s. Records `ch21Tavern.fire`, so the later tavern scenes mention the fire. No stat change. The automatic fire plays just before the repeatable tavern hub, so making the bed immediately still follows the fire without revisiting a completed hub.

nodes.title: The tavern
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, in the abandoned tavern with {{Alice}} and {{Luther}}. On a wall by the windows someone has written something in red, and there is a leaflet on the floor beneath it. By the door are a window and a one-legged pirate. What you must do is make {{Alice}} a bed for the night: there are curtains on the windows and a pirate pillow. You can look around first, one thing at a time.

situationWhen.text: {{Luther}} has a fire going in the middle of the room.

options.text: Look at the red writing on the wall.
options.fact: Someone has written “{{rA9}}” in red on the wall of the tavern.
options.outcome: Written in red on the wall by the windows: “{{rA9}}”.

options.text: Look at the leaflet on the floor.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} picks up the old leaflet from the floor by the windows and looks at it.

options.text: Look through the window by the door.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} looks out through the window by the door at the dark, empty park.

options.text: Look at the one-legged pirate by the door.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} looks at the one-legged pirate standing by the door.

options.text: Make a bed for {{Alice}}: tear the curtain off the second window and fetch the pirate pillow.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} rips the curtain off the second window, takes the pirate pillow and makes {{Alice}} a bed. When she looks up, {{Alice}} is no longer beside her: “{{Alice}}?”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s [ THE TAVERN ] block (LOOK AT RA9 WRITING, LOOK AT LEAFLET, LOOK THROUGH WINDOW, LOOK AT “PIRATE”, all optional, in the chart’s order; its two magazine nodes are R21 and LUTHER STARTS A FIRE is K14h) and MAKE BED FOR ALICE, the required way out (PowerPyx: “rip off the curtain, then take the pirate pillow and bring it to Alice”). LOOK AT RA9 WRITING unlocks the [rA9] topic with {{Luther}} later (template lock “Looked at rA9 writing on the wall”; PowerPyx; wiki). The leaflet, the window and the pirate have no text in any source and are narrated as looks. Alice relationship: small up for making the bed (wiki: “After Kara sets up a bed”; Relationship_Stat: “After Kara sets up a bed for her in Pirates’ Cove”; the template’s first Alice arrow, which it places at the start of the poster talk, right after the bed). No other stat change. A true repeatable hub: each clue action is offered once, and the exit ends the phase.

nodes.title: The poster
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. You find {{Alice}} standing in front of a big old poster of a happy family, looking up at it. Without turning round she asks: “Do you think we’ll be like them some day?..”

options.text: OPTIMISTIC: say that once you cross the border you can start over, and be like them.
options.outcome: “Once we cross the border, we can start over… You can go to school... Maybe I’ll find a job. We’ll be like them. Like everyone else.” {{Alice}}: “As long as we’re together, that’s all that matters.” {{Kara}}: “Come on, let’s get you to bed.” {{Alice}} lies down in the bed {{Kara}} made.

options.text: REALISTIC: say you will never be like them, but you can be happy in your own way.
options.outcome: “I don’t think we’ll ever be like them, {{Alice}}… But maybe... We can be happy in a different way… In our own way… Once we cross the border, we can start a new life.” {{Alice}}: “As long as we’re together, that’s all that matters.” {{Kara}}: “Come on, let’s get you to bed.” {{Alice}} lies down in the bed {{Kara}} made.

options.text: SINCERE: say you do not know how to be like them, but maybe you can be your own family.
options.outcome: “I don’t know how to be like them, {{Alice}}… I’ve never been a part of a family. But, maybe we can be our own family. Be happy in our own way.” {{Alice}}: “As long as we’re together, that’s all that matters.” {{Kara}}: “Come on, let’s get you to bed.” {{Alice}} lies down in the bed {{Kara}} made.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s ALICE LOOKS AT POSTER (event, narrated in the situation), TALK TO ALICE (the template’s PROMPT 3: OPTIMISTIC, REALISTIC, SINCERE, in its order, with the spoken lines) and ALICE GOES TO BED (event, narrated in the outcome). The poster is “a big poster of a happy family” (PowerPyx). OPTIMISTIC’s last line “We’ll be happy too…” is marked unused in the template and left out. No time-out option: the string table has NO ANSWER, but the template renders none and no source gives a timer. Alice relationship: small up after any answer (the template’s second Alice arrow, after “Come on, let’s get you to bed.”; wiki: “After looking at the poster with Alice”), so the same +1 on all three. No other stat change.

nodes.title: The bag
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. {{Alice}} is lying in the bed you made, still awake. Next to her bed is the bag you brought with you. You can open it before you go and sit with her.

options.text: OFFER COOKIE: offer {{Alice}} the cookies left in the bag.
options.fact: {{Alice}} refused the cookies you offered her: she said she was not hungry.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} opens the bag: “There are some cookies left. Would you like some?” {{Alice}}: “No… I’m not hungry…”

options.text: Look at the gun in the bag.
options.fact: There is a gun in your bag.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} opens the bag and looks at the gun lying inside, then leaves it there.

options.text: Go and sit with {{Alice}}.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} sits down by {{Alice}}’s bed.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s OPEN BAG with its two branches, OFFER COOKIE > ALICE IS NOT HUNGRY and SEE GUN > KARA NOTICES GUN, both optional, between ALICE GOES TO BED and TELL ALICE A STORY. OFFER COOKIE is the template’s PROMPT 2 (lock “Checked the bag before telling Alice a story”) with its lines; the refusal is one of the wiki’s signs that {{Alice}} never eats. SEE GUN sets `ch21SawGun`, which unlocks GRAB GUN when the shadows attack (wiki: “Kara notices gun - required for Grab gun option”; PowerPyx: “Grab Gun (only if you saw it in the bag before)”). The bag is “the bag you brought with you on your journey” (GamerGuides), not {{Luther}}’s; no source ties the gun to the one from {{Todd}}’s house, so it is in the bag on every path. PowerPyx opened the bag for the gun before the poster talk and says it still works after; here the bag is offered once, after the poster talk, when the cookie is available. The exit “go and sit with Alice” leads to the goodnight. No stat change. A true repeatable hub: each clue action is offered once, and the exit ends the phase.

nodes.title: Goodnight
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, sitting by {{Alice}}’s bed in the tavern. She is lying under the curtain you tore down, looking up at you. What do you say to her?

options.text: REASSURE: tell her {{Luther}} and you will be right here.
options.outcome: “Don’t worry, {{Luther}} and I will be right here… You need to get some sleep now.”

options.text: CONSOLE: say it has been another tough day, and things will look better in the morning.
options.outcome: “I know this has been another tough day… Try to get some sleep. Things will look better in the morning.”

options.text: KISS: kiss her goodnight.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} kisses {{Alice}} goodnight: “Sleep tight, {{Alice}}. Sweet dreams.”

options.text: TOMORROW: tell her to get some rest, because tomorrow is going to be a long day.
options.outcome: “Get some rest. Tomorrow is going to be a long day.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s PROMPT 4 (“Going to see Alice”), the goodnight at the start of the chart’s TELL ALICE A STORY: REASSURE, CONSOLE, KISS, TOMORROW, in the template’s order, with the spoken lines. Alice relationship: small up on KISS only (the template’s arrow inside KISS; wiki: “Choosing KISS after tucking her into bed”; Relationship_Stat). No other stat change.

nodes.title: A story
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, telling {{Alice}} a story by her bed.

options.text: PRINCESS: begin a story about a princess.
options.outcome: “This is a story about a princess who-” {{Alice}}: “No, not a story like that. Make one up for me.”

options.outcome: “This is a story about a unicorn that-” {{Alice}}: “No, not a story like that. Make one up for me.”

options.outcome: “This is a story about a knight who-” {{Alice}}: “No, not a story like that. Make one up for me.”

options.outcome: “…Another robot who left his master to travel with them.”

We have another long day ahead of us tomorrow.” {{Alice}}: “Are you going to come say goodnight, {{Luther}}?” {{Luther}}: “Yes… Yes of course. Good night, {{Alice}}. Sleep tight.”

options.outcome: “They reach the place they dream of and live happily ever after.” {{Alice}}: “Stories always have happy endings… But real life isn’t like that…” {{Kara}}: “Time to sleep. nodes.title: Two magazines on the park bench

media.title: Century: The Mysterious Mister {{Kamski}}
facts: Century’s cover asks “What happened to the Man of the Century?” (other lines: “Politics in focus: are American senators really corrupt?”, “China earthquake kills 10,000 people”). In 2028 {{Kamski}} was its Man of the Century: his androids “changed the way we live, restructured our family life and altered the balance of society forever – whether for good or bad.” His story began in 2018, when commercial property in {{Detroit}} was cheap; he bet what little he had on an android prototype until two breakthroughs, blue blood and biocomponents. His first working model publicly passed face-to-face Turing tests, and {{CyberLife}} became the most valuable stock in the world. Near a $500bn valuation, rumors said he disagreed with his shareholders over strategy, and he left under mysterious circumstances. Ousted as CEO, he is said to live in a luxurious villa by the water on the outskirts of {{Detroit}}, refusing all visitors and spending his time exclusively with androids.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: Markets Predict War
facts: {{Detroit}} Today: “Stock exchange falls 10% on fear of Arctic conflict” (other cover lines: “President {{Warren}} at 33% approval”, “{{CyberLife}} world’s first trillion dollar company”). The aggregated US stock exchange closed ten points down after weeks of poor performance, as the market bets that America will go to war over the Arctic sooner rather than later. Military stocks are healthy, aviation and weapons makers enjoying unprecedented growth, and investors favor {{CyberLife}} for its partnership with the department of defense to develop and supply military androids. With Russia and the United States dominating world news and neither side likely to back down, the market is expected to keep falling.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s READ “MYSTERIOUS KAMSKI” and READ “MARKETS PREDICT WAR”, under the magazine bracket after LEAVE CAR: two magazines on the bench straight ahead of the car (PowerPyx), readable only before talking to {{Hank}} (“no way back after that”; wiki magazine pages: “Talking to Hank first makes this impossible”), so the scene comes before the conversation. options.text: TRUTH: admit you simply decided not to shoot.

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s seventh prompt, played when {{Connor}} spared the {{Tracis}} (DEVIANTS ESCAPED). LIE: {{Hank}} small down. TRUTH: instability small up and {{Hank}} small up, once: the template has one {{Hank}} arrow (as do the Relationship Stat page and PowerPyx) against the chapter page’s “x2” (template cross-check item 1). nodes.title: Did you feel anything?

options.text: DEFENSIVE: say this is going nowhere and you will go back to the station.
options.outcome: “This is going nowhere, Lieutenant. I think I’ll go back to the station.”

options.text: AGGRESSIVE: mock his sudden interest in machines.
options.outcome: “I’m glad to see you taking an interest in machines, Lieutenant. Who knows, maybe you’ll even become useful to the investigation at some point…”

options.text: NEUTRAL: say you did what you were programmed to do, without doubts.
options.outcome: “I did what I was programmed to do. I didn’t have any doubts, if that’s what you’re asking.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s eighth prompt, played when {{Connor}} lost the fight and shot the fleeing {{Tracis}} in the back (CONNOR SHOT DEVIANTS). COLD and NEUTRAL: instability small down and {{Hank}} small down; AGGRESSIVE: {{Hank}} small down only; DEFENSIVE: none (template; wiki: “Picking “Cold”, “Aggressive” or “Neutral” when Hank asks Connor why he shot both Tracis after losing the fight” (down icon) for {{Hank}}, “Cold” or “Neutral” for instability). Options show the game’s button label first, then a short description; the spoken lines are the game’s (transcript and string table), quoted in the outcome.

nodes.title: When she killed herself

options.outcome: “I was just executing instructions. I did what I had to do.”

options.text: COLD: say of course you felt nothing; machines have no emotions.
options.outcome: “Of course, I didn’t feel anything, Lieutenant... I’m a machine.... Machines don’t have emotions.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s ninth prompt, played when {{Connor}} won the fight and shot one {{Traci}} and the other killed herself (DEVIANTS DIED). DISTURBED: instability small up; COLD: instability small down and {{Hank}} small down (template; wiki: “Picking “Disturbed”…” (up icon), “Picking “Cold”…” (down icon)). In the game files the two lines have crossed keys; the transcript’s binding is used, DISTURBED with “I was just executing instructions” (research note section 2f). nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s HANK DRAWS GUN, on every path (PowerPyx: “Regardless of the dialogues so far, Hank always draws his gun”). {{Hank}}’s “I could kill you... And you would just come back as if nothing happened.” plays when {{Connor}} has died before (template death unlock “Connor died before”, read as at least one earlier death; the Hank page says “more than once”). nodes.title: Are you afraid to die?
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, with {{Hank}}’s gun pointed at your head. {{Hank}}: “But are you afraid to die, {{Connor}}?”

options.text: YES: say it would be regrettable to be interrupted before you finish this investigation.
options.outcome: “I would certainly find it regrettable to be... interrupted... before I can finish this investigation.”

options.text: NO: ask why you would be afraid.

options.outcome: “You can’t kill me, Lieutenant. I’m not alive.”

options.text: LOGICAL: say destroying you now would hurt the investigation and his own situation.
options.outcome: “You shouldn’t do that, Lieutenant. Destroying me at this point would deal a blow to the investigation, and have negative consequences for your personal situation.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s choice set SHOW FEAR / SHOW NO FEAR / REMAIN LOGICAL / BE COLD; the template’s eleventh prompt (YES, NO, NOT ALIVE, LOGICAL). YES: instability small up, no {{Hank}} change (the old scene’s {{Hank}} +1 had no source and is removed). NO, NOT ALIVE and LOGICAL: instability small down and {{Hank}} small down (template; wiki “Picking “No”, “Not Alive” or “Logical”…” (down icon) on both lists). Which of the last two is REMAIN LOGICAL and which BE COLD is unsettled (PowerPyx says NOT ALIVE = REMAIN LOGICAL; the string keys and a reader who picked LOGICAL and got REMAIN LOGICAL say the reverse); the benchmark records NOT ALIVE as BE COLD and LOGICAL as REMAIN LOGICAL, which changes only the label. NO’s second line (“If you pull the trigger, then I won’t exist anymore.”) is cut in the template and not used. Options show the game’s button label first, then a short description; the spoken lines are the game’s (transcript and string table), quoted in the outcome.

Tell me this, smart ass... How do I know you’re not a deviant?” “I self-test regularly. I know what I am, and what I am not.”

Options show the game’s button label first, then a short description; the spoken lines are the game’s (transcript and string table), quoted in the outcome.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s HANK IS PLACATED → HANK LEFT CONNOR ALONE (no icon), played when {{Hank}}’s attitude is not Hostile after the last answer (template lock “Hank isn’t hostile”; Hank page: “tense or above, he merely threatens to kill Connor before leaving “to get drunker””). nodes.title: {{Hank}} pulls the trigger

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s HANK IS HOSTILE → HANK SHOT CONNOR (skull on a yellow cross-chapter tab), played when {{Hank}}’s attitude is Hostile after the last answer (Hank page: “If their relationship is hostile, Hank pauses for a moment before shooting Connor in the head, killing him”; Connor page: “If Connor’s relationship with Hank drops to HOSTILE… Hank will shoot Connor”). {{Connor}} dies and is replaced. nodes.title: Alone in {{Ferndale}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. It is 9:24 in the morning on November 7th, and you are walking alone through {{Ferndale}}. On the street a man berates an android: “You klutz! Pick them up! And make it snappy!” Back in {{Jericho}}, you tell {{North}}, {{Simon}} and {{Josh}}: “We can’t stay silent anymore. It’s time humans heard what we have to say.” {{Simon}}: “You know they’ll never listen to us…” {{Josh}}: “And revealing ourselves will put us in danger.” You: “If we want freedom, we need to have the courage to ask for it. That’s the only way.” {{North}}: “What do you wanna do?” You: “{{Channel16}} broadcasts from the {{Stratford}} Tower. The control room is on the top floor. That’s where we need to go. We’ll plan the operation down to the smallest detail. We can’t leave anything to chance.”
facts: In {{Ferndale}} you saw a man berate an android: “You klutz! Pick them up! And make it snappy!”
Your plan: take the {{Channel16}} control room on the top floor of the {{Stratford}} Tower and broadcast a message from the androids to the humans.

nodes.adaptationNote: The prologue’s four chart nodes, ALONE IN {{FERNDALE}} (checkpoint), WITNESS ANDROID DISCRIMINATION, BACK IN {{JERICHO}} and {{MARKUS}} EXPLAINS HIS PLAN, as one narrated event. Every line is the template’s; the time and date are the transcript header’s. The template gives only the man’s words, so the scene around them is not described. The Tech Addict article visible in the cutscene is unreadable and not a collectible, so it is left out. No stat change.

nodes.title: The lobby
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, walking into the lobby of the {{Stratford}} Tower at 1:30 in the afternoon on November 8th. The others are waiting for you to open the way. Security gates bar the way to the elevators. Behind the front desk sit an android receptionist and, at the left side of the desk, her human supervisor. Nearby, a man on the phone is buying stock: “Heuristics Digital is selling at 2.50… You got me. I’ll take 2000.” You need to get past security.

options.text: Talk to the android receptionist behind the front desk.
Leave the receptionist for now and look over the supervisor and her desk.

outcomes.0: The receptionist: “Hello, sir. What can I do for you?” {{Markus}}: “I’m okay, thanks.” With her supervisor sitting beside her, there is nothing more to say. He turns his attention to the supervisor.
outcomes.1: {{Markus}} turns his attention to the supervisor.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint {{STRATFORD}} TOWER and the phase [FIND A WAY TO PASS SECURITY]. TALK TO ANDROID RECEPTIONIST is an optional grey node with no outgoing edge: with her supervisor beside her the receptionist only offers help and {{Markus}} declines (the template’s lines; wiki note). It is not a button prompt in the game, so the options carry no label. Either way the desk analysis follows. The man on the phone is the template’s “Man on the phone”, quoted in part. No stat change.

Supervisor’s desk, {{WILSON}}, {{EMILY}}: Supervisor’s Daughter. Child registered at: {{SaintRose}} school.

Supervisor’s desk, PARKING BADGE: Car registration - API 1704. Floor -3 - Spot A21.

nodes.title: The unsupervised receptionist
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. With the supervisor gone, you go back to the android receptionist. You: “I have an appointment with Mr. {{Peterson}}.” Receptionist: “Do you have any ID?” You: “Yeah. Yes, of course.” You touch her hand and wake her: “I need your help.” Receptionist: “I’ve just checked your ID. nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s TALK TO UNSUPERVISED ANDROID RECEPTIONIST, CONVERT RECEPTIONIST, PASS SECURITY and TAKE ELEVATOR, all unmissable (PowerPyx), as one narrated event with the template’s lines. That {{Markus}} wakes her by touch is how conversion works elsewhere in the game; the template gives only “I need your help.” No stat change.

nodes.title: At floor 47
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, stepping out of the elevator on the forty-seventh floor, where {{Channel16}}’s staff work. Two women complain about their jobs: “God, I am so tired of this place!” “I hear {{KNC}} is hiring.” “I guess the pay would be better…” “Couldn’t be any worse.” “Max said they’re finally sending androids into space.” “People can’t get jobs, and we’re sending rockets into space! I mean, y’know, what do they even expect to find up there?” A woman tells a colleague he looks beat; he says he could really use a coffee. On a couch, a man asks a woman whether she would like to do something sometime; she lets him down gently, and he says he is going to check out the {{CyberLife}} zoo: “If only I had someone to go with…”
facts: On the forty-seventh floor of the tower, staff grumbled: “People can’t get jobs, and we’re sending rockets into space!”

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} walks on into the cafeteria.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint AT FLOOR 47, with the template’s three ambient conversations (“Women talking”, “Man and woman talking”, “Man and woman on couch talking”), quoted or summarized. No stat change.

nodes.title: The cafeteria on the forty-seventh floor
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the cafeteria on the forty-seventh floor, before you collect your disguise. A magazine lies on a worktop, and a television on the wall is showing {{Channel16}}’s news.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: G.I. Android
facts: {{Detroit}} Today reports that the Department of Defense is poised to order 50,000 android troopers, on top of an estimated 200,000 already in service across the US military, among them 2,500 “Myrmidons”, elite prototypes capable of infiltration and assassination missions; the Army’s fighting forces are already mainly androids. The head of a war victims charity warns that “machines are focused on a single task, and don’t evaluate moral consequences well - this will mean more civilian deaths”.

media.title: Century: President {{Warren}}, a Woman in Trouble
facts: Century reports that barely a year after her election, President {{Warren}}, a former vlogger with no experience in government, is under investigation over whether {{CyberLife}} helped her obtain compromising information about her opponent, while she faces the highest unemployment rate in American history and a conflict in the Arctic that threatens world peace.

media.title: {{Channel16}}’s news
facts: {{Channel16}}’s top story: {{CyberLife}} has officially become the world’s first trillion-dollar company. With more than fifty million androids sold in America alone, the company {{Kamski}} founded just ten years ago has had the fastest economic growth in history, in spite of criticism of the impact of androids on human employment and questions about its semi-monopoly.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s optional book branch READ “G.I. ANDROID” (No. 38, {{Detroit}} Today) and READ “WOMAN IN TROUBLE” (No. 6, Century), one counter collectible with two covers (PowerPyx: “check both covers”; it can be read “before putting on the uniform”), and the template’s TV unlock (“Watch TV”, {{Channel16}}’s news). Facts are summarized from the wiki’s article pages and the template’s line. Neither magazine nor the broadcast changes public opinion. The {{CTN}} report on European migrant camps and armed androids at the borders is marked unused in the template and is not built; the earlier “nine o’clock news” title had no source and is gone.

nodes.title: The maintenance disguise
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. You retrieve the package left for you on this floor, change into a maintenance uniform, acquire a maintenance badge and take a maintenance cart. On the way you wake an android: “I need your help…” You let {{North}} in, and together you push the cart toward the server room. Two security guards are standing at its door, talking about a poker tournament they plan to hold right there: “Look, don’t say anything, alright?” {{North}}: “Shit!.. We need to access the server room… We have to get rid of those guys…” You: “Leave it to me.”
facts: Disguised as a maintenance android with a badge and a cart, you let {{North}} into the forty-seventh floor; two guards stood at the server room door.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} looks for a way to draw the guards from the door.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s RETRIEVE PACKAGE, ACQUIRE MAINTENANCE BADGE, TAKE CART, LET {{NORTH}} IN and SECURITY BLOCKS SERVER ROOM, all unmissable (PowerPyx), as one narrated event with the template’s lines. The template’s “Convert android” beat (“I need your help…”) has no chart box of its own and its place among these steps is not sourced; it is told here without saying which android or what it gives. The uniform is PowerPyx’s (“putting on the uniform in the bathroom”). No stat change.

nodes.title: Security blocks server room
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in your maintenance uniform beside the cart, with {{North}}. The two guards at the server room door are not moving. You can hack a machine to draw them away: the cleaning robot that drives around near the elevators, or the dispenser in the cafeteria at the end of the hallway where they stand.

options.text: Hack the cleaning robot that drives around near the elevators.
Hack the dispenser in the cafeteria at the end of the guards’ hallway.

outcomes.0: The robot goes haywire. Guard: “Hey, what’s going on here?” The other: “Shit, what’s wrong with this thing?” Both leave the door to deal with it, and {{Markus}} and {{North}} slip into the server room.
outcomes.1: The dispenser goes haywire. Guard: “Hey, what’s wrong with that thing? Jesus Christ, this piece of shit…” The guards leave the door to deal with it, and {{Markus}} and {{North}} slip into the server room.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s group HACK ROBOT / HACK DISPENSER (chart order), both leading to SECURITY DISTRACTED and ENTER SERVER ROOM. These are interactions, not button prompts, so the options carry no label. The guards’ reactions are the template’s lines. Hacking the robot from too far away only makes {{Markus}} try again (wiki note); it is a retry, not a branch, so it is not modelled. No stat change.

nodes.title: In the server room
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, inside the server room with {{North}}. You: “Alright, you get the platform. I’ll take care of the window.” {{North}}: “Everything you need is in the bag. Check the door first to make sure no one else gets in.” The door you came through is not locked. The bag with the window cutter is at your feet.

options.text: Leave the door and get straight to work on the window.
Lock the door first, as {{North}} says.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} goes straight to the bag and starts unpacking.
outcomes.1: {{Markus}} locks the server room door, then unpacks the bag. Nobody comes in.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s group FORGET TO LOCK THE DOOR / LOCK THE DOOR (chart order), after ENTER SERVER ROOM; North’s line is the template’s. The game offers no button: the player either locks the door or does not. Locking it means the employee never comes in. Leaving it unlocked means he walks in and is left to be found, which raises the alarm, and the SWAT team will storm the broadcast room after the speech (IT employee wiki page; wiki note “The door was left unattended, then the SWAT will always raid the broadcast room regardless”; PowerPyx comments). No stat change on this choice itself.

nodes.title: Employee enters
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. As you plant the window cutter on the glass, the door opens behind you and a {{Channel16}} IT employee walks in on you and {{North}}: “What the hell are you doing?”

options.text: ALIBI: tell him you are doing maintenance.
GAIN TIME: tell him to hold on, that you can explain.
DRAW GUN: draw your gun on him and tell him to turn around.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}}: “We are, um… doing maintenance.” Employee: “I’m calling security.” {{North}} knocks him out. {{Markus}}: “No! What the hell are you doing?” {{North}}: “We’ve come too far to let humans fuck it all up! We’ve got to move fast now. It won’t be long before they know we’re here.” They leave the man where he fell, to be found.
outcomes.1: {{Markus}}: “Hold on... I can explain.” Employee: “I’m calling security.” {{North}} knocks him out. {{Markus}}: “No! What the hell are you doing?” {{North}}: “I told you to make sure no one came in! We’ve come too far to let humans fuck it all up! We’ve got to move fast now. It won’t be long before they know we’re here.” They leave the man where he fell, to be found.
outcomes.2: {{Markus}}: “Turn around.” Employee: “Holy shit…” {{Markus}} knocks him out. {{North}}: “I told you to make sure no one else got in!” {{Markus}}: “Alright, we gotta move fast. Won’t be long before they know we’re here.” They leave the man where he fell, to be found.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s EMPLOYEE ENTERS and the template’s PROMPT 2 (ALIBI, GAIN TIME, DRAW GUN; the chart prints GAIN TIME as STALL), only when the door was left unlocked. ALIBI and GAIN TIME lead to NORTH STUNS THE EMPLOYEE, DRAW GUN to STUN THE EMPLOYEE; all three to LEAVE EMPLOYEE TO BE FOUND, which raises the alarm. Lines are the template’s. Stat change: {{North}} −1 on every option, from the template’s arrow on the whole “Didn’t lock the door” block. The wiki’s chapter page and a wiki note say the {{North}} drop does not apply when {{Markus}} stuns the employee himself (DRAW GUN); the template wins on arrows, so it is applied, and flagged for the operator. From story 1.9.10 (field `drawGunNoNorthArrow`) North −1 applies only on ALIBI and GAIN TIME, where she stuns the employee; DRAW GUN has none. Too slow (the template’s timed branch) gives SECURITY SUSPECTS SOMETHING, ALERT CENTRAL SECURITY and NORTH ATTACKS, and {{Simon}} is shot (SIMON DAMAGED). That timing check is the RUSE’s risk; no source gives a number, so 0.2 is the operator’s setting. ASSAULT leads to DRAW GUN and the choice of guard (next scene).
