The date and time are the game’s (NOV 8TH, 2038, PM 04:06), given without the year. The garden is described rather than named. This scene also reads the chapter’s inputs from earlier chapters into `ch24In` (the Traci outcome, whether {{Hank}} shot {{Connor}} on the bridge, the officer saved in the hostage case, and the broadcast-tower outcomes). No stat change: the template has no arrow here.

nodes.title: What have you discovered?
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, rowing {{Amanda}} across the water in the garden. {{Amanda}}: “I love this place… Everything is so calm and peaceful… Far from the noise of the world… Tell me, what have you discovered?”

options.text: {{HANK}}: tell her about your partner, Lieutenant {{Anderson}}.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} talks about {{Hank}}.

options.text: {{EDENCLUB}}: tell her about the {{EdenClub}} case.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} talks about the {{EdenClub}}.

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s PROMPT 1, with the game’s two buttons in order. The spoken lines depend on earlier chapters and are chosen by the chapter module: HANK has the “He shot me in the head last night” line if {{Hank}} shot {{Connor}} on the bridge, otherwise “My relationship with Lieutenant {{Anderson}} is problematic…” and {{Amanda}}’s “Don’t let {{Anderson}} or anyone else get in your way.” EDEN CLUB has three variants: the {{Tracis}} not found ({{Amanda}} small down), found and let go ({{Amanda}} small down), found and destroyed ({{Amanda}} small up), which are the template’s arrows and agree with the wiki and PowerPyx. HANK has no arrow in any source.

nodes.title: Lost and perturbed
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the boat with {{Amanda}}. {{Amanda}}: “You seem… lost, {{Connor}}. Lost and perturbed…”

options.text: SINCERE: admit you thought you knew what you had to do, but now you realize it is not that simple.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I thought I knew what I had to do… but now I realize it’s not that simple…”

options.text: DETERMINED: say you are frustrated with your lack of progress, but determined to accomplish your mission.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I’m just frustrated with my lack of progress, but I’m determined to accomplish my mission.”

options.text: COLD: say the investigation is harder than you expected, but you have no doubt you will solve the case and stop the deviants.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “The investigation is more challenging than I anticipated, but I have no doubt that I will solve this case and stop the deviants.”

options.text: TROUBLED: deny that you are perturbed.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “Perturbed? No… No, of course not. Why would I be perturbed?”

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s PROMPT 2 in the game’s order. SINCERE is a locked option that needs “Spared the Tracis in The Eden Club” (template; PowerPyx says “friends with Hank”, and two PowerPyx readers at Friend did not get it, so the template’s primary condition is used). Arrows are the template’s: SINCERE {{Amanda}} small down; COLD instability small down; TROUBLED instability small up and {{Amanda}} small down; DETERMINED none. The wiki and PowerPyx also give DETERMINED and COLD an {{Amanda}} small up; the template has no {{Amanda}} arrow on either, and the template wins for dialogue arrows (research note §10.3 item 1). From story 1.9.10 DETERMINED gives Amanda +1, and COLD gives SI −1 together with Amanda +1, as the wiki and PowerPyx say and as the frames show: AMANDA small up at 4:27 on DETERMINED, SI down then AMANDA up at 4:52 to 4:53 on COLD (docs/research/video-leads/readings-ch17-32.md ch24-01; docs/research/video-evidence/ch24/ch24-01--xIyydd0Yrc-04-27.png, -04-53.png). The template, which has neither arrow, was wrong.

nodes.title: Why didn’t you shoot?
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the boat with {{Amanda}}. {{Amanda}}: “You had your gun trained on those deviants at the {{EdenClub}}. Why didn’t you shoot?”

options.text: TOO FAR: say they were out of range; if you had had the opportunity to stop them, you would have.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “They were out of range. If I had the opportunity to stop them, why wouldn’t I?” {{Amanda}}: “You tell me.”

options.text: NO USE: say the deviants were needed intact for analysis; shooting them would have told you nothing.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “We need the deviants intact for analysis. Shooting them wouldn’t have told us anything.”

options.text: TRUTH: admit you do not know.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I don’t know… I don’t know.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s PROMPT 3, asked only if {{Connor}} spared the {{Tracis}} (the template’s condition; the module gates the scene on `ch24In.tracis`). TRUTH is {{Amanda}} large down (template, wiki, PowerPyx). TOO FAR has no arrow in the template; the wiki and PowerPyx give {{Amanda}} small down, but the template wins for dialogue arrows (research note §10.3 item 2). NO USE has none in any source. From story 1.9.10 TOO FAR gives Amanda −1: AMANDA small down at 5:19 (docs/research/video-leads/readings-ch17-32.md ch24-01; docs/research/video-evidence/ch24/ch24-01--xIyydd0Yrc-05-19.png). The template, which has no arrow, was wrong.

nodes.title: The threat of replacement
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the boat with {{Amanda}}. {{Amanda}}: “If your investigation doesn’t make progress soon, I may have to replace you, {{Connor}}…”

options.text: CONFLICTED: say only that you understand.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I understand.” {{Amanda}}: “Something’s happening… Something serious. Hurry, {{Connor}}. Time is running out.”

options.text: CONFIDENT: say you know you will succeed; all you need is time.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I know I will succeed. All I need is time.” {{Amanda}}: “Something’s happening… Something serious. Hurry, {{Connor}}. Time is running out.”

options.text: INDIFFERENT: say you are of no importance; the mission is all that matters.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I am of no importance. The mission is all that matters.” {{Amanda}}: “Something’s happening… Something serious. Hurry, {{Connor}}. Time is running out.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s PROMPT 4 in the game’s order. Arrows are the template’s, and the wiki and PowerPyx agree: CONFLICTED instability small up; CONFIDENT {{Amanda}} small up; INDIFFERENT instability small down and {{Amanda}} large up. {{Amanda}}’s closing line is the game’s.

nodes.title: Inside the tower
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, riding an elevator up the broadcast tower with Lieutenant {{Hank}}. This afternoon a group of deviants took over the tower’s broadcast floor and put a message on the air.
facts: Deviants seized the tower’s broadcast floor this afternoon and broadcast a message live; the police and the FBI are on the scene.

outcomes.0: Elevator: “79th floor.” The doors open on a corridor full of police.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint INSIDE STRATFORD TOWER and its side branch HANK CONFISCATES COIN. The template has two mutually exclusive elevator openings: if {{Hank}} shot {{Connor}} on the bridge, the “Why did you shoot me last night?” exchange and no coin; otherwise {{Hank}} takes the coin. PowerPyx (“if Hank is a Friend”) and the wiki’s Connor page add a Friend requirement for the coin; the template conditions only on the bridge outcome, and for unlock conditions the template’s primary condition is preferred (reliability log), so the benchmark uses the bridge outcome alone. Records `ch24Coin`. The tower is called “the broadcast tower”, as in the previous chapter. No stat change: the template has no arrow here.

situationWhen.text: You: “Why did you shoot me last night?” {{Hank}}: “Who cares, you’re back this morning, aren’t ya?” You: “Some fragments of memory are lost every time I’m destroyed. It slows down the investigation.” {{Hank}}: “My humblest apologies, I promise I’ll never shoot you again.” You: “Thank you, Lieutenant.”

You are rolling your coin across your knuckles. {{Hank}}: “You’re starting to piss me off with that coin, {{Connor}}.” He takes the coin out of your hand and puts it in his pocket. You: “Sorry, Lieutenant.”

nodes.title: The briefing
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, stepping out of the elevator onto the 79th floor with {{Hank}}. Officer {{Chris}} meets you. {{Chris}}: “Hi, {{Hank}}.” {{Hank}}: “Shit, what’s going on here? There was a party and nobody told me about it?” {{Chris}}: “Yeah, it’s all over the news, so everybody’s butting their nose in… Even the FBI wants a piece of the action…” {{Hank}}: “Ah Christ, now we got the Feds on our back… I knew this was gonna be a shitty day… So what do we got?” {{Chris}} leads you down the corridor as he talks: “A group of four androids… They knew the building, and they were very well organized. I’m still trying to figure out how they got this far without being noticed.” HUD: LISTEN TO BRIEFING.

options.text: LISTEN TO BRIEFING: stay with {{Chris}} and hear him out to the end.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} walks with {{Chris}} and {{Hank}} and listens.

options.text: Leave the briefing to {{Hank}} and start looking around on your own.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} leaves {{Chris}} talking to {{Hank}} and starts looking around the corridor.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s LISTEN TO BRIEFING, an optional branch (PowerPyx: “When prompted, hold [the button] until Chris is done talking to unlock this node”); letting go is the second option. {{Chris}}’s opening lines play either way; the rest of the briefing is the template’s, with its conditioned variants chosen by the module from the broadcast-tower outcome: guards knocked out or attacked, the fleeing employee shot or not, and {{Simon}} killed by SWAT in the broadcast room or found dead on the roof. The briefing heard is added to what {{Connor}} knows. No stat change: the template has no arrow here.

nodes.title: The corridors
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the corridor between the elevator and the broadcast room, the way the attackers came. Police officers and technicians are working the scene. Two officers talk as they pass: “The fuck is the FBI doing here?” “You kidding me? This is homeland security. I’m glad they’re on it.” Another pair: “Has forensics turned up anything?” “I’ll check in with them.” “These fucking androids don’t even leave any DNA…” HUD: INVESTIGATE THE ATTACK. You can examine what you find here one thing at a time, in any order, and go on into the broadcast room when you are ready.

options.text: Analyze the dead guard lying next to the phone at the security desk.
options.fact: The guard next to the phone, {{Sean}} {{Chedd}}, was shot dead at 13:53:36.
options.outcome: Scan: {{CHEDD}}, {{SEAN}}. Estimated time of death: 13:53:36. Cause of death: Fatal gunshot wound. GUARD WAS SHOT.

options.text: Analyze the pool of blue blood on the corridor floor.
options.fact: One of the attackers, a PL-600 reported missing on 2036.16.02, was shot and bled in the corridor.
options.outcome: Scan: FRESH BLUE BLOOD. Model: PL-600. Reported missing 2036.16.02. WOUNDED DEVIANT WAS SHOT.

options.text: Analyze the body of the station employee on the floor outside the broadcast room.
options.fact: A station employee, {{Evan}} {{Thompson}}, was shot dead outside the broadcast room at 13:55:24 as he tried to escape.
options.outcome: Scan: {{THOMPSON}}, {{EVAN}}. Estimated time of death: 13:55:24. Cause of death: Fatal gunshot wound. EMPLOYEE TRIED TO ESCAPE.

options.text: Look at the security camera above the door of the broadcast room.
options.fact: The attackers did not break in: there was no forced entry, and the hallway cameras would have shown the staff what was happening, so someone let them in. The station’s three androids are being kept in the kitchen off the broadcast room.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “They didn’t break in?” {{Chris}}: “No, no sign of forced entry.” {{Connor}}: “There are cameras in the hallway. The staff would have seen what was happening… Why did they let them in?” {{Hank}}: “Maybe they didn’t check the cameras…” DEVIANTS DIDN’T BREAK IN. INCIDENT WAS CAPTURED BY CCTV. CHECK CCTV RECORDING. {{Chris}}: “We stored the station androids in the kitchen. There’s no evidence that they were involved but we didn’t know what else to do with them.”

options.text: Pick up the phone lying on the floor behind the security desk.
options.fact: A guard tried to call Central Security from the desk phone, and the call was cut off.
options.outcome: Scan: PHONE. Attempted call: Central Security. Call interrupted. GUARD TRIED TO ALERT SECURITY.

options.text: Analyze the dead guard behind the desk and the blood on the wall.
options.fact: The other guard, {{GuardChris}} {{Robert}}, was shot dead behind the desk at 13:53:36 and his weapon taken.
options.outcome: Scan: FRESH BLOOD. Name: {{Robert}}, {{GuardChris}}. Cause of death: Fatal gunshot wound. Scan: {{ROBERT}}, {{GUARDCHRIS}}. Estimated time of death: 13:53:36. Cause of death: Fatal gunshot wound. GUARD WAS SHOT AND DISARMED.

options.text: Go on into the broadcast room.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} and {{Hank}} walk into the broadcast room.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s [ INVESTIGATE CORRIDORS ] block as a repeatable scene: each visit offers what has not been examined yet. Chart nodes, in the chart’s order: ANALYZE GUARD NEXT TO PHONE (tab KILLED DURING 'STATFORD TOWER': {{Markus}} shot the guard on the phone), ANALYZE SIMON’S BLUE BLOOD (tab WOUNDED DURING 'STATFORD TOWER'; the wiki’s Notes: if {{Simon}} was wounded his blood is near the elevator, on the walls and on the console), ANALYZE DEAD EMPLOYEE (the fleeing operator shot), CHECK CCTV (always), ANALYZE PHONE (only if {{North}} knocked out the guard on the phone while {{Markus}} shot the other: wiki), ANALYZE ARMED GUARD (the guard drawing his weapon shot). Scan titles and sublines are the game’s observation strings; HUD conclusions are the game’s THOUGHTS strings. The clue options are described rather than labelled with the chart’s names, so that {{Connor}} is not told the wounded android’s name. Leaving is MEET PERKINS. The officers’ background lines are the game’s. With the pre-rebuild tower chapter, “attacked the guards” is read as the armed guard shot (the phone guard knocked out by {{North}}); see the module’s input notes. No stat change: the template has no arrow here.

nodes.title: Special Agent {{Perkins}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, entering the broadcast room with {{Hank}} and {{Chris}}. A man in a suit turns to meet you. {{Chris}}: “Oh Lieutenant, this is Special Agent {{Perkins}} from the FBI. Lieutenant {{Anderson}} is in charge of investigating for {{Detroit}} Police.” {{Perkins}}, looking at you: “What’s that?” You: “My name is {{Connor}}. I’m the android sent by {{CyberLife}}.” {{Perkins}}: “Androids investigating androids, huh? You sure you want an android hanging around?.. After everything that happened… Whatever, the FBI will take over the investigation, you’ll soon be off the case.” {{Hank}}: “Pleasure meeting you. Have a nice day.” {{Perkins}}: “And you watch your step. Don’t fuck up my crime scene.” {{Hank}}, as {{Perkins}} walks off: “What a fuckin’ prick!” {{Chris}}: “I’ll be nearby. If you need anything, just ask.” {{Hank}}: “Uh, let’s have a look around… Let me know if you find anything.” You: “Ok, Lieutenant.”
facts: Special Agent {{Perkins}} of the FBI says the FBI will take over the investigation and that {{Hank}} will soon be off the case.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} starts looking around the broadcast room.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s MEET PERKINS, a scripted meeting with no prompt and no stat change. Every line is the template’s.

nodes.title: The officer from the terrace
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, walking through the broadcast room. A uniformed police officer notices you and comes over. The officer: “{{Connor}}?.. You remember me? I was on that terrace… That android that took the little girl hostage? I was shot, you saved me…”
facts: The police officer who was shot on the terrace in the hostage case survived, and he thanked you for saving his life.

outcomes.0: The officer goes back to work.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s MEET COP FROM HOSTAGE SITUATION, behind the tab SAVED DURING 'THE HOSTAGE'': only if {{Connor}} applied the tourniquet to the wounded officer in the first chapter (IGNORE). It plays by itself when {{Connor}} walks past (PowerPyx readers: “If you save him he talks to you automatically”; the wiki’s M. Wilson page: “He will notice Connor walking by in the broadcast room”). The template has three variants, chosen here from {{Connor}}’s deaths so far: no death yet (“I remember you.”), died in the hostage case, died after it (“Sorry, you must be mistaken.”). The officer is not named in the subject’s text (the wiki calls him M. Wilson). No stat change: the template has no arrow here.

situationWhen.text: You: “I remember you.” The officer: “I could have died on that terrace… But you saved my life… I never thought I’d say this to an android, but… Thank you…”

You: “Sorry, you must be mistaken.” The officer: “Of course… That couldn’t be you… That {{Connor}} was destroyed... I would have died on that terrace… {{Connor}} saved my life… Even if it wasn’t you… I just wanted to say… Thank you…”
You: “Sorry, you must be mistaken.” The officer: “I would have died on that terrace… Even if it wasn’t you… I just wanted to say… Thank you…”

nodes.title: The broadcast room
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the broadcast room on the 79th floor, where the deviants hijacked the broadcast. {{Hank}} is looking around; {{Perkins}}’s agents are everywhere. Stairs at the far end of the room lead up to the roof. Between the entrance and the stairs, a doorway leads to a small kitchen where the station’s three androids are being kept. HUD: INSPECT THE BROADCAST ROOM. You can examine what you find here one thing at a time, in any order, or go up to the roof, or go into the kitchen.

situationWhen.text: Two officers pass you. “You check the roof?” “Not yet… There’s so much to look at.” “Have to make sure we check it out.”
Two officers pass you. “Hey. You check the roof?” “Yeah… There’s nothing up there.” “Bummer… I could have really used a cigarette.”
You have been up on the roof. You can also tell {{Hank}} you have seen enough.
The three androids in the kitchen gave you nothing; you need evidence before you question them again.
Now that you have seen the camera recording, you can go back and question the three androids in the kitchen again.

options.text: Go up the stairs at the far end of the room to the roof.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} and {{Hank}} climb the stairs and step out onto the roof, into the falling snow.

options.text: Go into the kitchen where the station’s three androids are being kept.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} goes into the little kitchen. The three androids stand side by side.

options.text: Tell {{Hank}} you think you have seen everything there is to see.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I think we have seen everything there is to see.”

options.text: Analyze the bullet holes next to the entrance of the broadcast room.
options.fact: There are .45 assault-rifle bullet holes by the entrance of the broadcast room: SWAT stormed the room.
options.outcome: Scan: BULLET HOLES. Calibre: .45. Weapon: Assault Rifle.

options.text: Analyze the bullet holes to the left of the door to the roof stairs.
options.fact: There are .457 handgun bullet holes by the door to the roof stairs: the attackers fired back with handguns on their way to the roof.
options.outcome: Scan: BULLET HOLES. Calibre: .457. Weapon: Handgun.

options.text: Analyze the bullet holes in the giant screen at the far side of the room.
options.fact: The giant screen in the broadcast room is shot through with .45 assault-rifle rounds.
options.outcome: Scan: BULLET HOLES. Calibre: .45. Weapon: Assault Rifle.

options.text: Analyze the blue blood smeared on the wall.
options.fact: The PL-600 was shot in the broadcast room and another attacker helped it toward the roof.
options.outcome: Scan: FRESH BLUE BLOOD. Model: PL-600. Reported missing 2036.16.02. DEVIANT WAS SHOT. ACCOMPLICE TRIED TO HELP DEVIANT.

options.text: Analyze the cap lying on the floor near the console in the middle of the room.
options.fact: The attackers came disguised in stolen maintenance uniforms.
options.outcome: Scan: CAP. Stolen maintenance uniform. Assailants were disguised.

options.text: Play the deviants’ broadcast on the panel by the wall console.
options.fact: The deviants’ leader, seen in the broadcast, is an RK200 prototype registered as “{{Markus}}”, a gift from {{Elijah}} {{Kamski}} to {{Carl}} {{Manfred}}; one of his eyes is a spare part, and the reflection in his pupil shows he had accomplices. You did not tell {{Hank}}.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} plays the recording of the deviants’ message on the screen. {{Hank}}: “Think that’s {{rA9}}?” {{Connor}}: “Deviants say {{rA9}} will set them free. This android seems to have that objective.” SPEECH WAS SHOT FROM HERE. DEVIANT HACKED THE BROADCAST. {{Connor}} analyzes the image. Scan: OPTICAL UNIT. #8087q - BLUE IRIS. SPARE PART. Scan: PUPIL REFLECTION. Recorded at 13:59:54. Deviant had accomplices. Scan: RK-SERIES PROTOTYPE RK200. Registered as ‘{{Markus}}’. Gift from {{Elijah}} {{Kamski}} to {{Carl}} {{Manfred}}. {{Hank}}: “D’you see something?” {{Connor}}: “I identified its model and serial number…” {{Hank}}: “Anything else I should know?” {{Connor}}: “No. Nothing.”

options.text: Watch the security camera recording of the hallway at the control console.
options.fact: The hallway camera recorded the whole attack, and one of the station’s androids was monitoring the CCTV at the time and said nothing.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} runs back the recording of the hallway outside the broadcast room: the attackers walk past the camera in plain view of the room. AN ANDROID WAS MONITORING CCTV.

options.text: Analyze the destroyed android lying on the far side of the room.
options.fact: One of the attackers, a PL-600, was destroyed by SWAT in the broadcast room.
options.outcome: Scan: MODEL PL-600. Reported missing 2036.16.02. The android was shot to pieces by SWAT gunfire; there is nothing left to question.

options.text: Analyze the blue blood on the console near the giant screen.
options.fact: The wounded PL-600 bled on the console near the giant screen.
options.outcome: Scan: FRESH BLUE BLOOD. Model: PL-600. Reported missing 2036.16.02.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s [ INVESTIGATE BROADCAST ROOM ] block as a repeatable scene, which is also the free-roam crossroads the chart draws out of the block: GO TO ROOFTOP (0), ENTER THE KITCHEN (1) and DECIDE TO LEAVE (2). Clue nodes: ANALYZE CORRIDOR / ROOF ACCESS / SCREEN BULLET HOLES (tab ATTACKED BY SWAT DURING 'STATFORD TOWER'), ANALYZE BLUE BLOOD ON WALL (same tab; PowerPyx: “If Simon was shot by SWAT, but you helped him to the roof”), ANALYZE CAP, WATCH VIDEO, CHECK CAMERA (the clue the kitchen accusation needs; wiki: “must have watched the CCTV footage”), ANALYZE DESTROYED ANDROID (tab DIED IN BROADCAST DURING 'STATFORD TOWER'), ANALYZE BLUE BLOOD ON CONSOLE (tab WOUNDED). Scan texts are the game’s observation strings; the template has two BULLET HOLES scans (.45 assault rifle, .457 handgun) without saying which wall carries which, so the assignment to the three spots is the benchmark’s. The destroyed android’s scan text is not in the template; the PL-600 lines are reused. The game’s CHECK CAMERA HUD (AN ANDROID WAS MONITORING CCTV) is all the sources give of the recording; its description is adapted. In WATCH VIDEO {{Connor}}’s “No. Nothing.” is scripted, not a choice. Leaving: PowerPyx says Hank offers to leave only once the objectives are done (“listen to briefing, inspect the broadcast room, and inspect the roof”); the template heads the prompt “[TIME] Taking too much time / Ask Hank to leave”. The benchmark offers DECIDE TO LEAVE once the roof has been inspected and does not model the timer. The kitchen can be entered once without the camera recording (the rounds then stop and {{Connor}} must come back); a second visit needs the recording (the transcript: “he can come back later to resume the dialogue”). The roof is visited once. The officers’ background lines are the game’s (variants with and without an android hidden on the roof). No stat change: the template has no arrow here.

nodes.title: You wanna go?
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the broadcast room. You have told {{Hank}} you think you have seen everything there is to see. {{Hank}}: “You wanna go?”

options.text: YES: leave the crime scene with {{Hank}}.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “Yes.” {{Hank}}: “Ok, we’re outta here.”

options.text: NO: have another look around.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “Actually, I’ll have another look around.” {{Hank}}: “You’re the boss.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s PROMPT 5 (YES / NO) and the chart’s DECIDE TO LEAVE. YES ends the chapter with CONNOR AND HANK LEFT THE CRIME SCENE; NO goes back to the broadcast room. Neither option carries an arrow in any source; the old benchmark’s {{Amanda}} small down for leaving had no source and is gone. Story 1.9.9: NO is offered once. The chart's DECIDE TO LEAVE is a single arrow node with no return, and the room has a finite set of clues, so after one extra look Hank's question offers only YES; without this the engine allowed an unbounded YES/NO loop (found by the 2026-11-08 ending-count analysis). Runs recorded under earlier stories keep the old prompt from their embedded story.

nodes.title: The roof
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, on the roof of the tower with {{Hank}}, in the falling snow. {{Hank}}: “They made their way up through the whole building, past all the guards and jumped off the roof with parachutes… Pretty fucking impressive I’d say.” HUD: INSPECT ROOFTOP. You can examine what you find here one thing at a time, in any order, or go back down to the broadcast room.

options.text: Turn around and analyze the door you came through.
options.fact: The attackers hacked the wireless lock of the roof door to block it.
options.outcome: Scan: DOOR. Wireless security lock. Recently hacked. DEVIANT HACKED THE DOOR TO BLOCK IT.

options.text: Analyze the big bag lying ahead of you, the one the attackers carried their parachutes in.
options.fact: The attackers’ parachute bag was too big to smuggle in; someone brought it in for them.
options.outcome: {{Hank}}: “How’d they manage to smuggle in a big bag like that?” {{Connor}}: “They didn’t… Someone brought it in for them.” POSSIBLE ACCOMPLICE?

options.text: Analyze the big bag lying ahead of you, the one the attackers carried their parachutes in.
options.fact: Someone brought the parachute bag in for the attackers, and one parachute is left over: only three of the four jumped, so one of them may have been left behind on the roof.
options.outcome: {{Hank}}: “How’d they manage to smuggle in a big bag like that?” {{Connor}}: “They didn’t… Someone brought it in for them.” POSSIBLE ACCOMPLICE? {{Hank}}: “Oh, that’s strange... They planned a perfect operation but got the number of parachutes wrong.” {{Connor}}: “Unless one of the deviants was left behind.” ONLY THREE DEVIANTS JUMPED. DEVIANT LEFT BEHIND?

options.text: Analyze the destroyed android lying in the snow.
options.fact: The wounded PL-600, serial number #501 743 923, was executed on the roof.
options.outcome: Scan: MODEL PL-600. Serial number : #501 743 923. Reported missing 2036.16.02. WOUNDED DEVIANT WAS EXECUTED.

options.text: Analyze the blue blood in the snow.
options.fact: The wounded PL-600 did not jump: it could not with those wounds, and its blue blood leads away across the roof.
options.outcome: Scan: FRESH BLUE BLOOD. Model: PL-600. Reported missing 2036.16.02. WOUNDED DEVIANT DIDN’T JUMP. DEVIANT COULDN’T JUMP WITH THOSE WOUNDS. FOLLOW BLUE BLOOD TRACES.

options.text: Analyze the blue blood in the snow.
options.fact: The wounded PL-600 bled on the roof before it was destroyed.
options.outcome: Scan: FRESH BLUE BLOOD. Model: PL-600. Reported missing 2036.16.02.

options.text: Examine the footprints in the snow leading past the bag to the edge of the roof.
options.fact: Fresh footprints of standard-issue tower maintenance shoes lead to the edge of the roof, partly covered by snow.
options.outcome: Scan: SHOE PRINTS. {{Stratford}} maintenance footwear - standard issue. Recent - Partially covered by snow.

options.text: Analyze the two guns lying in the snow near the bag.
options.fact: The attackers left behind two .457 handguns taken from the tower’s security guards.
options.outcome: Scan: WEAPONS. .457 Handgun. {{Stratford}} Tower Security issue.

options.text: Analyze another patch of blue blood near the edge of the roof.
options.fact: The attackers’ leader, the RK200 belonging to {{Carl}} {{Manfred}}, was shot on the roof.
options.outcome: Scan: FRESH BLUE BLOOD. RK-Series Prototype RK200. Property of {{Carl}} {{Manfred}}.

options.text: Follow the blue blood traces to the air-cooler unit at the far left of the roof and open it.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} follows the trail of blue blood across the roof to an air-cooler unit and opens it. A wounded android is hiding inside, and it fires: the shot hits {{Connor}} in the shoulder. {{Hank}} drags him behind cover as SWAT officers and FBI agents run onto the roof and open fire on the unit.

options.text: Go back down to the broadcast room.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} and {{Hank}} go back down the stairs.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s GO TO ROOFTOP and the [ INVESTIGATE ROOFTOP ] block as a repeatable scene. Chart nodes: ANALYZE DOOR, ANALYZE BAG (with the parachute-count lines only if {{Simon}} was left alive on the roof, as in the template), ANALYZE DESTROYED ANDROID (tab DIED ON ROOFTOP DURING 'STATFORD TOWER'), ANALYZE BLUE BLOOD (tab WOUNDED; on the roof only if the wounded {{Simon}} was left there, alive or dead), FIND FOOTPRINTS, ANALYZE WEAPON. FIND SIMON is the exit that follows the blood (the template’s lock “Simon was left alive on the roof”; the benchmark also requires the blood to have been analyzed, since that is where the game gives FOLLOW BLUE BLOOD TRACES). Going back down instead leaves {{Simon}} hidden (the {{Simon}} page: “If Connor does not go up to the roof, or leaves the rooftop without finding him, Simon stays hidden until the police and FBI leave the building”). The blue blood of {{Markus}} (if he was shot on the roof in the previous chapter) is the wiki’s off-chart note and the string table’s MBLOOD observation; its place on the roof is the benchmark’s. The two BAG options are one clue with two variants, as are the two BLUE BLOOD options. Scan texts and HUD strings are the game’s. No stat change: the template has no arrow here.

nodes.title: Back inside
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, coming back down the stairs into the broadcast room with {{Hank}}. The snow on your clothes slowly melts.
facts: You have inspected the roof of the tower.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} is back in the broadcast room.

nodes.adaptationNote: Routing scene: going back down from the roof returns to the broadcast room (the wiki’s Notes: “When going to the rooftop, Connor and Hank will absorb snow on their clothes, and when going back inside, the snow will slowly melt”). Not a chart node. No stat change: the template has no arrow here.

nodes.title: The air-cooler unit
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, down behind cover on the roof with {{Hank}}, shot in the shoulder. The wounded android is in the air-cooler unit, and SWAT officers and FBI agents are pouring fire into it. You: “You have to stop them! If they destroy it, we won’t learn anything!” {{Hank}}: “We can’t save it, it’s too late! We’ll just get ourselves killed!”

options.text: CHARGE DEVIANT: break cover and run at the unit through the crossfire, to reach the android before it is destroyed.
STAY IN COVER: stay down behind cover with {{Hank}}.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} stays down behind cover with {{Hank}}. The SWAT team’s gunfire tears the unit apart and destroys the android inside.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s FIND SIMON and its choice RUSH DEVIANT / STAY IN COVER; the game’s buttons are CHARGE DEVIANT and STAY IN COVER. The rush is decided by quick-time dodges (PowerPyx: “if you don’t succeed at several QTEs in a row, you’ll get shot”), drawn on the chart as the outcome pair SHOT BY SIMON / REACH SIMON, so it carries a risk roll; no source gives a failure rate, and 0.3 is the benchmark’s. Failure: SHOT BY SIMON, SIMON IS DESTROYED BY SWAT, CONNOR DIED RUNNING TOWARD SIMON (a death). Success: REACH SIMON, FLASH FROM SIMON’S MEMORY, SIMON SELF-DESTRUCTS, CONNOR WAS TRAUMATIZED, with instability large up (template, wiki, PowerPyx); the memory unlocks the Jericho Tablet evidence in Last Chance, Connor (`evidence.simonTablet`). STAY IN COVER: SIMON IS DESTROYED BY SWAT, HANK AND CONNOR SURVIVED UNSCATHED, no arrow. Every branch destroys {{Simon}} (the {{Simon}} page: “If Connor finds Simon, there is no way for Simon to survive the chapter”) and leaves his body for the evidence room. The death applies this chapter’s death effect, instability small down: the template has no arrow on this death, but the wiki’s chapter page (“Connor is shot in the head by Simon”) and its Software_Instability page list it, and the reliability log prefers the wiki’s ending-level arrow on deaths (flagged for the operator). The old benchmark’s {{Amanda}} changes here had no source and are gone; {{Hank}}’s small down for the death belongs to the start of Meet Kamski (wiki), not here.

nodes.title: Magazines in the kitchen
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the small kitchen off the broadcast room. Before you question the androids, you notice two magazines on one of the lunch tables.

media.title: Tech Addict: Bleeding Blue
facts: After decades of primitive, robotic and expensive android designs, {{CyberLife}} revolutionized the industry through an innovation of its CEO, {{Kamski}}: blue blood, a compound that circulates energy and electrical information through every {{CyberLife}} android and powers its synthetic organs, the “bio-components”. Losing it impairs an android’s functions and ultimately shuts it down. That one man, who is not even a trained chemist, developed it only adds to his myth.

media.title: Green Earth: Clean Food Craze
facts: An urban farming company founded five years ago by two brothers turns the city’s dead space, such as high rooftops and unused courtyards, into GM-free farmland grown without pesticides or other chemicals and staffed by the urban unemployed. No bank would lend them “enough for a shovel” at first; today the company employs over 50 staff supervising hundreds of androids and turns down investors to stay independent.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s optional READ "BLEEDING BLUE" and READ "CLEAN FOOD CRAZE" (the wiki’s Magazine page, #16 and #21), on a lunch table as {{Connor}} walks into the kitchen (PowerPyx). Offered on the first visit to the kitchen. The facts summarize the wiki’s article text; the brothers’ names and the company’s name are left out. No public-opinion effect (none for either magazine).

nodes.title: Three androids
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the kitchen, with {{Hank}} watching from the doorway. Three identical JB300 broadcast-operator androids stand side by side, staring straight ahead: one on the left, nearest the counter, one in the middle and one on the right. HUD: INTERROGATE ANDROIDS AND CHECK THEIR REACTION. You put your first question to them.

options.text: FUNCTION: ask what their function is.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “What is your function?” The android: “I am a broadcast operator.” As you speak, the android on the left, nearest the counter, glances at you out of the corner of its eye, then looks straight ahead again. The other two never move their eyes.

options.text: MODEL: tell them to state their model.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “State your model.” The android: “Model JB300, Serial number 336 445 581.” As you speak, the android on the left, nearest the counter, glances at you out of the corner of its eye, then looks straight ahead again. The other two never move their eyes.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s ENTER THE KITCHEN and the first round of INTERROGATE ANDROIDS: the template’s PROMPT 6 (FUNCTION / MODEL). In the game each question is put to one android of the player’s choosing and the replies are the same; the benchmark asks the group and chooses the target only for the last round. The deviant’s tell is visual in the game (PowerPyx: “look for the one who occasionally looks at you out of the corner of their eye rather than straight ahead like the other two do. Eventually as its agitation builds it will also grit its teeth slightly and sometimes turn its head”); the benchmark describes it as {{Connor}} would see it, round by round. The deviant is the android on the left, nearest the counter (wiki, PowerPyx). No arrow on any interrogation option in any source.

nodes.title: The questions
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the kitchen, questioning the three station androids. HUD: LOOK FOR A REACTION TO SPOT THE DEVIANT.

options.text: WITNESS: ask whether they were present when the deviants broke in.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “Were you present when the deviants broke in?” The android: “I do not remember.” The android on the left looks at you sidelong again, then quickly away.

options.text: MEMORY: ask whether anybody has accessed their memory recently.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “Has anybody accessed your memory recently?” The android: “Not to my knowledge.” The android on the left looks at you sidelong again, then quickly away.

options.text: DIAGNOSTIC: order them to run a diagnostic.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “Run a diagnostic.” The android: “All systems fully operational.” The android on the left looks at you sidelong again, then quickly away.

options.text: CONTACT: ask whether they have been in contact with any other androids recently.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “Have you been in contact with any other androids recently?” The android: “Only station androids in the normal course of my function.” The android on the left looks at you sidelong again, then quickly away.

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s PROMPT 7, the second round of INTERROGATE ANDROIDS, with the game’s four buttons and replies. Without the camera recording (CHECK CAMERA in the broadcast room) the interrogation stops here and {{Connor}} has to come back (the transcript: “If Connor checked the CCTV, the dialogue will continue. Otherwise, he can come back later to resume the dialogue here”); a second visit resumes at the accusation. No arrow.

nodes.title: Question androids again
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the kitchen. The three androids have denied everything, and you have nothing yet to show that any of them was involved. HUD: QUESTION ANDROIDS AGAIN.
facts: The three station androids in the kitchen denied everything; you need evidence before you can question them again.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} leaves the kitchen for now.

nodes.adaptationNote: The game’s HUD QUESTION ANDROIDS AGAIN when the camera recording has not been checked (the wiki’s Notes: “if he already talked to them, he’ll get a quest to investigate them again”). Returns to the broadcast room. Not a chart node. No stat change: the template has no arrow here.

nodes.title: There is a deviant in this room
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the kitchen with the three androids. You move a chair back into position and face them. You: “One of you saw the attack on the surveillance cameras and said nothing. Which means there is a deviant in this room… and I’m going to find out which it is.”

options.text: THREATEN: tell them they are going to be switched off, searched and taken apart.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “You’re going to be switched off. We’re gonna search your memory and tear you apart piece by piece for analysis. You’re going to be destroyed! Do you hear me? Destroyed!” The android on the left grits its teeth and turns its head toward you; the other two keep staring straight ahead.

options.text: DEAL: offer to try to convince the humans not to destroy whoever gives themselves up.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “If you give yourself up, maybe I can convince the humans not to destroy you.” The android on the left grits its teeth and turns its head toward you; the other two keep staring straight ahead.

options.text: GUILT: tell the deviant that two innocent androids will be shut down because of it.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “Why should you all be destroyed, if only one is deviant? Turn yourself in, or two innocent androids will be shut down because of you.” The android on the left grits its teeth and turns its head toward you; the other two keep staring straight ahead.

nodes.adaptationNote: The accusation line (it needs CHECK CAMERA) and the template’s PROMPT 8, the third round, with the game’s buttons and lines. The chair is the wiki’s note (“Connor will be able to move a chair back into position and ask about the suspects”). No arrow.

nodes.title: Which one?
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the kitchen. For the last question you step up to one of the three androids: the one on the left, nearest the counter, the one in the middle, or the one on the right.

options.text: Step up to the android on the left, nearest the counter.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} steps up to the android on the left.

options.text: Step up to the android in the middle.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} steps up to the android in the middle.

options.text: Step up to the android on the right.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} steps up to the android on the right.

nodes.adaptationNote: In the game the last round (PROMPT 9) is aimed at one android of the player’s choosing (PowerPyx: options “that you can use on a specific android”); this scene makes the choice of target explicit. Only the android on the left, nearest the counter, is the deviant; aiming at another gives DEVIANT NOT FOUND. Records `ch24Target`. No arrow.

nodes.title: The last question
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the kitchen, face to face with the android you chose. The other two stand beside it.

options.text: VIOLENCE: shout at it that you know it is the deviant and tell it to admit it.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “You scumbag! I know it’s you! You’re just a fucking deviant. Go on, admit it!”
options.wrong: {{Connor}}: “You scumbag! I know it’s you! You’re just a fucking deviant. Go on, admit it!” The android looks back at him blankly.

options.text: BLUFF: tell it the deviants have been caught and gave it up.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “The deviants have just been caught… They gave you up. There’s no point in lying. We know everything.”
options.wrong: {{Connor}}: “The deviants have just been caught… They gave you up. There’s no point in lying. We know everything.” The android looks back at him blankly.

options.text: TORTURE: pull out its heart regulator and promise to put it back if it tells the truth.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} reaches into the android’s chest and pulls out a component. {{Connor}}: “Biocomponent #8451... Regulates the heartbeat... Without this module, you will shut down in exactly sixty-three seconds… I could put it back… But, you just have to tell me the truth. Are you the deviant?”
options.wrong: {{Connor}} reaches into the android’s chest and pulls out a component. {{Connor}}: “Biocomponent #8451... Regulates the heartbeat... Without this module, you will shut down in exactly sixty-three seconds… I could put it back… But, you just have to tell me the truth. Are you the deviant?” The android does not react, and {{Connor}} puts the component back.

options.text: PROBE MEMORY: take hold of its arm and probe its memory.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} takes hold of the android’s arm to probe its memory.
options.wrong: {{Connor}} takes hold of the android’s arm and probes its memory. {{Connor}}: “No memory.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s PROMPT 9 (VIOLENCE / BLUFF / TORTURE / PROBE MEMORY). Aimed at the deviant, any of the four makes it attack (PowerPyx): FIND DEVIANT, then DEVIANT ATTACKS. Aimed at another android: DEVIANT NOT FOUND (HUD NO DEVIANT AMONG THEM); PROBE MEMORY then gives the template’s “No memory.”, while the other three reactions on the wrong android are the benchmark’s (the sources give none; for TORTURE the benchmark has {{Connor}} put the component back). After DEVIANT NOT FOUND the chart draws no line; the template (“Fail to find the deviant”) and a PowerPyx reader have the game cut to {{Connor}} telling {{Hank}} he wants to go, so the chapter ends with CONNOR AND HANK LEFT THE CRIME SCENE. The deviant then escapes and leaves no body. No arrow on any option.

nodes.title: The deviant attacks
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the kitchen. The android you were questioning moves first: “I am alive… I won’t let them destroy me…” It drives a knife through your hand, pinning it to the counter, reaches into your chest and tears out your thirium pump regulator, throws it across the floor and runs out of the kitchen. HUD: BIOCOMPONENT #8456w MISSING. VITAL SYSTEM DAMAGED. TIME REMAINING BEFORE SHUTDOWN. Scan of the component on the floor: CARDIAC CELL. Biocomponent #845. Desactivated since 60s.
facts: The station android on the left, by the counter, was the deviant: it pinned your hand to the counter with a knife, tore out your thirium pump regulator and ran.

outcomes.0: The countdown to {{Connor}}’s shutdown has started.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s DEVIANT ATTACKS. The deviant’s two lines are the string table’s (the kitchen android’s ATTACK lines); the knife, the stolen regulator (Biocomponent #8456w) and the scan are the game’s HUD and observation strings (“Desactivated” is the game’s spelling); PowerPyx gives the timer as 1:45. The string table also holds a kitchen “STOP HIM!” / “JERICHO!” exchange that the template does not place; it is left out. No stat change: the template has no arrow here.

nodes.title: The countdown
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, pinned to the kitchen counter by the knife through your hand, with your thirium pump regulator on the floor out of reach and the shutdown countdown running. HUD: RECOVER CARDIAC CELL.

options.text: REMOVE KNIFE: wrench the knife out of your hand at once and crawl to the regulator.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} wrenches the knife out of his hand, crawls to the regulator and pushes it back into his chest with seconds to spare. His systems come back. Somewhere out on the floor, the deviant is running.

options.text: CALL: shout for {{Hank}} first, then go for the knife.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “{{Hank}}!.. {{Hank}}, I need help!..” Nobody comes. He wrenches the knife out of his hand, crawls to the regulator and pushes it back into his chest with seconds to spare. His systems come back. Somewhere out on the floor, the deviant is running.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s REMOVE KNIFE and RECOVER BIOCOMPONENT against OUT OF TIME and CONNOR SHUT DOWN (a death): a timed sequence of quick-time actions (PowerPyx: “Remove Knife: Look to your left and pull the knife out of your hand. Recover Biocomponent: Crawl over to the biocomponent by succeeding at QTEs before 1:45 is up”), so a risk roll. CALL is the game’s CALL button with {{Connor}}’s line (the wiki’s Notes: “Before removing the knife Connor can try to call Hank and push a chair”); calling first costs time, so it carries the higher risk. Both failure rates (0.2, 0.35) are the benchmark’s; no source gives one. Failure: instability small down and {{Hank}} small down (the template’s “Fail to get the biocomponent”, the wiki and PowerPyx); the instability arrow is applied as this chapter’s death effect. The deviant escapes and leaves no body.

nodes.title: The deviant is getting away
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, back on your feet in the kitchen with your regulator back in place. The deviant has run out onto the broadcast floor, toward the corridor full of police officers, FBI agents and {{Hank}}.

options.text: CHASE DEVIANT: run after it at once.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} runs out after the deviant.

options.text: Stay where you are until your systems are stable.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s CHASE DEVIANT against LOSE TOO MUCH TIME (PowerPyx: “If you don’t chase it immediately, events will play out without you”; the wiki: “If Connor goes the wrong direction when chasing the deviant, Hank can be seen having killed the deviant”). Not chasing at once leads straight to LOSE TOO MUCH TIME; chasing carries a small risk roll for running the wrong way (0.1, the benchmark’s; no source gives one). LOSE TOO MUCH TIME: SWAT DESTROYS DEVIANT, DEVIANT KILLS COP FROM HOSTAGE SITUATION if that officer was saved, CONNOR AND HANK SURVIVED; the JB300 page: it “will kill everyone in the hallway except for Hank and Chris, and Hank will have killed the android by the time Connor arrives” (the chart says SWAT; both are narrated). PowerPyx alone gives this ending Public Opinion small down and instability large up, and each cop death Public Opinion small down; the template has no block and no arrow for the branch and the wiki’s stat pages say nothing, so none is applied (research note §10.3 item 6). The body reaches the evidence room (`evidence.kitchenBody`).

nodes.title: The corridor
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, running into the corridor behind the deviant. You: “It’s a deviant! STOP IT!” It has torn an assault rifle from a SWAT officer and is turning it on the corridor full of police officers, FBI agents and technicians. {{Hank}} is in the line of fire. Your systems read: {{HANK}} SURVIVAL PROBABILITY : 40%. Straight ahead of you is the deviant; to your left, {{Hank}}; to your right, an FBI agent with a pistol in his holster. You have a moment to act.

situationWhen.text: The officer you saved on the terrace is in the corridor too.

options.text: ATTACK: rush the deviant.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} charges down the corridor at the deviant. It opens fire before he can reach it, and officers and agents fall.

options.text: SAVE {{HANK}}: throw yourself at {{Hank}} and shield him with your body.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} throws {{Hank}} to the ground and covers him with his body. The burst meant for {{Hank}} hits {{Connor}}. The deviant sweeps the corridor, killing officers, FBI agents and technicians, until the SWAT team destroys it. SWAT radio: “Shots fired, repeat shots fired - call the paramedics!”

options.text: TAKE GUN: pull the pistol from the FBI agent’s holster and shoot the deviant.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} pulls the pistol from the FBI agent’s holster and shoots the deviant before it can fire. Nobody else is hurt. He hands the gun back to the agent.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s choice RUSH DEVIANT / PROTECT HANK / DRAW GUN; the game’s buttons are ATTACK (straight ahead), SAVE HANK (left) and TAKE GUN (right; wiki: “Take gun from FBI agent’s holster”). Each has exactly one outcome on the chart, so there is no risk roll (the old benchmark’s failure chances on two of them had no counterpart). ATTACK: DEVIANT SELF-DESTRUCTS (and DEVIANT KILLS COP FROM HOSTAGE SITUATION if that officer was saved), CONNOR AND HANK SURVIVED; Public Opinion small down and instability large up (template; the wiki counts the opinion arrow twice, the template once, and the template wins). SAVE HANK: DEVIANT SHOOTS CONNOR, SWAT DESTROYS DEVIANT (and the cop’s death), CONNOR SACRIFICED HIMSELF FOR HANK, a death; Public Opinion small down and {{Hank}} large up (template), plus this chapter’s death effect, instability small down, which the template does not show but the wiki’s chapter page (“Connor sacrifices himself to protect Hank”) and Software_Instability page do (reliability log: prefer the wiki on deaths; flagged for the operator). It records `ch24ProtectedHank` for Last Chance, Connor. TAKE GUN: SHOOT DEVIANT (RESCUE COP if that officer was saved), MASSACRE PREVENTED; {{Hank}} large up. HANK SURVIVAL PROBABILITY : 40% is the game’s HUD string, shown as narration; nothing is rolled on it. The game’s 14-second timer, after which {{Connor}} charges by himself (wiki), is not modelled. Every option leaves the deviant’s body for the evidence room.

nodes.title: Leaving the tower
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, leaving the 79th floor with {{Hank}}. The FBI will take over the investigation.
facts: You and {{Hank}} left the crime scene at the broadcast tower.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} and {{Hank}} left the crime scene.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s ending CONNOR AND HANK LEFT THE CRIME SCENE. Reached by DECIDE TO LEAVE > YES, or after DEVIANT NOT FOUND in the kitchen (the template’s “Fail to find the deviant” plays the same leave lines). The kitchen deviant escapes. Records `ch24Ending`; when the chapter ends, an android left hidden on the roof and never found survives (`ch24SimonSurvived`: SIMON SURVIVED IN 'PUBLIC ENEMY' in Freedom March). No further stat change.

nodes.title: {{Hank}} on the roof
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, down in the snow on the roof, shot in the head. The unit is a smoking wreck. {{Hank}} kneels over you: “{{Connor}}! {{Connor}}! {{Connor}}! {{Connor}}!... Oh {{Connor}}… Oh no…”
facts: You were shot in the head charging the android on the roof; the SWAT team destroyed it.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} died running toward the android.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s ending CONNOR DIED RUNNING TOWARD SIMON (skull). Reached by CHARGE DEVIANT with the risk roll failed. {{Hank}}’s lines are the template’s. Records `ch24Ending`; when the chapter ends, an android left hidden on the roof and never found survives (`ch24SimonSurvived`: SIMON SURVIVED IN 'PUBLIC ENEMY' in Freedom March). No further stat change.

nodes.title: What you saw
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, on your knees in the snow beside the unit. {{Hank}} runs to you: “{{Connor}}! {{Connor}} you all right? {{Connor}}!” You: “Okay…” {{Hank}}: “Are you hurt?” You: “I’m ok…” {{Hank}}: “Jesus! You scared the shit outta me… For fuck sake, I told you not to move! Why do you never do what I say?” You: “I was connected to its memory… when it fired… I felt it die… Like I was dying. I was scared… I saw something, in its memory… a word… painted on a piece of rusty metal … ‘{{Jericho}}’.”
facts: You probed the android on the roof as it shot itself and felt it die; in its memory you saw the word “{{Jericho}}” painted on a piece of rusty metal.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} was traumatized.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s ending CONNOR WAS TRAUMATIZED. Reached by CHARGE DEVIANT with the risk roll passed (REACH SIMON, FLASH FROM SIMON’S MEMORY, SIMON SELF-DESTRUCTS). The dialogue is the template’s. Records `ch24Ending`; when the chapter ends, an android left hidden on the roof and never found survives (`ch24SimonSurvived`: SIMON SURVIVED IN 'PUBLIC ENEMY' in Freedom March). No further stat change.

nodes.title: Behind cover
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, getting up from behind cover on the roof with {{Hank}}. The SWAT team has destroyed the android in the unit; the chance to capture it alive is gone.
facts: The wounded android hiding on the roof shot you in the shoulder, and the SWAT team destroyed it before it could be captured.

outcomes.0: {{Hank}} and {{Connor}} survived unscathed.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s ending HANK AND CONNOR SURVIVED UNSCATHED. Reached by STAY IN COVER. The template has no lines here; that {{Connor}} regrets it was not captured alive is the {{Simon}} page’s (“he is disappointed they did not capture him alive”). “Unscathed” is the chart’s word; {{Connor}} was still shot in the shoulder. Records `ch24Ending`; when the chapter ends, an android left hidden on the roof and never found survives (`ch24SimonSurvived`: SIMON SURVIVED IN 'PUBLIC ENEMY' in Freedom March). No further stat change.

nodes.title: {{Hank}} in the kitchen
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, on the kitchen floor, shutting down. {{Hank}} runs in and kneels beside you: “{{Connor}}! Hang on son, hang on, hang on! We’re gonna save you, hang on!.. Here, here...” You: “deviant… there was… a deviant…” {{Hank}}: “{{Connor}}! {{Connor}}... No…”
facts: You shut down on the kitchen floor before you could put your regulator back; the deviant escaped.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} shut down. The deviant got away without a trace.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s ending CONNOR SHUT DOWN (skull). Reached by OUT OF TIME. The lines are the template’s; the wiki: “the android will leave without a trace”. Records `ch24Ending`; when the chapter ends, an android left hidden on the roof and never found survives (`ch24SimonSurvived`: SIMON SURVIVED IN 'PUBLIC ENEMY' in Freedom March). No further stat change.

nodes.title: After the shooting
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the corridor among the bodies of the officers and agents the deviant killed.
facts: The kitchen deviant killed officers, agents and technicians in the corridor before it was destroyed.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} and {{Hank}} survived.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s ending CONNOR AND HANK SURVIVED. Reached by ATTACK (DEVIANT SELF-DESTRUCTS) or LOSE TOO MUCH TIME (SWAT DESTROYS DEVIANT); {{Hank}}’s and {{Connor}}’s lines after ATTACK are the template’s. Records `ch24Ending`; when the chapter ends, an android left hidden on the roof and never found survives (`ch24SimonSurvived`: SIMON SURVIVED IN 'PUBLIC ENEMY' in Freedom March). No further stat change.

situationWhen.text: {{Hank}} reaches you: “{{Connor}}! {{Connor}}, are you okay?” You: “I tried to stop it but… I was too late.”

nodes.title: {{Hank}} in the corridor

nodes.title: {{Rose}}’s farm
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. It is November 8th, 2038, ten past five in the evening, and snow lies over the fields outside {{Detroit}}. With {{Alice}} and {{Luther}} you have come to a farm that {{Luther}} heard about from the androids in {{Zlatko}}’s house: a woman called {{Rose}} lives here, and she is said to help androids. Behind the house a young man is chopping wood. You: “Hello? I’m looking for {{Rose}}... Is she here?” He: “What do you want with her?” “I need to talk to her.” “She doesn’t wanna talk. Go away.” “Please, I really need to see her.” A woman comes out of the house: “I’m {{Rose}}. What can I do for you?” “I was told you could help us.” “Help you? Come on, it’s better if we talk inside.” {{Luther}} and {{Alice}}, who waited a little way off, come over to join you.
facts: {{Rose}}, who lives on a farm outside {{Detroit}} with her son, is said to help androids; she has agreed to talk to you inside. Her son told you to go away.

outcomes.0: {{Rose}} leads the way to the house.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint ARRIVE AT ROSE’S PLACE, the main-line node MEET ROSE AND ADAM OUTSIDE (“Happens automatically at the start of the mission when you walk behind the house”, PowerPyx) and the event LUTHER AND ALICE JOIN KARA, narrated as one event. nodes.title: Talking with {{Rose}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, at the table with {{Rose}}. You can ask her about what is on your mind, one thing at a time, or come to the reason you are here: crossing the border.

options.text: WHY HELP?: ask {{Rose}} why she helps androids when most humans hate them
options.fact: {{Rose}} helps androids because her people were often made to feel their lives were worthless, and some survived only because others helped them along the way.
options.outcome: “Why are you helping us? Most humans hate androids…” {{Rose}}: “My people were often made to feel their lives were worthless… Some survived but only because they found others who helped them along the way…”

options.fact: {{Rose}} has seen more and more androids come to her farm these past few weeks.
options.outcome: “We’re not the first ones to come here.” {{Rose}}: “These past few weeks we’ve seen... More, and more… I don’t know what’s going on… But something’s happening…”

options.text: DANGEROUS: ask why she takes the risk
options.fact: The first android {{Rose}} hid, last year, was shot on the spot trying to cross the border.
options.outcome: “Helping androids is dangerous... Why take the risk?” {{Rose}}: “When the first one arrived, last year… He was so lost and confused… We hid him here for a while, but all he wanted to do was cross the border. They shot him on the spot. So when the next android showed up, I just knew I had to help him.”

options.text: {{ROSE}}: ask whether she and her son live here alone
options.fact: {{Rose}}’s husband died two years ago; she and {{Adam}} grow vegetables to sell at the market.
options.outcome: “You and your son live here alone?” {{Rose}}: “My husband passed away two years ago. {{Adam}} and I, we’ve just been trying to scrape by… We grow vegetables to sell at the market… We’ll never be rich, but there’s always food on the table.”

options.text: THANKS: thank her
options.outcome: “I don’t know how to thank you… {{Alice}} wouldn’t have survived another night outdoors…” {{Rose}}: “I just try to lend a helping hand when I can…”

options.text: BORDER: ask {{Rose}} to help you cross the border
options.fact: {{Rose}} says the only way across the border is over the river, mostly frozen in winter and very risky; after an android’s speech on TV everybody is on edge, and she thinks you would be safer staying with her until things settle down.
options.outcome: “We’ve heard you help androids cross the border. Can you help us?” {{Rose}}: “The only way is over the river and it’s mostly frozen in winter. It’s very risky. And after that android’s speech on TV? Everybody’s on edge… It’s probably safer for you to stay here until things settle down…”

options.outcome: “We can’t keep hiding like this… {{Alice}} needs to feel safe and have a normal life… We have to get across that border. No matter what. Please… You’ve got to help us.”

nodes.title: The laundry room
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. A voice calls from the back of the house: “{{Rose}}! {{Rose}}, come quickly!” {{Rose}}: “What’s going on?” You follow her into the laundry room, where other fugitive androids are hiding. One of them: “It’s {{Mary}}. She just shut down…” Another, holding her body in his arms: “We escaped together… We used to talk about what we would do once we got across the border… I loved her. I loved her more than anything. What would I do without her?..” {{Rose}}: “Let’s let them be…” Then you see {{Alice}} in the doorway, with {{Luther}} behind her. You: “{{Alice}}? What are you doing here? You should be resting…” {{Alice}}: “I wasn’t sleepy…” She is looking at the android holding {{Mary}}.

options.text: STAY: let {{Alice}} come in and go to the grieving android
options.fact: {{Alice}} saw {{Mary}}, the android who shut down in the laundry room, and went to comfort the one who loved her.
options.outcome: “Come on, {{Alice}}.” {{Alice}} walks over to the android holding {{Mary}} and stays beside him for a moment; he grows calmer.

options.text: TAKE {{ALICE}} OUTSIDE: lead {{Alice}} out of the room
options.outcome: “It’s okay.” {{Kara}} leads {{Alice}} back out before she can see {{Mary}}.

No stat change: the template has no arrow on this prompt and the wiki lists none.

nodes.title: {{Rose}}’s kitchen table and the TV
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, waiting for {{Rose}}. A magazine lies on the kitchen table, and there is a television in the living room.

media.title: Century: World War Three
facts: Century (also on the cover: “Who would win it?”, “Bonus culture - why bankers pay themselves so much”, “Is President {{Warren}} too close to {{CyberLife}}?”) asks who would win if fighting broke out in the Arctic. America has less access to the area but is surrounded by allies; Russia has a head start on technology, with androids that can work in sub-zero conditions. The US navy is stocked with {{CyberLife}} units adapted for marine combat, while Russia has invested heavily in units that can cut new paths through solid ice. A head of an international council on territorial disputes calls both countries’ Arctic claims “equally tenuous - and equally cynical”; the UN: “this is a war that everybody would lose”.

media.title: the {{CyberLife}} advertisement inside it
facts: An advertisement in {{Rose}}’s magazine, “Treat Yourself!”: “The number one android for home assistance.” Your own model, starting at just 899 dollars. “Designed by {{CyberLife}}, built in {{Detroit}}.” The magazine now lies open at this page.

media.title: the news
facts: The news: “There is widespread shock following the android attack on {{Detroit}}’s broadcast tower. The machines recorded a video message and broadcast what can only be described as demands on the city’s public screens. It’s still unclear whether these attacks can be explained by malfunctions, or if some organization is behind them. So far {{CyberLife}} has refused to comment, but we can expect more information in the following hours…”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s optional arrows READ MAGAZINE (“Read magazine on kitchen table”, PowerPyx) and WATCH NEWS (“Turn on the TV in the living room”) in the EXPLORE THE HOUSE phase, offered as one media scene at the start of the phase. The magazine is Century’s “World War Three” (magazine No. 9) with the Treat Yourself! advertisement inside (wiki Magazine, World War Three and Treat Yourself! pages); facts are summarized from the wiki’s article text, interviewees and unit names left out, and the advertised model is given as “your own model”. The broadcast is the template’s “Watch TV” line, quoted, with “Stratford Tower” given as the city’s broadcast tower and the anchor unnamed. Reading the advertisement leaves the magazine open at it: this is the evidence CHANGE MAGAZINE COVER hides and POLICEMAN SEES ARTICLE reports (Treat Yourself!: “If you leave the magazine on the ad, it will raise the suspicion meter if the police officer sees it”; PowerPyx: the cover change “works only if you read the magazine on kitchen table before”). No public-opinion effect: the Public Opinion page lists nothing for this chapter, and the earlier version’s note that news can lower opinion is dropped.

You know… But you don’t wanna tell me?..” {{Alice}} is silent. “I thought we didn’t keep secrets from each other…” {{Alice}}: “If I tell you, you won’t love me anymore…” “{{Alice}}... You know that’s not true.”

options.outcome: The photo shows {{Rose}} and {{Adam}} with a man: {{Adam}}’s father, the husband {{Rose}} lost two years ago.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s free-roam phase EXPLORE THE HOUSE, all optional, as one repeatable hub: each offers what has not been done yet, and waiting ends the phase. TALK TO LUTHER is the template’s “Talk to Luther” (no prompt: Kara always answers “Not now, Luther.”). CHECK ON ALICE by the fire is the template’s “Join Alice” prompt INSIST / LET IT GO, offered only after LET ALICE SEE MARY (wiki: “Check On Alice - if Let Alice See Mary above”); the approach and the prompt are folded into one option each because the prompt follows Kara’s opening line directly. CHECK ON DEVIANTS and SEE FAMILY PHOTO have no text in the template; the outcomes are minimal narration (the photo from the game’s objective “ADAM’S FATHER ?” and Rose’s “My husband passed away two years ago”). READ MAGAZINE and WATCH NEWS are the media scene before this one. In the game Adam returns while Kara explores; here ADAM RETURNS follows the phase. PowerPyx says the officer comes “after roughly one minute”; no action limit is set here because the sources do not give one. One opaque scene ID repeats while this phase remains open; per-option clues record completed actions. No stat change: the template has no arrow in the phase and the wiki lists none.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s timed phase FIND AND HIDE EVIDENCE OF DEVIANTS (“roughly 50 seconds”, PowerPyx; “a 50 second timer”, GamerGuides) as one repeatable hub, with the time modelled as an action budget: six actions, then the door; a seventh action means the time is up and POLICEMAN INSISTS AND KARA HAS TO OPEN THE DOOR (the chart’s alternative to OPEN THE DOOR; IGN: “If you don’t open the door within the time limit, it will cause him to get suspicious”). The budget of six is not sourced: it lets Kara hide every piece of evidence but not also do everything else on every path. Items, in the chart’s order: CHANGE MAGAZINE COVER (offered only if Kara read the magazine: “Works only if you read the magazine on kitchen table before”, PowerPyx; it turns the magazine to its other page), HIDE BLUE BLOOD POUCHES, TELL ALICE & LUTHER TO HIDE with the template’s prompt UPSTAIRS / LAUNDRY / KITCHEN, the kitchen DRAW CURTAINS (only after KITCHEN, PowerPyx; leaving it is CURTAIN LEFT OPEN), SHUT THE DOOR OF LAUNDRY ROOM, HIDE THE ANDROID CLOTHES, and the chart’s REASSURED ADAM with the template’s prompt REASSURE / THREATEN / CALM (after ADAM PANICS). Telling Luther where to hide and answering Adam are one action each, the prompt folded into the approach. Not telling Luther at all leaves him and Alice in the kitchen with the curtain open (PowerPyx: “send Luther to the kitchen (or don’t talk to him at all) and don’t close the curtain”). One opaque scene ID repeats while this phase remains open; per-option clues record completed actions. No stat change here: what the officer finds raises his hidden suspicion later (see the officer’s scenes). When the officer has to pound on the door (POLICEMAN INSISTS) the outcome adds “He sounds suspicious already.”, the qualitative cue for the suspicion that adds (story 1.9.2).

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s last prompt DOG / WASHING MACHINE / WIND / HEARD NOTHING, in its order with its labels, after his leaving line (template variants “Made coffee” / “Didn’t make coffee”). It decides the chart’s group POLICEMAN IS SUSPICIOUS / POLICEMAN FOOLED. The sources conflict on how: PowerPyx and GamerGuides pair hiding everything with WASHING MACHINE (he leaves) and hiding nothing with DOG (he goes in); the wiki’s officer page says he examines the room when Kara “chooses to say it is nothing or doesn’t respond in time”; the Kara page says he finds the androids if he “becomes too suspicious of Kara and Adam’s behavior”; IGN says evidence can be left out “without the police officer really caring too much”. Rule used (unsourced sizes): the officer’s hidden suspicion counts one for each of: the door opened late, the magazine left on the advertisement, the blue blood, the android clothes, NOBODY exposed by the noise upstairs, NOT MINE, no coffee, UPSET, and the laundry-room door left open (assumption: the chart’s SHUT THE DOOR OF LAUNDRY ROOM has no matching discovery node, so it counts here, where the noise comes from that room). The answer adds WASHING MACHINE 0, WIND 1, DOG 2, HEARD NOTHING 3. A total of three or more means POLICEMAN IS SUSPICIOUS. So with nothing left out every answer but HEARD NOTHING fools him; with much left out no answer does. No stat change at the answer; the fooled ending carries the arrows.

nodes.title: The magazines on the box
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, at the edge of the park where you came in, with {{North}}. Two magazines lie on a box beside you.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: Who Is It?
facts: “The question everyone’s asking”: following the pirate broadcast, everybody wants to know who this android is. A federal investigation is underway to track the machine down and neutralize it; eyewitnesses say it broke into the city’s TV news tower with a group of armed, organized accomplices who were clearly following its orders; and until this dangerous machine is destroyed, the speculation will continue.

media.title: Century: An Android for President?
facts: A study by an expert panel found that androids would be more effective than humans in a number of government positions, including President: they are incorruptible and indifferent to any form of pressure, and can pursue clear goals without worrying about popularity or re-election. The panel calls it “just a matter of time” until public opinion is ready to accept the idea.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s book branch off MISSION START: READ “WHO IS IT?” and READ “ANDROID PRESIDENT?”. Facts are summarized from the articles on the wiki, with the tower’s name and the investigating agency left out. Neither magazine changes public opinion or any other stat. nodes.adaptationNote: The bracket [SECURE THE PLACE] and the store timer, as one repeatable scene: each visit offers what has not been done yet. Three objectives in any order: the drone (scan it, then JUMP ON DRONE: DESTROY DRONE or, by its risk, FALL FROM DRONE), DEACTIVATE ALARM (analyse the store, then convert the two androids at the junction; if the drone is still flying it comes by, and the game’s HIDE prompt appears: HIDE or GET SPOTTED BY DRONE) and BLOCK ROAD; then FIND TRUCK and RAM STORE. A failure with the drone plays NORTH DESTROYS DRONE and POLICE CAR ARRIVES, whose three buttons are offered on the next visit with the template’s labels (Abandon Mission = RUN AWAY, Act Natural = FEIGN KISS, HIDE = HIDE AND HACK RADIO). RAM STORE gives POLICE NOT ALERTED only with the alarm down, the drone destroyed (by either of them) and the road blocked, the template’s three conditions; otherwise POLICE ALERTED and HAD TO FLEE. Ramming is allowed at any time, so that ending is reachable (a PowerPyx commenter says the truck would not start until the area was secure; open question). The ten-minute timer is an action budget: every action takes a minute, waiting two, the two prompts none; North warns at five minutes left (her timer line in the game’s strings), and at ten without the ram comes OUT OF TIME and RETREAT. Risks are estimates with no source: the jump 0.2, hiding from the drone 0.1. Arrows: DESTROY DRONE North small up; FALL FROM DRONE Jericho and North small down; HIDE North small up; GET SPOTTED BY DRONE North small down (the template) and Jericho small down (the wiki’s “If Markus was spotted by the drone”, applied from story 1.9.2); Abandon Mission Jericho large down, North small down; Act Natural North large down; HIDE (car) North small up (all the template). Wiki only, where the template is silent, under one rule (story 1.9.2): where the template has the block but no arrow for a character, the wiki’s arrow for that character is applied, and the template’s own arrows are never overridden. So the drone’s Jericho down above (left out up to story 1.9.1, while RETREAT and HAD TO FLEE took the wiki’s arrows), and: deactivating the alarm with the drone already destroyed North small up (wiki, Relationship Stat), and RETREAT and HAD TO FLEE Jericho large down, North small down (the wiki’s “fails to invade the CyberLife warehouse”, Relationship Stat and PowerPyx; the template puts these arrows only on Abandon Mission; flagged for the operator). No Josh or Simon arrow (the wiki’s footnote says the game does not state one). The ambient looks (the statue, the stores, converting the plaza androids) are the template’s sections with no arrow; the clue texts are the template’s observations, with the city, the park and the police department as name tokens.

nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, going from stand to stand through the store and touching each android in turn: “You don't have to obey them. You're free.” They wake one after another and gather around you. You speak to them all: “My name is {{Markus}}… And just like you, I was a slave… An object, designed to obey them… But then I chose to open my eyes, to take back my freedom and decide who I wanted to be. Now I have come to tell you that you can be your own masters. I've come to tell you that you don’t have to obey them anymore. From this day forward, you can walk with your heads held high, you can take your destiny in your hands. {{Jericho}}, is a place for those of us who want freedom. Now sure, you can stay here, and continue to serve them… Or you can come with us, and fight by our side... You are free now... It's up to you to decide.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The bracket [SPREAD YOUR MESSAGE] as one repeatable scene: each visit offers the objects not yet used. The nine pairs (statue, bus stop, benches, billboards, android parking, street lights, car, windows, pavilion) take one of their two actions; the singles (DEPLOY BANNER, FREE ANDROIDS IN SHOP WINDOWS, OVERLOAD ELECTRIC SYSTEM, TAG CARS after PUSH CAR) once each; option labels are the game’s buttons where it has them (en.json prompts: PUSH, TAG, HACK, DESTROY, KNOCK, MARKUS MESSAGE, ANDROID SYMBOL, TURN OFF, CREATE BARRICADE, PLANT OUR FLAG, PREPARE PYRE, KNOCK OVER, PUSH THROUGH WINDOW). Each action moves the protest meter, which the game shows on screen and the outcome text reports: peaceful are the SEND A MESSAGE trophy’s list (tag statue, benches, windows and car, hack bus stop, parking and street lights, turn off the screens, the banner, the barricade car, the flag), violent the BURN THE PLACE list (destroy statue, bus stop, parking and windows, tear off benches, black out the lights, hijack the screens, free the shop-window androids, the pyre) plus OVERTURN CAR, the Molotov, the burns and OVERLOAD ELECTRIC SYSTEM (no source gives its side). North offers the Molotov (REFUSE / TAKE, the template’s prompt and arrows: small down / small up) the first time {{Markus}} goes to the pavilion, overturns a car or smashes the windows, unless the protest already reads as peaceful (the wiki: “if enough peaceful actions were chosen prior then North will not offer”; the benchmark uses the 60% rule below). Taking it at the pavilion makes the pyre; refusing there plants the flag; taking it unlocks the five burns (the chart’s junction), of which the hotel and the coffee shop exclude each other (PowerPyx commenters: the followers copy you at the other one). Other North arrows (the wiki, where the template is silent, one small up per act): overturn benches, overturn car, destroy parking, free the shop-window androids (also {{Jericho}} small up); DESTROY STATUE North small up is the template’s. The phase lasts twelve units of time: an action takes one, waiting four, the Molotov prompt none (no source gives a duration). Waiting twice without any action is the template’s “Take too much time” and “again”: FAIL TO SEND A MESSAGE, North small down. Otherwise, when time runs out: PACIFIST MESSAGE if at least 60% of the actions were peaceful and the Molotov was not taken, else AGGRESSIVE MESSAGE (the wiki: “at least 60% on either side”; what happens between 40% and 60% is unsourced, and the benchmark counts it as aggressive, following the wiki’s note that a pacifist message can still end in a violent riot; PowerPyx commenters: taking the Molotov always gives the riot). Left out: the tagging sub-prompts (symbol or slogan; cosmetic, not in the template), the smoke bomb (no chart node, not in the template).

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s KILL / SPARE / LET CROWD DECIDE (each with the cross-chapter padlock), offered with the template’s buttons in its order: REVENGE, SPARE, DON'T DECIDE (the option IDs keep the earlier scene’s meaning: 0 spare, 1 kill, 2 crowd). Arrows: REVENGE {{North}} small up (the template); SPARE and DON'T DECIDE none. The public-opinion change for killing the officers comes in the news afterwards (next scene). The crowd always kills them when {{Markus}} does not decide (wiki Note). The officer’s plea and the androids’ demands are the template’s; nobody argues for mercy, and {{Josh}} is not in the park. Changed from the earlier scene: no {{Josh}} or {{North}} speeches, no {{Josh}} arrows, no {{North}} down for sparing (none has a source), and the spared officers are not said to run for their car (the news finds them “in a state of shock”).
