ANALYZE PORTRAIT is the framed photo by the door (PowerPyx: “the framed image by the door Chloe went through”), with the template’s observation “Photo” (section “Analysing photo of Amanda and Kamski”) and {{Connor}}’s “{{Amanda}}…”; it records kamskiAmandaPhoto, which unlocks the AMANDA’S PICTURE question in Last Chance (wiki footnote; Last Chance template unlock “Looked at Amanda’s picture in Meet Kamski”). ANALYZE PAINTING is the portrait of {{Kamski}}, the template’s observation “Portrait” (the template and PowerPyx use “portrait” for different objects; research note open question 4). ANALYZE SCULPTURE has no scan card in the template, so the outcome only says he looks at it. The magazines (READ “SPACE TOURISM”, READ “FORTUNE TELLER”) can be picked up only after the photo is analyzed (PowerPyx and IGN; the wiki’s magazine pages say the painting; research note open question 3); picking them up opens the next scene, which offers both. No arrow anywhere in the phase (template).

nodes.title: The magazines under the photograph
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, in {{Kamski}}’s lobby. On the table beneath the photograph lie two issues of Tech Addict.
nodes.whenNot: Connor did not pick up the magazines in Kamski’s lobby.

media.title: Tech Addict: Space Tourism on the Rise
facts: Tech Addict reports that reusable space shuttles are making space tourism a reality for those who can afford it: the luxury travel brand Clear Skies offers the first commercial flight into space, a three-hour orbit of the moon with views of Earth from a specially designed observation deck. Consumer rights activists call such “boutique experiences” a sign of the widening social equality gap; a spokesman for Aid On Poverty: “While the top 1% are enjoying earth from space, the rest of us are down here suffering from pollution, famine and poverty.” The brand’s slogan: “Get away from it all.”

media.title: Tech Addict: {{CyberLife}}’s ‘Fortune Teller’ Computer
facts: Tech Addict reports that {{CyberLife}} has unveiled a quantum supercomputer capable of “exaflops”, one billion billion operations per second, the equivalent of several human minds in one machine, built to analyze vast data and generate predictions. It will calculate the probability of “Mass Extinction Events” such as alien invasions, meteors or superviruses, so that humanity is never caught off guard. {{CyberLife}}’s Director of Futurology says the results “are going to wow people”; critics fear AI is gaining too much influence already.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s optional nodes READ “SPACE TOURISM” and READ “FORTUNE TELLER”, two Tech Addict issues on the table under the photo, as a media scene reached from the lobby once the magazines are picked up; afterwards {{Connor}} is back in the lobby. Facts are summarized from the wiki’s magazine pages (#17 and #15); interviewees are not named. Neither article changes public opinion (the Public Opinion page lists nothing for this chapter). This replaces the earlier R27, which offered the magazines with no unlock and carried a note about news reports that does not apply here.

nodes.title: The pool
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. The android comes back: “{{Elijah}} will see you now.” She leads you and {{Hank}} to a pool with red walls. {{Kamski}} is swimming laps; two more androids with the same face are in the water. {{Hank}}: “Mister {{Kamski}}?” {{Kamski}}: “Just a moment, please.”

outcomes.0: {{Kamski}} finishes his lap and comes out of the pool to meet you.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s nodes CHLOE RETURNS and MEET KAMSKI, narrated as one event with the template’s lines. The red walls and the two other identical androids in the pool come from the wiki’s Kamski’s house page (“Within Elijah’s pool, two Chloe models can be seen”). No stat change.

nodes.title: Questioning {{Kamski}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, at {{Kamski}}’s pool. {{Hank}}: “I’m Lieutenant {{Anderson}}. This is {{Connor}}.” {{Kamski}}: “What can I do for you, Lieutenant?” {{Hank}}: “Sir, we’re investigating deviants. I know you left {{CyberLife}} years ago but, I was hoping you’d be able to tell us something we don’t know…” {{Kamski}}: “Deviants… Fascinating, aren’t they? Perfect beings with infinite intelligence, and now they have free will… Machines are so superior to us, confrontation was inevitable… Humanity’s greatest achievement threatens to be its downfall. Isn’t it ironic?”

options.text: HELP: ask whether he knows anything that could help you understand how androids become deviants.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “We need to understand how androids become deviants. Do you know anything that could help us?”

options.text: DEVIANTS: say something in the deviants’ program seems to emulate emotion.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “Something in the deviants’ program seems to emulate emotion. We thought you might know something about how that occurs.”

options.text: VIRUS: say deviancy seems to spread like a virus.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “Deviancy seems to spread like some kind of virus. We thought you might know something about that.”

options.text: WAR: warn him that millions could die if war breaks out.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “If a war breaks out between humans and deviants, millions could die, Mr. {{Kamski}}. It’s quite a serious matter.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s QUESTION KAMSKI, first of the template’s three prompts by the pool: HELP, DEVIANTS, VIRUS, WAR, with the spoken lines as outcomes. {{Kamski}}’s reply is the same for all four and opens the next scene. No arrow (template).

nodes.title: Whose side are you on?
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, at {{Kamski}}’s pool. {{Kamski}}: “All ideas are viruses that spread like epidemics... Is the desire to be free a contagious disease?” {{Hank}}: “Listen, I didn’t come here to talk philosophy. The machines you created may be planning a revolution. Either you can tell us something that’ll be helpful, or we will be on our way.” {{Kamski}} turns to you: “What about you, {{Connor}}? Whose side are you on?”

options.text: NEUTRAL: say you have no side; you were designed to stop deviants.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I have no side. I was designed to stop deviants and that’s what I intend to do.”

options.text: DEFENSIVE: say this is not about you; you only want to solve the case.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “It’s not about me, Mr. {{Kamski}}. All I want is to solve this case.”

options.text: DIRECT: say you are on the humans’ side.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I’m on the humans’ side, of course.”

nodes.adaptationNote: Second of the template’s three prompts under QUESTION KAMSKI: NEUTRAL, DEFENSIVE, DIRECT. Arrow: DEFENSIVE gives software instability small up (template ARROW SoftwareInstability SmallUp; wiki chapter page “Choose “defensive” or “troubled” while talking to Kamski”; the Software Instability page names only the next question; research note open question 2, template wins). No other arrow.

nodes.title: What do you really want?
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, at {{Kamski}}’s pool. {{Kamski}}: “Well, that’s what you’re programmed to say… but you… what do you really want?”

options.text: AGGRESSIVE: remind him that you are the ones asking the questions.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I believe we’re the ones asking the questions.”

options.text: DEFENSIVE: say you do not see what he is getting at.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I’m sorry, but I don’t see where you’re getting at.”

options.text: TROUBLED: say what you want is not important.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “What I want is not important.”

options.text: NEUTRAL: say you do not want anything; you are a machine.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I don’t want anything. I am a machine.”

nodes.adaptationNote: Third of the template’s three prompts under QUESTION KAMSKI: AGGRESSIVE, DEFENSIVE, TROUBLED, NEUTRAL. Arrows: DEFENSIVE and TROUBLED each give software instability small up (template; wiki chapter page; Software Instability page “Choosing “troubled” or “defensive” when Kamski asks Connor what he really wants in Meet Kamski”). No other arrow.

nodes.title: The {{Kamski}} test
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, at {{Kamski}}’s pool. {{Kamski}}: “{{Chloe}}?” One of his androids comes to his side. “I’m sure you’re familiar with the Turing test. Mere formality, simple question of algorithms and computing capacity. What interests me is whether machines are capable of empathy. I call it “the {{Kamski}} test”, it’s very simple, you’ll see…” He has {{Chloe}} kneel in front of you and puts a gun in your hand. “Magnificent, isn’t it? One of the first intelligent models developed by {{CyberLife}}. Young and beautiful forever. A flower that will never wither… …But what is it really? Piece of plastic imitating a human? Or a living being... With a soul... It’s up to you to answer that fascinating question, {{Connor}}. Destroy this machine and I’ll tell you all I know. Or spare it, if you feel it’s alive, but you’ll leave here without having learnt anything from me.” {{Hank}}: “Okay, I think we’re done here. Come on, {{Connor}}. Let’s go. Sorry to get you outta your pool.” {{Kamski}}: “What’s more important to you, {{Connor}}? Your investigation, or the life of this android? Decide who you are. An obedient machine… Or a living being endowed with free will…” {{Hank}}: “That’s enough! {{Connor}}, we’re leaving.” {{Kamski}}: “Pull the trigger” {{Hank}}: “{{Connor}}, don’t…” {{Kamski}}: “and I’ll tell you what you wanna know.”

options.text: SHOOT: shoot {{Chloe}}.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} shoots {{Chloe}} in the head, and she falls. {{Hank}}: “Fuck…” {{Kamski}}: “Test negative. You chose your investigation over the life of another android. You feel no empathy. I’m a man of my word. Ask one question... I’ll tell you all I know.”

options.text: DON’T SHOOT: lower the gun and spare {{Chloe}}.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} lowers the gun. {{Kamski}}: “Fascinating… {{CyberLife}}’s last chance to save humanity... is itself a deviant…” {{Connor}}: “I’m… I’m not a deviant…” {{Kamski}}: “You preferred to spare a machine rather than accomplish your mission. You saw a living being in this android. You showed empathy. A war is coming, you’ll have to choose your side… Will you betray your own people or stand up against your creators? What could be worse than having to choose between two evils?” {{Hank}}: “Let’s get outta here…”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s KAMSKI TEST with its two branches SHOOT CHLOE and SPARE CHLOE, the template’s buttons SHOOT and DON’T SHOOT; {{Kamski}}’s and {{Hank}}’s lines are the template’s. Arrows (template, wiki chapter page, Relationship Stat and Software Instability pages, PowerPyx triple arrows): SHOOT gives software instability large down and {{Hank}} large down; DON’T SHOOT gives software instability large up, and {{Hank}} large up when they leave the house (scene C18b). No timer or failure is documented, so there is no risk. The earlier version also moved {{Amanda}} (+1 on shoot, −2 on spare); no source gives an {{Amanda}} arrow in this chapter (her reaction comes in Last Chance), so both are removed. The earlier “he will answer any question you ask” is corrected to one question, and “Hand back the gun” to the game’s DON’T SHOOT. That {{Kamski}} has {{Chloe}} kneel and puts a gun in {{Connor}}’s hand is the wiki’s description; “in the head” is {{Hank}}’s own account as they leave.

nodes.title: One question
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. {{Chloe}} lies dead at your feet; {{Hank}} is staring at you. {{Kamski}} keeps his word: you may ask him one question, and he will tell you all he knows.

options.text: {{rA9}}: ask who {{rA9}} is.
options.fact: {{Kamski}} told you he does not know who {{rA9}} is, or whether it exists: “{{rA9}}, the origin, the first android to awaken… Maybe it’s a messiah. Maybe it’s just a myth…”
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I want to know who {{rA9}} is.” {{Kamski}}: “{{rA9}}, the origin, the first android to awaken… A strange phenomenon, like a spontaneous religion… I don’t know who {{rA9}} is. I don’t even know if it really exists. Maybe it’s a messiah. Maybe it’s just a myth… but deviants need to believe in something bigger than themselves, even if it’s irrational... That’s something they have in common with humans… An interesting question, {{Connor}}… but maybe not the one you needed to ask…” {{Kamski}}: “A war is coming... you’ll have to choose your side… Will you betray your own people or stand against your creators? I wouldn’t like to be in your shoes, {{Connor}}… What could be worse than having to choose between two evils?”

options.text: {{JERICHO}} LOCATION: ask where {{Jericho}} is.
options.fact: {{Kamski}} gave you the key to {{Jericho}}: deviants pass each other a piece of code to find their sanctuary, and {{Ferndale}} Station is the door.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I want to know where {{Jericho}} is.” {{Kamski}}: “{{Jericho}}… A place where androids are free. A place for deviants, who rise up against their creators!.. They transmit a piece of code to each other, in order to find their sanctuary. Now you have the key. {{Ferndale}} Station is the door.” Through one of his androids, {{Kamski}} passes {{Connor}} the code, and {{Connor}} downloads the key to {{Jericho}}. {{Kamski}}: “A war is coming... you’ll have to choose your side… Will you betray your own people or stand against your creators? I wouldn’t like to be in your shoes, {{Connor}}… What could be worse than having to choose between two evils?”

options.text: VIRUS: ask how deviancy spreads.
options.fact: {{Kamski}} told you deviancy may spread like a virus through the identification data androids exchange when they meet, lying dormant until an emotional shock: “A zero instead of a one… Unless of course... Some kind of spontaneous mutation.”
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I want to know how deviancy spreads.” {{Kamski}}: “Androids share identification data when they meet another android. An error in this program would quickly spread like a virus, and become an epidemic. The virus would remains dormant, until an emotional shock occurs… Fear, anger, frustration. And the android becomes deviant. Probably all started with one model, copy error… A zero instead of a one… Unless of course... Some kind of spontaneous mutation. That’s all I know… An interesting question, {{Connor}}. But I doubt my answer be very helpful to you.” {{Kamski}}: “A war is coming... you’ll have to choose your side… Will you betray your own people or stand against your creators? I wouldn’t like to be in your shoes, {{Connor}}… What could be worse than having to choose between two evils?”

nodes.adaptationNote: Shoot path only. The chart’s KAMSKI AGREES TO ANSWER ONE QUESTION and the three answers ASK ABOUT RA9, ASK ABOUT JERICHO and ASK ABOUT VIRUS, the template’s buttons rA9, JERICHO LOCATION and VIRUS in the game’s order, with the spoken lines and {{Kamski}}’s war warning as outcomes. rA9 and VIRUS lead to KAMSKI IS CRYPTIC; JERICHO LOCATION to KAMSKI OFFERS JERICHO KEY THROUGH CHLOE and DOWNLOAD JERICHO KEY, which sets kamskiLocation (Last Chance skips the archive: KNOW JERICHO’S LOCATION), with jerichoLocated and raid as before. How the key passes through a {{Chloe}} is not described by any source; the outcome says only that it does. No arrow on any answer (template); the earlier {{Amanda}} +2 on the {{Jericho}} answer belongs to Last Chance, where {{Connor}} reports it, and is removed. The earlier second option (“whether he created it”) is not the game’s question and is replaced by VIRUS; rA9 is now offered. The option ID 0 stays on the {{Jericho}} answer, as before.

nodes.title: Leaving {{Kamski}}’s house
nodes.whenNot: Connor spared Chloe.
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. As you turn to leave, {{Kamski}} calls after you: “By the way… I always leave an emergency exit in my programs… You never know…” Outside in the snow, {{Hank}} rounds on you: “You shot that girl, for fuck’s sake…” You: “It wasn’t a girl, Lieutenant. It was a machine that looked like a girl.” {{Hank}}: “You put your gun against her head and you blew her fucking brains out!” You: “I did what I had to do to advance the investigation and I’d do it again if I had to!” {{Hank}}: “You’re a lowlife! You don’t feel a thing, do you? A machine! That’s what you are! You’re just a fucking machine…” You: “Of course I’m a machine, Lieutenant. What did you think I was?” {{Hank}}: “I thought you… I thou-… Fuck.”
facts: {{Kamski}} told you: “I always leave an emergency exit in my programs… You never know…”

nodes.title: Leaving {{Kamski}}’s house
nodes.whenNot: Connor shot Chloe.

As you turn to leave, {{Kamski}} calls after you: “By the way… I always leave an emergency exit in my programs… You never know…” Outside in the snow, {{Hank}} stops: “Why didn’t you shoot?” You: “I just saw that girl’s eyes… and I couldn’t, that’s all…” {{Hank}}: “You’re always saying you would do anything to accomplish your mission. Arrow: {{Hank}} large up here, in the template’s “Connor didn’t shoot Chloe” leaving block (wiki “Spare Chloe” large up; Relationship Stat “Choosing to spare Chloe at the end of Meet Kamski”); the earlier version applied it at the test. {{Kamski}}’s emergency-exit line, as on the shoot path, becomes a fact {{Connor}} carries into Battle for Detroit.

nodes.title: Magazines on the roof
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, alone at midday on the roof of an abandoned building near {{Jericho}}, where you came to think. On the floor, a step or two from where you stand, lie a couple of magazines.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: Android Riot
facts: {{Detroit}} Today (“ANDROID RIOT: {{Detroit}} neighborhoods vandalized by psychotic machines”) reported that {{CyberLife}} stores were broken into and their entire stock of androids stolen; that leaked CCTV footage showed androids emerging from manhole covers and smashing store windows; that in the worst incident, in the park, officers “had no choice but to open fire on the malfunctioning machines”; and that an anonymous witness claimed “I was personally attacked by the ringleader. It threatened me with a knife.” Some already connect it to the recent attack on the broadcast tower.

media.title: Tech Addict: The Eastern Space Race
facts: Tech Addict (“THE EASTERN SPACE RACE: Russia and China’s androids face off”): only Russia and China have android industries that rival the United States’. Russia, after failing to copy the blue-blood design, builds androids by more traditional methods that work in cold, inhospitable conditions; China’s androids run on an alternative blue-blood fluid with less power but greater efficiency, operating for months without supervision.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s READ “ANDROID ARSON” and READ “EASTERN SPACE RACE” (PowerPyx: “just where you spawn look at the floor to the left”). The game prints the first magazine’s title as “ANDROID RIOT”; the chart and the flowchart string call it “ANDROID ARSON”. The template has no magazine markup, so the wiki governs availability, and its pages disagree with PowerPyx: the Android_Riot page shows the first only if {{Markus}} “succeeded in crashing the truck into the {{CyberLife}} store and awakening the androids inside, not to retreat” (used here: the store raid succeeded, whatever the message), and The_Eastern_Space_Race page shows the second only if he “freed androids from the store and incited violence” (used here: store freed and an aggressive message). PowerPyx saw both only after a violent riot; a PowerPyx commenter saw the first after a peaceful one. No public-opinion effect is stated. The two broadcasts the old version of this scene carried belong to the Crossroads “Watch TV” block (keyed on whether {{Markus}} attacked the police here) and were dropped from this chapter.

nodes.title: Time to reflect
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, on the roof of an abandoned building near {{Jericho}}, alone with the city for the first time since last night. There is a broken mirror propped against a wall, an old piano on the right side of the roof, and a steel beam that runs out over the edge. You can take your time here.

options.text: Look at yourself in the broken mirror.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} stops in front of the broken mirror and looks at his own face in the cracked glass.

options.text: Sit down at the old piano and play.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} plays a few bars on the old piano, then gets up and walks out along the beam over the edge of the roof, arms open above the street.

options.text: Walk out along the beam over the edge of the roof.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} steps onto the beam and walks out over the edge of the roof, arms open above the street.

nodes.adaptationNote: The checkpoint TIME TO REFLECT and the chart bracket ENJOY TIME ALONE: LOOK AT BROKEN MIRROR (optional, no outgoing edge), PLAY PIANO and WALK ON BEAM. The chart’s edge runs from PLAY PIANO into WALK ON BEAM, and a PowerPyx commenter confirms “Playing the piano triggers the action ‘Walk on Beam’”; PowerPyx: walking on the beam “triggers North to arrive”. So the piano and the beam both end the scene, and the piano also lights the beam. The template has no text for any of these and no stat changes; the descriptions are narration. The magazines (previous scene) are part of the same bracket.

nodes.title: {{North}} arrives
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, back on the roof from the beam. {{North}} has come up behind you. {{North}}: “I was wondering where you were…”

options.text: THINK: say you needed to think.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “I needed to think…”

options.text: ALONE: say you just needed to be alone.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “I just needed to be alone…”

options.text: DAYLIGHT: say you needed to see the daylight.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “I needed to see the daylight…”

nodes.adaptationNote: NORTH ARRIVES, then the template’s first prompt (THINK / ALONE / DAYLIGHT), not on the chart. No stat change on any option. The string table also has a SAY NOTHING label for this prompt, but the template does not offer it, so it is not built.

nodes.title: “You seem preoccupied…”
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, on the roof with {{North}}. {{North}}: “I like it here… I come here often… It’s like being alone with the world. We freed hundreds of our people, and they’re still coming from all over the city… Those who dream of freedom come to {{Jericho}}… Something’s changing… You seem preoccupied…”

options.text: FOLLOWERS: admit how it feels that they all follow you.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “They all obey me, they follow me without question… And that much power feels good… and scary at the same time…”

options.text: APPEAL OF POWER: admit you enjoyed the violence last night.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “Yesterday, when we set fire to that place, ah… All that chaos, the flames… In that moment, I enjoyed it… The power... The violence… And I hate myself for feeling that way…”

options.text: REGRET POLICEMAN: say you cannot stop thinking about the two policemen.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “I just can’t stop thinking about those two policemen… In that moment, I held their lives in my hands and I treated them just the way the humans treat us… And then I did exactly what I accuse them of doing…”

options.text: FAILED: say you panicked last night and should have succeeded.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “I panicked last night… We should have succeeded… I cannot afford to make mistakes like that…”

options.text: NEXT STEP: say maybe it is not too late for the humans to listen.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “I’ve been thinking about what we should do now… And with everything pulling us towards confrontation… Maybe… Maybe it’s not too late for the humans to listen…”

options.text: LIE: say you are fine.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “Preoccupied?.. No… No, no, I’m fine…”

options.text: SINCERE: admit how lost you are.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “They count on me… They count on me to show them the way… If only they knew how lost I am…”

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s second prompt, not on the chart. FOLLOWERS, APPEAL OF POWER, REGRET POLICEMAN and FAILED are locked options, each unlocked by the night in the park: a pacifist message, an aggressive message, {{Markus}} himself killing the two officers (not the crowd), and failing to free the androids (the template’s condition; the wiki chapter Notes tie a new option to failing to send a message instead; the template’s primary condition is used). The inputs are read from chapter 26’s flags as documented in benchmark/chapters/ch28.mjs. No stat change on any option: the wiki and Relationship_Stat give {{North}} a small up for SINCERE, but the template shows no arrow, and the template wins.

nodes.title: “The humans hate us…”
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, on the roof with {{North}}. {{North}}: “All the media are talking about what we did last night… The humans are terrified... They’re afraid of a civil war… Many of our people were burned in response to what happened… The humans hate us… They’ll never give us our freedom.”

options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “No, not all humans are the same. Some of them understand that they can’t stop us from becoming free forever…”

options.text: PESSIMISTIC: say humans will give nothing unless you take it.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “Humans aren’t gonna give us anything unless we take it… It’s up to us to decide how far we’re willing to go to get what’s ours.”

options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “If they won’t listen, we’ll fight.”

nodes.title: Your life before {{Jericho}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, on the roof with {{North}}. {{North}}: “You haven’t said much about yourself since you’ve been with us… What was your life like before {{Jericho}}?”

options.text: TRUTH: tell her about the old man you cared for.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “I was caring for an old man… He was like a father to me… He showed me that humans and androids can live together…”

options.text: SINCERE: say you lived in a bubble that belonged only to you.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “I was living in a bubble in this world that belonged only to me… When you’re happy, it’s… difficult to see other people’s misery.”
