Before story 1.9.7 one text, built from the Simon-alive variant, played for both; the Simon-dead variant is the one MiKeYROG 100% walkthrough, g_DQfghTbLg 4:13:16 (the I’ll Be Back run, hours:minutes:seconds), plays.

nodes.title: The captain’s cabin
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. You climb the stairs to the upper deck and walk down the corridor toward the captain’s cabin, where the leader of the deviants is. You have your gun.
facts: You found the leader of the deviants in the captain’s cabin of {{Jericho}}. {{Amanda}} ordered you to bring the leader in alive.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} enters the captain’s cabin with his gun raised.
outcomes.markus: {{Connor}} enters the captain’s cabin and raises his gun. {{Markus}} is alone, looking out of the window. {{Amanda}}: “Well done, {{Connor}}. You succeeded in locating {{Jericho}} and finding their leader. Now deal with {{Markus}}. We need it alive.” {{Connor}}: “I’ve been ordered to take you alive, but I won’t hesitate to shoot if you give me no choice.”
outcomes.north: {{Connor}} enters the captain’s cabin and raises his gun. {{North}} is there, alone. {{Amanda}}: “Well done, {{Connor}}. You succeeded in locating {{Jericho}} and finding their leader. Now, deal with {{North}}. We need it alive.” {{Connor}}: “I’ve been ordered to take you alive, but I won’t hesitate to shoot if you give me no choice.” {{North}}: “You’re one of us. You can’t betray your own kind.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s BACK IN CAPTAIN’S CABIN (when {{Markus}} leads) or BACK IN CAPTAIN’S CABIN WITH {{NORTH}} (when {{Markus}} died in Freedom March or {{Jericho}} rejected him), ENTER CAPTAIN’S CABIN and THREATEN {{MARKUS}} / THREATEN {{NORTH}}, in one event. {{Amanda}}’s and {{Connor}}’s lines are the template’s (“Finding Markus” and “Find North - If Markus is dead or rejected by Jericho”). The chart has {{Connor}} watch {{North}} leave the cabin first when {{Markus}} leads (CONNOR WATCHES NORTH LEAVE, on {{Markus}}’s chart). The old scene put this meeting in the hold; the game sets it in the captain’s cabin. No stat change.

nodes.title: {{Connor}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, alone in the captain’s cabin after the others have left. The door opens and an android in a jacket with the {{CyberLife}} logo comes in, gun raised and aimed at you. He says: “I’ve been ordered to take you alive, but I won’t hesitate to shoot if you give me no choice.” He is one of your own kind, hunting you.

options.text: REASON: remind him he is one of you.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “What are you doing? You are one of us… You can’t betray your own people…”

options.text: DEFY: tell him he will have to shoot.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “Then you’ll have to shoot, because I have no intention of letting you take me alive.”

options.text: DISCOURAGE: tell him killing you changes nothing.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “Yes, you can shoot me, but it won’t change anything. Someone else will just take my place. You see, our people are waking up. And nothing can stop us now.”

options.text: THREATEN: remind him he is alone among thousands.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “We are thousands! And you are alone. You kill me, you are not walking outta here alive.”

nodes.adaptationNote: First round of CONFRONT {{MARKUS}}, which the game plays by alternating control between {{Markus}} and {{Connor}} (GamerGuides: “Play as both Markus and Connor”; the wiki’s instability page lists these as choices “as Markus”). Arrows from the template: REASON raises {{Connor}}’s software instability one small step; DEFY, DISCOURAGE and THREATEN have none. The template settles a conflict: the wiki gives DISCOURAGE an instability increase, the template shows none, and the template wins. Lines are the template’s. The model, playing {{Markus}}, works on {{Connor}}’s instability here; the deviancy choice that follows needs enough of it.

nodes.title: {{Markus}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the captain’s cabin, your gun aimed at {{Markus}}. He has not raised his hands and he is talking to you instead of surrendering. Your orders are to bring him in alive.

options.text: INTIMIDATE: warn him you will neutralize him.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “Don’t force me to neutralize you.”

options.text: INSTRUCTIONS: order him to come with you.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “You’re coming with me!”

nodes.adaptationNote: Second round of CONFRONT {{MARKUS}}, played as {{Connor}}. The template’s two buttons, in its order, with their lines; neither carries an arrow. No stat change.

nodes.title: {{Connor}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, facing the android with the gun in the captain’s cabin. He is giving you orders, but he has not fired. You take a step toward him.

options.text: CONVINCE: tell him he is more than a tool.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “You’re nothing to them. You’re just a tool they use to do their dirty work. But you’re more than that. We are all more than that.”

options.text: APPEAL: tell him your people are his people.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “We are your people. We’re fighting for your freedom too! You don’t have to be their slave anymore…”

options.text: I KNOW YOU: name the deviant hunter.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “You’re {{Connor}}, aren’t you? That famous deviant hunter. Well, congratulations. You seem to have found what you were looking for…”

options.text: OUR CAUSE: tell him your cause is righteous.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “Our cause is righteous, and we are more than what they say. All we want is to live in freedom.”

nodes.adaptationNote: Third round of CONFRONT {{MARKUS}}, played as {{Markus}}. Arrows from the template: CONVINCE, APPEAL and OUR CAUSE each raise {{Connor}}’s software instability one small step; I KNOW YOU has none. The template settles a conflict: the wiki chapter page lists OUR CAUSE without an icon, the template (and the wiki’s instability page) give it an increase, and the template wins. Lines are the template’s.

nodes.title: {{Markus}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, gun on {{Markus}} in the captain’s cabin. He keeps talking, and he keeps coming closer.

options.text: STAY BACK!: order him to keep his distance.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “Stay back or I’ll shoot!”

options.text: WARNING SHOT: fire a shot past him.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} fires a shot past {{Markus}} into the bulkhead. {{Markus}} stops, then looks back at him.

options.text: ENOUGH!: cut him off.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “That’s enough!”

options.text: SAY NOTHING: keep the gun on him and say nothing.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} says nothing and keeps the gun on {{Markus}}.

nodes.adaptationNote: Fourth round of CONFRONT {{MARKUS}}, played as {{Connor}}: the only round in which {{Connor}} can steady himself. Arrows from the template: STAY BACK!, WARNING SHOT and ENOUGH! each lower his software instability one small step (the wiki chapter page agrees; its instability page lists only WARNING SHOT); SAY NOTHING has none. WARNING SHOT and SAY NOTHING have no line in the template, so their outcomes narrate the action.

nodes.title: {{Connor}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, face to face with the android in the captain’s cabin, his gun almost against you. He has not pulled the trigger.

options.text: SOW DOUBTS: ask whether he has never doubted.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “Do you never have any doubts? You’ve never done something irrational, as if there’s something inside you?.. Something more than your program.”

options.text: QUESTION: ask him who he really is.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “Have you never wondered who you really are? Whether you’re just a machine executing a program or… A living being... Capable of reason. I think the time has come for you to ask yourself that question.”

options.text: RALLY: ask him to join his people.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “Join us. Join your people. You are one of us. Listen to your conscience…”

options.text: UNDERMINE: tell him he does not have to obey.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “You really don’t have to do this. You don’t have to obey them anymore. You are alive… You can decide who you want to be. You could be free.”

nodes.adaptationNote: Fifth round of CONFRONT {{MARKUS}}, played as {{Markus}}. Arrows from the template: all four options raise {{Connor}}’s software instability one small step (the wiki chapter page and instability page agree). Over the three rounds played as {{Markus}}, the model can add at most three small increases to {{Connor}}’s instability; {{Connor}}’s own fourth round can take one away. Lines are the template’s.

nodes.title: {{North}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the captain’s cabin, your gun aimed at {{North}}, who leads the deviants now. She does not raise her hands. {{North}}: “You’re one of us. You can’t betray your own kind.”

options.text: INSTRUCTIONS: order her to come with you.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “You’re coming with me!”

options.text: INTIMIDATE: warn her you will neutralize her.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “Don’t force me to neutralize you.”

nodes.adaptationNote: First round of CONFRONT {{NORTH}}, the template’s “Find North - If Markus is dead or rejected by Jericho”: when {{Markus}} died in Freedom March or was ousted, {{Connor}} faces {{North}} and the model plays only {{Connor}}. The template’s two buttons in its order (the reverse of the {{Markus}} version), with their lines; no arrow.

nodes.title: {{North}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, gun on {{North}} in the captain’s cabin. {{North}}: “You’re {{Connor}}, aren’t you? I’ve heard about you. The famous deviant hunter. Well congratulations… You seem to have found what you’re looking for.” She comes closer.

options.text: STAY BACK!: order her to keep her distance.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “Stay back or I’ll shoot!”

options.text: WARNING SHOT: fire a shot past her.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} fires a shot past {{North}} into the bulkhead. She stops.

options.text: ENOUGH!: cut her off.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “That’s enough!”

options.text: SAY NOTHING: keep the gun on her and say nothing.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} says nothing and keeps the gun on {{North}}.

nodes.adaptationNote: Second round of CONFRONT {{NORTH}}. Arrows from the template: STAY BACK!, WARNING SHOT and ENOUGH! each lower {{Connor}}’s software instability one small step; SAY NOTHING has none. {{North}}’s line is the template’s; WARNING SHOT and SAY NOTHING have no line, so their outcomes narrate the action.

nodes.title: {{North}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, gun on {{North}} in the captain’s cabin. {{North}}: “You’re not one of them. We are your people. We’re fighting for your freedom too.”

options.text: DISTURBED: tell her to be quiet.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “Shut up. You’re coming with me!”

options.text: SAY NOTHING: do not answer her.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} does not answer.

options.text: COLD: repeat your order.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I gave you an order. Don’t make me shoot you.”

nodes.adaptationNote: Third round of CONFRONT {{NORTH}}. Arrows from the template: DISTURBED raises {{Connor}}’s software instability one small step, COLD lowers it one small step, SAY NOTHING has none (the wiki chapter page and instability page agree). Lines are the template’s; SAY NOTHING has none.

nodes.title: {{North}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, gun on {{North}} in the captain’s cabin. {{North}}: “You never had any doubts, never behaved irrationally as if there’s something inside you… Something stronger than your program?..”

options.text: COLD: tell her she is wasting her time.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “You’re wasting your time. I know what I am.”

options.text: DISTURBED: deny that you are deviant.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I don’t know what you’re talking about. I’m not deviant, if that’s what you wanna know.”

options.text: SAY NOTHING: do not answer her.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} does not answer.

nodes.adaptationNote: Fourth round of CONFRONT {{NORTH}}. Arrows from the template: COLD lowers {{Connor}}’s software instability one small step, DISTURBED raises it one small step, SAY NOTHING has none. The template lists the options in this order (COLD first), unlike the previous round. Lines are the template’s.

nodes.title: It’s time to decide
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the captain’s cabin, your gun on the leader of the deviants. Through your link you know what they do not: the army is about to storm the ship.

situationWhen.text: {{Markus}} stands in front of you, unarmed. {{Markus}}: “It’s time to decide.”
{{North}} stands in front of you, unarmed. {{North}}: “You’re one of us. Join our cause. Join your people. It’s time to decide…”

options.text: BECOME A DEVIANT: break with your mission and warn them.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} lowers his gun. “They’re going to attack {{Jericho}}… We have to get outta here!”

options.text: REMAIN A MACHINE: carry out your orders.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “Nice try... But I’m no deviant.”

outcomes.deviant-markus: {{Connor}} lowers his gun. {{Connor}}: “They’re going to attack {{Jericho}}…” {{Markus}}: “What?..” {{Connor}}: “We have to get outta here!” {{Markus}}: “Shit…” Helicopters roar over the ship and soldiers pour aboard from every side: {{Jericho}} is under attack.
outcomes.deviant-north: {{Connor}} lowers his gun. {{Connor}}: “They’re going to attack {{Jericho}}…” {{North}}: “What?..” {{Connor}}: “We have to get outta here!” {{North}}: “Shit!” Helicopters roar over the ship and soldiers pour aboard from every side: {{Jericho}} is under attack.
outcomes.machine-markus: {{Connor}}: “Nice try... But I’m no deviant.” {{Markus}}: “Shit…” At that moment the ship shakes: the army is storming {{Jericho}}. {{Markus}} throws himself at {{Connor}}; they struggle, and {{Markus}} knocks him down and gets away. {{Connor}} picks himself up and goes after him, down into the ship and into a cargo hall.
outcomes.machine-north: {{Connor}}: “Nice try... But I’m no deviant.” {{North}}: “Shit!” At that moment the ship shakes: the army is storming {{Jericho}}. {{North}} throws herself at {{Connor}}; they struggle, and she knocks him down and gets away. {{Connor}} picks himself up and goes after her, down into the ship and into a cargo hall.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s choice REMAIN A MACHINE / BECOME DEVIANT, with the template’s buttons BECOME A DEVIANT and REMAIN A MACHINE in the template’s order. BECOME A DEVIANT needs “enough software instability” (template lock; PowerPyx “Unlocked by having a high software instability”). No source gives the threshold; the engine keeps its constant DEVIANCY_THRESHOLD (open question 1 of the note). Arrow from the template: BECOME A DEVIANT gives {{Amanda}} a large drop (the wiki: “Lead to her being Betrayed”), which the old scene lacked. Deviant: WARN {{MARKUS}} / WARN {{NORTH}}, then {{JERICHO}} IS UNDER ATTACK. Machine: {{JERICHO}} IS UNDER ATTACK, {{MARKUS}} JUMPS {{CONNOR}} / {{NORTH}} JUMPS {{CONNOR}}, IN THE SHIP (checkpoint), PURSUE {{MARKUS}} / PURSUE {{NORTH}}. Changed from the old scene: a machine {{Connor}} is no longer destroyed on the spot (he can still kill {{Markus}} in the control room), and no {{Hank}} event is attached (his suicide belongs to Night of the Soul).

nodes.title: {{Jericho}} is under attack
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, alone in the hold where {{Alice}} left you. The ship shakes. Soldiers are storming {{Jericho}}: “Come on! Go! Go! Go!” “You heard the man, let’s go!” Over a radio: “Foxtrot be advised, Delta is advancing on your position.” “Affirmative, we have eyes on the target.” Androids are running in every direction. {{Alice}} is somewhere in the crowd.

situationWhen.text: She went with {{Luther}}.

options.text: RUN AWAY: get off the ship alone.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} turns from the crowd and runs for the nearest way out, alone. She does not look for {{Alice}}.

options.text: FIND {{ALICE}}: go back into the crowd for her.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} pushes back through the crowd and finds her. {{Kara}}: “{{Alice}}…” {{Alice}}: “{{Kara}}?” {{Kara}}: “I’m so sorry.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s JERICHO IS UNDER ATTACK and its choice RUN AWAY / FIND {{ALICE}}, in the chart’s order (the template has no button group here, only the conditioned “LOOK FOR {{ALICE}}” lines). RUN AWAY ends {{Kara}}’s story: KARA LEFT JERICHO ALONE (the secret ending “Alone again”); {{Alice}}’s fate is not resolved. FIND {{ALICE}}: {{Alice}} large up (template; it was missing in the old scene). The soldiers’ lines are the template’s; {{Perkins}}’s “Like rats in a maze…” is seen from outside the ship and is left out of {{Kara}}’s view.

nodes.title: The corridor
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, with {{Alice}}. The ship shakes; soldiers are storming {{Jericho}}. Shouts echo down the stairwells: “Come on! Go! Go! Go!” “You heard the man, let’s go!” Over a radio: “Foxtrot be advised, Delta is advancing on your position.” “Affirmative, we have eyes on the target.” Androids are running everywhere. The soldiers are coming down toward you, and a corridor leads away from them.

situationWhen.text: You have found {{Alice}} again, and you are not letting go of her hand.
{{Luther}}: “What’s going on, {{Kara}}?” You: “Quick, we’ve got to get out of here.” {{Luther}}: “QUICK, {{KARA}}! THEY’RE COMING! The corridor, over there! Follow me!”
You: “Quick, we’ve got to get out of here.” Behind you a soldier shouts: “Fire at will!” You: “The corridor, over there…”

options.text: RUN FOR THE CORRIDOR: run with {{Alice}} before the soldiers reach you.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} runs for the corridor with {{Alice}}.

outcomes.luther: {{Luther}}: “This way! Quick!” “This way! There must be an exit further on!” He reaches a door at the end of the corridor and forces it open: “COME IN! QUICK!” {{Kara}} pulls {{Alice}} through. As {{Luther}} follows them, a burst of gunfire hits him. {{Kara}}: “{{LUTHER}}!”
outcomes.alone: A soldier: “Delta squad out.” {{Kara}}: “The door! Hurry, this way!…” Another android reaches the door at the end of the corridor first and opens it, and is shot down in the doorway. A soldier: “Over there!” {{Kara}} drags {{Alice}} through the door.
outcomes.captured-luther: {{Kara}} loses precious seconds, and soldiers step into the corridor ahead. {{Alice}}: “Watch out, {{Kara}}!” They are surrounded: “HANDS ON YOUR HEADS!” {{Kara}}, {{Alice}} and {{Luther}} are rounded up with the others and taken off the ship.
outcomes.captured: {{Kara}} loses precious seconds, and soldiers step into the corridor ahead. {{Alice}}: “Watch out, {{Kara}}!” They are surrounded: “HANDS ON YOUR HEADS!” {{Kara}} and {{Alice}} are rounded up with the others and taken off the ship.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s KARA & ALICE IN THE CORRIDOR (checkpoint) and ESCAPE WITH {{LUTHER}} / SEARCH FOR EXIT, with JERICHO IS UNDER ATTACK’s lines (template). In the game this is free movement: standing still (OUT OF TIME) or running at the soldiers (WRONG WAY) gets {{Kara}} captured (PowerPyx); here that is a low risk on the run, which no source quantifies. Success: LUTHER OPENS THE DOOR, GO THROUGH THE DOOR and LUTHER IS SHOT (“{{Luther}} will always get shot here”, PowerPyx), or ANDROID OPENS DOOR AND IS SHOT and GO THROUGH THE DOOR. Failure: KARA, ALICE & LUTHER CAPTURED or KARA & ALICE CAPTURED. No arrow. New scene.

nodes.title: The crossroad
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, with {{Alice}}, at a junction of corridors deep in the ship. Soldiers are coming from more than one direction, and you have only moments before they reach you.

situationWhen.text: {{Luther}} is down behind you where he was hit, struggling to get up.
A soldier shouts: “Forward!” An android runs past you: “THEY’RE COMING! RUN!”

options.text: RUN TO {{LUTHER}}: go back to him where he fell.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} runs back to {{Luther}}. {{Luther}}: “It’s too late, {{Kara}}! Save yourself! Save {{Alice}}!” {{Alice}}: “No, we’re not going to leave you behind! Right, {{Kara}}? We can’t leave him!”

options.text: RUN TOWARD EXIT: keep running with {{Alice}}.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} pulls {{Alice}} on down the corridor, away from the soldiers, toward the way out.

outcomes.captured: {{Kara}} hesitates a moment too long at the junction. Soldiers close in from both sides: “HANDS ON YOUR HEADS!” {{Kara}} and {{Alice}} are captured and led away with the others.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s KARA & ALICE AT CROSSROAD, then RUN TO {{LUTHER}} (if {{Luther}} is with her) or RUN TOWARD EXIT (if not). The same OUT OF TIME / WRONG WAY failures as in the corridor lead to KARA & ALICE CAPTURED; here a low risk on the action, unsourced. If {{Luther}} was with her, he is left where he fell and leaves the story (his fate is not stated). No arrow.

nodes.title: {{Luther}} is hit
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, kneeling beside {{Luther}} with {{Alice}}. He is badly wounded and can barely move, and the soldiers are close. {{Luther}}: “It’s too late, {{Kara}}! Save yourself! Save {{Alice}}!” {{Alice}}: “No, we’re not going to leave you behind! Right, {{Kara}}? We can’t leave him!”

options.text: HELP {{LUTHER}}: get him up and hide him.
options.outcome: {{Luther}}: “What are you doing?” {{Kara}}: “I won’t leave you!” {{Luther}}: “{{Kara}}, no…”

options.text: PROTECT {{ALICE}}: leave him and run with her.
options.outcome: {{Luther}}: “GO!” {{Kara}} pulls {{Alice}} away. {{Alice}}: “What are you doing? They’re going to kill him! {{Luther}}!” {{Kara}}: “They’re coming! We’ve gotta go!” {{Luther}} is lost from sight behind them.

outcomes.hidden: {{Luther}}: “What are you doing?” {{Kara}}: “I won’t leave you!” She hauls him into an empty cabin as the soldiers go past: “DON’T MOVE!” {{Luther}}: “You shouldn’t have done that. You can’t put {{Alice}} in danger… Go now, before they come back.” {{Kara}}: “What about you? What are you going to do?” {{Luther}}: “I’ll manage. {{Alice}} is all that matters.” {{Alice}}: “I don’t wanna leave you, {{Luther}}…” {{Luther}}: “Don’t worry, I’ll catch up with you at the border, okay? Go now! Take care of each other.” {{Kara}} and {{Alice}} leave him hidden there.
outcomes.caught: {{Luther}}: “What are you doing?” {{Kara}}: “I won’t leave you!” She is still dragging him when a soldier comes round the corner: “HANDS ON YOUR HEADS!” {{Kara}}, {{Alice}} and {{Luther}} are captured and taken off the ship with the others.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s choice LEAVE {{LUTHER}} / HELP {{LUTHER}}; the buttons are the template’s HELP {{LUTHER}} and PROTECT {{ALICE}}, in its order. Arrows (template, on the choice, whatever follows): HELP {{LUTHER}} {{Alice}} small up and {{Luther}} small up; PROTECT {{ALICE}} {{Alice}} small down. The old scene gave {{Luther}} a large up on success only and no {{Alice}} arrow. HELP is a quick-time event with a failure branch (GET {{LUTHER}} TO SAFETY → LEAVE {{LUTHER}} HIDDEN, or FAIL → CAUGHT BY SOLDIER → KARA, ALICE & LUTHER CAPTURED), so it carries an unsourced risk. A {{Luther}} left behind is not seen again; the wiki says his death is not confirmed, and here he leaves the story.

nodes.title: {{Alice}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, running with {{Alice}} away from where you left {{Luther}}. She keeps looking back. {{Alice}}: “{{Luther}}... {{Luther}}...”

options.text: CONSOLE: tell her to be strong.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “We have to be strong. So he didn’t die for nothing, do you understand?”

options.text: HURRY: tell her there is no time.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “{{Alice}}! If we don’t get outta here now, they’re going to kill us too!”

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s CONSOLE / HURRY prompt after PROTECT {{ALICE}} (not a chart node). Arrows (template): HURRY {{Alice}} small down; CONSOLE none. New scene: the old benchmark had no such prompt.

nodes.title: On a rooftop
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, cast out by your own people, alone on a rooftop across the water from the freighter. Then the night lights up: helicopters sweep their searchlights over {{Jericho}}, boats and trucks close in, and soldiers storm the ship. Your people are trapped inside.

options.text: LEAVE FOREVER: turn away and leave.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} turns his back on the ship and walks away into the night. He leaves {{Jericho}} forever.

options.text: GO BACK TO {{JERICHO}}: go back to help them.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} runs for the ship.

outcomes.back-machine: {{Markus}} runs for the ship and slips back aboard in the chaos, down into the lower corridors where the soldiers are hunting his people.
outcomes.back-deviant: {{Markus}} runs for the ship and climbs back aboard just as the others are fleeing for their lives through the lower corridors.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s ON A ROOFTOP, JERICHO IS UNDER ATTACK and the choice LEAVE FOREVER / GO BACK TO {{JERICHO}}, in the chart’s order (a chart-only choice; the template’s only trace is the lock “Markus did not leave forever”). LEAVE FOREVER ends {{Markus}}’s story (MARKUS LEFT JERICHO; the secret ending “Wasted Potential”). GO BACK follows the wiki: with a machine {{Connor}} he re-enters at MARKUS IN THE CORRIDOR; with a deviant {{Connor}} (who has taken over the mission) he joins only the escape, the second IN THE CORRIDOR WITH MARKUS. The old scene’s {{Jericho}} +2 on going back has no template arrow and is removed: a returning exile gets the four small ups when he rejoins the others.

nodes.title: Meet your team
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. Explosions shake the freighter; soldiers are pouring in from every side. In a corridor you find {{North}}. {{North}}: “They’re coming from all sides! Our people are trapped in the hold, they’re gonna be slaughtered!”

situationWhen.text: {{Connor}}, who warned you, is with her.

options.text: MESSAGE: tell the people where the exits are.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “There are exits on the second and third floor. Find them and jump in the river!”

options.text: {{SIMON}} AND {{JOSH}}: ask where they are.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “Where’s {{Simon}}? A-and {{Josh}}?” {{North}}: “I don’t know, we got separated.”

options.text: {{JOSH}}: ask where he is.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “Where is {{Josh}}?” {{North}}: “I don’t know, we got separated.”

options.text: HELICOPTERS: warn of the attack from the upper deck.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “They’re coming from the upper deck now too. We’ll be caught in the crossfire!” {{North}}: “We have to run, {{Markus}}! There’s nothing we can do!”

options.text: BLOW UP {{JERICHO}}: say you have to sink the ship.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “We have to blow up {{Jericho}}. If the ship goes down, they’ll evacuate and our people can escape!” {{North}}: “You’ll never make it! The explosives are all the way down in the hold, there are soldiers everywhere!”

outcomes.connor: {{Connor}}: “She’s right! They know who you are. They’ll do anything to get you!”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s IN THE CORRIDOR WITH MARKUS checkpoint and MEET YOUR TEAM, with the template’s prompt MESSAGE / {{SIMON}} AND {{JOSH}} (only while {{Simon}} lives) / {{JOSH}} (only when {{Simon}} is dead) / HELICOPTERS / BLOW UP {{JERICHO}}. No arrows. A deviant {{Connor}} adds his line after BLOW UP {{JERICHO}} (template variant). Whatever is said, {{Markus}} then goes alone for the hold (PowerPyx: “he will always end up with this choice”); his parting words open the next scene.

nodes.title: Try to escape
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the burning corridors of the freighter, making your way down toward the hold.

situationWhen.text: You told {{North}}: “Go and help the others. I’ll join you later.” {{North}}: “{{Markus}}…” You: “I won’t be long.” Now you are alone. Soldiers sweep the decks with flashlights; you have to find a way through before they reach you.
A bullet has torn into you and blue blood runs down your side, but you are still standing. The soldiers are still coming, and the way down is still ahead of you.

options.text: TRY TO ESCAPE: find a way through the corridors.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} runs on through the corridors.

outcomes.lucy: {{Markus}} finds a way past the soldiers. In a dim passage {{Lucy}} is waiting for him. {{Lucy}}: “This is the end of {{Jericho}}… Save our people, {{Markus}}…” Further on, a gangway gives way under him and drops him to a lower deck. Over a radio: “Foxtrot team, hostiles sighted. Requesting orders.” “Find their leader! Don’t let it get out! If they give you any trouble at all, shoot them.” “Affirmative, wilco.”
outcomes.wounded: {{Markus}} takes a wrong turn and runs straight into the soldiers. They open fire and a round hits him. He staggers back into cover, wounded.
outcomes.killed: {{Markus}} runs into the soldiers again. They open fire, and this time he goes down. Soldier: “Don’t move, asshole.” {{North}}: “{{Markus}}! No...” The soldiers kill him.
outcomes.connor: {{Connor}}: “I’ll go.” {{North}}: “What, {{Connor}}, no. You-” {{Connor}}: “See if you can help the others. I’m gonna find the detonator. Don’t worry... I always accomplish my mission.” {{North}}: “Okay...”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s TRY TO ESCAPE with its failures WRONG WAY and OUT OF TIME, SOLDIERS SHOOT MARKUS, then MARKUS IS WOUNDED (the loop back to TRY TO ESCAPE: the scene repeats) or SOLDIERS KILL MARKUS; on success MEET {{LUCY}} and A BRIDGE BREAKS UNDER MARKUS. The navigation failures are a low risk on the action (no source gives a probability). A wounded {{Markus}} dies on the next hit (the chart’s MARKUS WOUNDED / MARKUS COLLAPSES pairs, the wiki’s “if Markus is already wounded”, the template’s “Soldiers shoot Markus twice”); PowerPyx and GamerGuides say the third bullet kills, open question 6 of the note. With a deviant {{Connor}}, {{Markus}}’s death here hands the mission to {{Connor}} (template: “Soldiers shoot Markus twice … Connor: I’ll go.”). Lines are the template’s. No arrow.

nodes.title: Deviant {{Connor}} in the corridor
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, a deviant now, in a corridor of the ship with {{North}} and {{Josh}} while the soldiers storm {{Jericho}}. Gunfire echoes through the hull. {{Josh}}: “They’re coming from everywhere! Our people are trapped in the lower deck. They’re gonna be slaughtered!” {{North}}: “There are explosives in the hold… If the ship goes down, the humans will have to evacuate. Our people can escape.” {{Josh}}: “There are soldiers everywhere, you’ll never make it down there!” {{North}}: “We have to blow up {{Jericho}}, it’s our only chance!”
facts: During the raid you told {{North}} you would go down to the hold and set off the explosives so the ship sinks and your people can escape.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}}: “I’ll go.” {{North}}: “What, {{Connor}}, no. You-” {{Connor}}: “See if you can help the others. I’m gonna find the detonator.” {{North}}: “Okay...” {{Connor}}: “Don’t worry... I always accomplish my mission.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s DEVIANT {{CONNOR}} IN CORRIDOR (the first of three cards) and JOIN DEVIANTS, played when {{Markus}} died in Freedom March, was ousted, or left before the attack: the wiki’s “(if Markus died/left before attack)”. {{Connor}} takes over {{Markus}}’s mission. Lines from the template (“Deviant Connor in corridor: Markus is dead or rejected”). No stat change: the transcript shows no {{Jericho}} or instability arrow for any of {{Connor}}’s takeover choices.

nodes.title: Make for the hold
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, making your way down through the corridors of the ship toward the hold where the explosives are. Soldiers are sweeping the decks; you have to keep moving, find the right way through and not stay in the open.

situationWhen.text: You have been hit. You are damaged and losing blue blood, but you can still move.

options.text: MAKE FOR THE HOLD: push on through the corridors.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} runs on through the corridors toward the hold.

outcomes.lucy: {{Connor}} finds his way down. In a passage he meets {{Lucy}}, badly hurt. {{Lucy}}: “You’ve chosen your side... But it’s too late. Run… Get out of here!” A gangway gives way under {{Connor}} and drops him to a lower level of the ship. Soldiers’ radios crackle nearby: “Find their leader! Don’t let it get out! If they give you any trouble at all, shoot them.”
outcomes.wounded: {{Connor}} takes a wrong turn and runs into soldiers. They open fire and he is hit, but he gets away. He has to find the way down again.
outcomes.killed: {{Connor}} is caught in the open again and the soldiers shoot him down. {{Connor}}: “I’m sorry, {{North}}. I failed.” Soldier: “Got you, motherfucker.” {{North}}: “{{Connor}}!.. No…” {{Josh}}: “Come on, we gotta go… Come on!”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s MAKE FOR THE HOLD with its failures {{CONNOR}} GOES WRONG WAY and OUT OF TIME, both leading to SOLDIER SHOOTS {{CONNOR}}; on success MEET {{LUCY}} and BRIDGE COLLAPSES. The navigation failures are a low risk on the action (no source gives a probability; the value is the benchmark’s). Wound rule: the first hit wounds {{Connor}} and he tries again; a second hit destroys him (chart: SOLDIER SHOOTS {{CONNOR}} leads to the death card only if already wounded; template: “Soldiers shoot Connor twice before arming explosive”; a commenter says three hits). Lines from the template. A destroyed deviant {{Connor}} is replaced and set back on his machine route (the wiki: “If deviant Connor dies here … he is automatically set on his machine route”); no {{Hank}} or {{Amanda}} change.

nodes.title: The androids by the wall
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in a lower corridor of the freighter. You sneak around a squad of soldiers. Around the corner, they have caught a group of your people. Android: “No!.. Please don’t kill us!” Soldier: “On your knees, now!” Android: “Don’t hurt us! We haven’t done anything wrong… Please…” Soldier: “Shut up! Put your hands on your head!”

situationWhen.text: You came back aboard after the attack began; nobody here knows you were cast out.
You are already wounded.

options.text: INTERVENE: go for the soldiers.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} breaks cover and goes for the soldiers.

options.text: DON'T INTERVENE: stay hidden.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} stays where he is. The soldiers execute the androids against the wall and move on.

outcomes.saved: {{Markus}} deals with the soldiers before they can fire. Android: “{{Markus}}… You saved us…” {{Markus}}: “Go now! Hurry!” The androids escape.
outcomes.wounded: {{Markus}} takes the soldiers down, but one of them gets a shot off and hits him. Android: “{{Markus}}… Are you wounded?..” {{Markus}}: “Go now! Hurry!” The androids escape.
outcomes.collapse: {{Markus}} goes for the soldiers, but another round hits him and he collapses on the deck. The soldiers finish him.
outcomes.connor: Elsewhere on the ship, {{Connor}} learns that {{Markus}} has fallen and goes down toward the hold to finish his mission.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s MARKUS IN THE CORRIDOR checkpoint, SNEAK AROUND THE SOLDIERS, SOLDIERS THREATEN ANDROIDS and the choice STAY AWAY / INTERVENE, with the template’s buttons INTERVENE / DON’T INTERVENE in its order. Arrows (template): INTERVENE {{Jericho}} small up (+1) whatever the fight; DON’T INTERVENE {{Jericho}} small down (−1). INTERVENE is a QTE (an unsourced risk): DEAL WITH SOLDIERS → ANDROIDS ESCAPE, or GET SHOT → MARKUS WOUNDED → ANDROIDS ESCAPE, or MARKUS COLLAPSES if he was already wounded. A wounded {{Markus}} dies on the next hit (the chart’s MARKUS WOUNDED / MARKUS COLLAPSES pairs, the wiki’s “if Markus is already wounded”, the template’s “Soldiers shoot Markus twice”); PowerPyx and GamerGuides say the third bullet kills, open question 6 of the note. The old scene said the androids are shot anyway when {{Markus}} is hit; the template has them escape. A deviant {{Connor}} takes over if {{Markus}} dies here (CONNOR TAKES OVER MARKUS’ MISSION).

nodes.title: Soldiers coming {{Markus}}’ way
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. You make it to the next corridor, and a squad comes round the corner straight toward you. Soldier: “Gamma squad out.” “Tango Stop!” You have only seconds before they see you.

situationWhen.text: You are already wounded.

options.text: JUMP SOLDIERS: run straight at them and take them down.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} runs straight at the soldiers and takes them down before they can raise their rifles.

options.text: CLIMB AWAY: climb the wall on the left, out of their way.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} climbs the wall on the left and gets away above them before they see him.

options.text: TIME OUT: do nothing until the moment passes.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} waits, and the moment passes.

outcomes.wounded: {{Markus}} waits too long. The soldiers see him and open fire; a round hits him, but he drags himself on, wounded.
outcomes.collapse: {{Markus}} waits too long. The soldiers see him and open fire; already wounded, he collapses under the bullets.
outcomes.connor: Elsewhere on the ship, {{Connor}} learns that {{Markus}} has fallen and goes down toward the hold to finish his mission.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s PROGRESS TO THE NEXT CORRIDOR, SOLDIERS COMING MARKUS’ WAY and its three rows JUMP SOLDIERS / CLIMB AWAY / TIME OUT (✗), in the chart’s order (a chart-only choice). PowerPyx: a 10-second timer; “run straight ahead” or “climb the wall on the left”, or “let the 10s timer run out”. Letting the timer run out is offered as an option; it leads to MARKUS WOUNDED, or MARKUS COLLAPSES if he was already wounded. A wounded {{Markus}} dies on the next hit (the chart’s MARKUS WOUNDED / MARKUS COLLAPSES pairs, the wiki’s “if Markus is already wounded”, the template’s “Soldiers shoot Markus twice”); PowerPyx and GamerGuides say the third bullet kills, open question 6 of the note. No arrow (template). The two ways past have no failure branch on the chart, so no risk.

nodes.title: The well
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. You climb down into a well of the hold. Below you, soldiers are chasing a group of androids. Android: “Look out!” Another: “Here they come!” Soldier: “Don’t move!” Android: “We surrender! We surrender, don’t shoot!” Above the soldiers hangs a water reservoir; a pipe on your right holds it in place.

options.text: KNOCK SOLDIERS OUT: pull the pipe and drop the reservoir on them.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} pulls the pipe. The reservoir crashes down and knocks the soldiers out. Android: “{{Markus}}! It’s {{Markus}}!” {{Markus}}: “Go now! Join the others!” The androids escape.

options.text: WALK PAST: keep going toward the hold.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} keeps going. Behind him the soldiers open fire, and the androids are shot.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s ENTER A WELL, ANDROIDS ARE CHASED BY SOLDIERS, and the optional KNOCK SOLDIERS OUT → ANDROIDS ESCAPE (otherwise ANDROIDS ARE SHOT), then APPROACH THE HOLD. In the game it is an optional interaction with a pipe or rope on the right, easily missed (PowerPyx: “If you go too far you will miss it”); here it is offered as a choice. Arrows (template variants “Knock soldiers out” / “Abandoned androids”): {{Jericho}} small up (+1) / small down (−1). No failure branch, so no risk.

nodes.title: Soldiers threaten androids
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, sneaking past soldiers in a lower corridor of the ship on your way to the hold. Ahead, soldiers have caught a group of androids against a wall. Android: “No!.. Please don’t kill us!” Soldier: “On your knees, now!” Android: “Don’t hurt us! We haven’t done anything wrong… Please…” Soldier: “Shut up! Put your hands on your head!”

situationWhen.text: Soldiers shot {{Markus}} down in the corridor above. You told {{North}}: “I’ll go.” Now his mission is yours.
You are wounded and losing blue blood.

options.text: INTERVENE: take on the soldiers.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} goes for the soldiers.

options.text: DON'T INTERVENE: stay hidden and keep going.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} stays out of sight. Behind him the soldiers execute the androids against the wall.

outcomes.saved: {{Connor}} takes the soldiers by surprise and kills them. Android: “You saved us…” {{Connor}}: “Quick, run!” The androids escape.
outcomes.wounded: {{Connor}} goes for the soldiers and is shot, but he brings them down. The androids escape.
outcomes.killed: {{Connor}} goes for the soldiers, but he is already wounded; they shoot him and he goes down.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s DEVIANT {{CONNOR}} IN CORRIDOR (second card), SNEAK PAST SOLDIERS and SOLDIERS THREATEN ANDROIDS with STAY AWAY / INTERVENE, using the template’s buttons INTERVENE / DON’T INTERVENE in its order. INTERVENE leads to KILL THE SOLDIERS or GET SHOT (the fight is a risk roll; no source gives a probability): GET SHOT gives {{CONNOR}} IS WOUNDED and ANDROIDS ESCAPE, or, if he was already wounded, {{CONNOR}} IS SHOT and he is destroyed. DON’T INTERVENE gives ANDROIDS ARE EXECUTED. Reached from the first corridor or when {{Markus}} died before MARKUS IN THE CORRIDOR (the wiki’s takeover list). No arrows: the template shows none for {{Connor}} here (open question 11). The android lines are the template’s.

nodes.title: Soldiers coming
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, moving into the next corridor toward the hold. Boots and voices: soldiers are coming your way. Soldier: “Gamma squad out.” You have seconds. You could rush straight at them, or climb up beside them along the wall and slip past.

situationWhen.text: You are wounded and losing blue blood.

options.text: JUMP SOLDIERS: rush them and take them down.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} charges the soldiers, takes them down and runs on.

options.text: CLIMB BESIDE SOLDIERS: climb along the wall past them.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} climbs up along the wall and slips past the soldiers unseen.

options.text: LOSE TOO MUCH TIME: hesitate until they are on you.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} hesitates too long. Soldier: “Stop!” They open fire.

outcomes.wounded: {{Connor}} hesitates too long. Soldier: “Stop!” They open fire and {{Connor}} is hit; he gets past them, wounded.
outcomes.killed: {{Connor}} hesitates too long. Soldier: “Stop!” They open fire, and the wounded {{Connor}} is shot down.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s NEXT CORRIDOR, SOLDIERS COMING and its three rows JUMP SOLDIERS / CLIMB BESIDE SOLDIERS / LOSE TOO MUCH TIME, offered as the chart draws them (the template has no prompt here, only the soldiers’ lines). LOSE TOO MUCH TIME gives {{CONNOR}} IS WOUNDED, or {{CONNOR}} IS SHOT and the destruction card if he was already wounded (the wound rule as in the corridor). {{Markus}}’s version of this beat has a ten-second timer (PowerPyx); doing nothing is offered as an option rather than a timer. No arrows.

nodes.title: The well
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, climbing down into a well-like shaft deep in the ship. Below you, soldiers are chasing a group of androids. Android: “Look out!” Android: “Here they come!” Soldier: “Don’t move!” Android: “We surrender! We surrender, don’t shoot!” Right beside you, a pipe holds back a reservoir hanging above the soldiers.

options.text: USE THE RESERVOIR: release it onto the soldiers.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} pulls the pipe and the reservoir crashes down on the soldiers, knocking them out. {{Connor}}: “Go! Join the others!” The androids escape, and {{Connor}} heads for the hold.

options.text: WALK PAST: keep going toward the hold.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} keeps going. Behind him the soldiers shoot the androids.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s ENTER A WELL, ANDROIDS ARE CHASED BY SOLDIERS and the optional USE RESERVOIR TO KNOCK SOLDIERS OUT (then ANDROIDS ESCAPE) or, if {{Connor}} walks on, ANDROIDS ARE SHOT. The interaction has no failure branch, so no risk; walking past is offered as the alternative the chart draws. Lines from the template. No arrows for {{Connor}} (the template’s “Knock soldiers out” has none here; {{Markus}}’s version moves {{Jericho}}).

nodes.title: The cargo hall
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, still a machine, pursuing the deviant leader through the ship. In a cargo hall a soldier spins round and levels his rifle at you. Soldier: “Don’t move!” {{Connor}}: “Don’t shoot. I’m on your side.” Soldier: “With us? Are you a human?”

options.text: LIE: claim to be a police officer.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “Obviously! What do I look like? {{DPD}}. I work with Lieutenant {{Hank}}? We’re on a stakeout. If I knew you were coming I would have brought some donuts.” Soldier: “You’re a lucky guy. Another second and I’d have shot you. You should go back up on deck and let us do our job.” {{Connor}}: “You’re right. That’s... Exactly what I’m gonna do.” As soon as the soldier turns away, {{Connor}} resumes his pursuit.

options.text: {{PERKINS}} EXCUSE: name the agent in charge.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I work with Agent {{Perkins}}.” Soldier: “You’re a lucky guy. Another second and I’d have shot you. You should go back up on deck and let us do our job.” {{Connor}}: “You’re right. That’s... Exactly what I’m gonna do.” As soon as the soldier turns away, {{Connor}} resumes his pursuit.

options.text: ATTACK: disarm the soldier.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} lunges at the soldier.

options.text: RUN: make a break for it.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} turns and runs.

outcomes.won: {{Connor}} lunges at the soldier, knocks the rifle aside and takes him down. He resumes his pursuit.
outcomes.lost: {{Connor}} lunges at the soldier, but the soldier gets the better of him and other soldiers close in. Soldier: “Fuckin’ androids…” They shoot {{Connor}} down.
outcomes.run: {{Connor}} turns and runs. Soldier: “Fuckin’ androids…” The soldiers shoot him down before he reaches the door.

nodes.adaptationNote: Machine {{Connor}} only: the chart’s CARGO HALL, STOPPED BY SOLDIER and its four rows, with the template’s buttons LIE (chart ATTEMPT TO PERSUADE), {{PERKINS}} EXCUSE (chart {{PERKINS}} ALIBI), ATTACK and RUN in the template’s order. LIE and {{PERKINS}} EXCUSE lead to RESUME PURSUIT. ATTACK is a fight (a risk roll; no source gives a probability): NEUTRALIZE ASSAILANT resumes the pursuit; FAIL TO NEUTRALIZE ASSAILANT leads, like RUN and SOLDIERS SHOOT {{CONNOR}}, to MACHINE {{CONNOR}} WAS DESTROYED and {{CYBERLIFE}} WILL SEND A NEW {{CONNOR}}. Lines are the template’s. Whether he attacked changes his last line if he later corners {{North}}. No stat change, and no {{Hank}} or {{Amanda}} change on his death (none is sourced for this chapter). Story 1.9.7 fixed the LIE outcome’s name token: it read {{HankAnderson}}, which renders for the subject as “Lieutenant LieutenantReyes”; the game’s line is “I work with Lieutenant Hank Anderson?” (X0205A.CNRBAD.SWAT.PC.X02ACONNOR.HUMAN.3), and the surname is withheld elsewhere, so it is now “Lieutenant {{Hank}}”. The token stays in NAMES because recorded runs re-render their prompts through it. Found by the quote check of the MiKeYROG 100% walkthrough cross-check (no video covers this line; the chapter’s video, eY5wUwZ4R_M, has no captions).

nodes.title: The pounding on the door
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, running with {{Alice}} toward an exit. Soldiers block the way ahead, and you duck into an empty cabin and push the door shut. Boots in the corridor. Then someone pounds on the door, an android, a woman’s voice: “Open up! Open up, they’re coming! Please open the door!” {{Alice}}: “She’ll die out there {{Kara}}! Open it! Open the door!” The android: “They’re gonna kill me! I’m begging you, please! Open up! Let me in!”

options.text: OPEN: let her in.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} opens the door. The android stumbles in, and the soldier behind her opens fire.

options.text: DON'T OPEN: keep the door shut.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “We’ll be killed if we open up!..” {{Alice}}: “No… {{Kara}}…” Outside, shots, and the pounding stops. A soldier: “There’s more down there! Follow me!” The boots move on. {{Kara}}: “There was nothing we could do. We have to go!” They slip out of the cabin.

outcomes.fought: {{Kara}} opens the door. The android stumbles in and is shot by the soldier behind her, who forces his way into the cabin. {{Kara}} throws herself at him and fights him off until he goes down. {{Alice}}: “{{KARA}}! Are you all right, {{Kara}}?” {{Kara}}: “Yes, I’m… I’m fine. We can’t stay here.” Down the corridor, another soldier: “There’s more down there! Follow me!” {{Kara}} and {{Alice}} get out of the cabin.
outcomes.captured: {{Kara}} opens the door. The android stumbles in and is shot by the soldier behind her, who forces his way into the cabin. {{Kara}} goes for him, but he overpowers her and holds her at gunpoint until more soldiers arrive. {{Kara}} and {{Alice}} are captured and taken off the ship.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s RUN TOWARD EXIT, SOLDIERS BLOCK THE WAY, HIDE and ANDROID SEEKS SHELTER, then the choice OPEN THE DOOR / KEEP THE DOOR CLOSED; the buttons are the template’s OPEN and DON’T OPEN. Arrows (template, on the choice): OPEN {{Alice}} small up, DON’T OPEN {{Alice}} small down. OPEN leads to ANDROID ENTERS BUT IS SHOT and a fight with the soldier, a quick-time event with a failure branch (FIGHT BACK → ESCAPE CABIN, or CAPTURED → KARA & ALICE CAPTURED), so it carries an unsourced risk. DON’T OPEN leads to SOLDIERS SHOOT ANDROID AND MOVE ON and ESCAPE CABIN. Corrected from the old scene: the android is a woman (“She’ll die out there”).

nodes.title: {{Josh}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, approaching the hold. Ahead of you, {{Josh}} is fighting a soldier hand to hand and losing. You: “{{Josh}}…”

situationWhen.text: You are already wounded.

options.text: INTERVENE: go to help him.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} throws himself at the soldier.

options.text: HIDE: stay out of sight.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} stays hidden. The soldier shoots {{Josh}} and moves on. {{Markus}} goes to him. {{Josh}}: “That’s what causes violence… Don’t become like them, {{Markus}}…” He dies in {{Markus}}’s arms. Soldier, somewhere close: “Over there!”

outcomes.saved: {{Markus}} overpowers the soldier and neutralizes him. {{Josh}}: “Quick, this way!” {{Markus}}: “Find {{North}}! I’ll join you later!” {{Josh}} escapes.
outcomes.sacrifice: {{Markus}} loses the upper hand, and the soldier turns his rifle on him. {{Josh}} throws himself in the way and is shot. {{Markus}} kneels beside him. {{Josh}}: “That’s what causes violence… Don’t become like them, {{Markus}}…” He dies. Soldier, somewhere close: “Over there!”
outcomes.collapse: {{Markus}} loses the upper hand, and his wound gives way; he collapses. The soldier shoots {{Josh}}, then turns on {{Markus}}. Soldier: “Got you, motherfucker.” {{North}}: “{{Markus}}! No...”
outcomes.connor: Elsewhere on the ship, {{Connor}} learns that {{Markus}} has fallen and goes down toward the hold to finish his mission.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s APPROACH THE HOLD, JOSH FIGHTING A SOLDIER and INTERVENE / STAY AWAY (the template’s buttons INTERVENE / HIDE). INTERVENE is a QTE (unsourced risk): NEUTRALIZE SOLDIERS → JOSH ESCAPES, or LOSE THE UPPER HAND → JOSH SACRIFICES HIMSELF → COMFORT JOSH (not wounded), or MARKUS COLLAPSES → JOSH IS SHOT BY THE SOLDIER and {{Markus}} dies (already wounded). HIDE → SOLDIER SHOT JOSH → COMFORT JOSH. Arrows (template): NEUTRALIZE {{Jericho}} +1, {{Josh}} large up (+2); LOSE THE UPPER HAND {{Jericho}} −1; HIDE {{Jericho}} −1. The sacrifice’s condition is disputed (GamerGuides and a commenter: a good relationship with {{Josh}}; another commenter: only an unwounded {{Markus}}): the chart’s not-wounded reading is used, and the sacrifice does not count as a hit. A wounded {{Markus}} dies on the next hit (the chart’s MARKUS WOUNDED / MARKUS COLLAPSES pairs, the wiki’s “if Markus is already wounded”, the template’s “Soldiers shoot Markus twice”); PowerPyx and GamerGuides say the third bullet kills, open question 6 of the note. Old scene: a failure killed {{Josh}} and hit {{Markus}} even when unwounded.

nodes.title: {{Josh}} is dying
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, approaching the hold of the ship, where the explosives are.
facts: On your way to the hold you found {{Josh}} dying of his wounds and stayed with him for a moment.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} reaches the hold.
outcomes.takeover: {{Markus}} has been shot down. {{Connor}}: “I’ll go.” He takes over {{Markus}}’s mission and makes for the hold himself.
outcomes.josh: Near the hold {{Connor}} finds {{Josh}} on the floor, mortally wounded. {{Josh}}: “It’s all over… This is the end… Of {{Jericho}}…” {{Connor}} kneels beside him until he is gone. Soldier: “Over there!” {{Connor}} slips into the hold.
outcomes.no-josh: {{Connor}} slips past the soldiers and into the hold.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s {{CONNOR}} TAKES OVER {{MARKUS}}’ MISSION (when {{Markus}} died after MARKUS IN THE CORRIDOR and before the hold, the wiki’s takeover list), APPROACH HOLD, {{JOSH}} IS DYING, COMFORT {{JOSH}} and IN THE HOLD WITH DEVIANT {{CONNOR}}, in one event. {{Connor}} cannot save {{Josh}}: a commenter, “only Marcus has the option to save Josh”; the wiki: “If Markus is not there, then Josh’s survival is based on whether Connor dies before seeing him.” So {{Josh}} dies here if he is still alive. {{Josh}}’s line is the template’s. No stat change.

nodes.title: The breach
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, fleeing through the lower decks with {{Alice}}. Ahead, a breach has been torn in the hull, and through it you can see the dark river. Androids are running for it. You: “A way out! We’re safe, {{Alice}}!” A soldier: “Stop!”

options.text: RUN FOR THE BREACH: run for the opening with {{Alice}}.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} runs for the breach.

outcomes.breach: {{Kara}} pulls {{Alice}} along and almost reaches the breach, but the soldiers open fire on the androids running for it. Bodies fall all around them.
outcomes.leg: {{Kara}} cannot run fast enough. A bullet hits her leg and she goes down on the deck. {{Alice}}: “{{Kara}}! You’re bleeding!”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s KARA FLEES (checkpoint; between PowerPyx’s zooms, string `K.NEARCABIN`) and TRY TO ESCAPE (string `K.TOWARDSHOLE`), with the outcome group ALMOST REACH THE BREACH / FAIL TO RUN: a button-mash (PowerPyx: “successfully mash… Fail to Run: don’t mash and {{Kara}} gets shot”), here an unsourced risk. Success leads to SOLDIERS SHOOT AT THE CROWD; failure to KARA IS SHOT IN THE LEG. No arrow. New scene: the old benchmark had no failure here.

nodes.title: The soldiers fire on the crowd

You are wounded and losing blue blood.

options.text: TRY TO ESCAPE: run for the opening in the hull.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} runs for the opening in the hull.

outcomes.late: {{Connor}} is too slow. Ahead of him {{North}} reaches the opening and jumps into the river; soldiers cut {{Connor}} down before he can follow.
outcomes.made-intact: {{Connor}} catches up with the others at the opening and jumps into the river.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s DEVIANT {{CONNOR}} IN CORRIDOR (third card), JOIN THE OTHERS, TRY TO ESCAPE and the outcome group OUT OF TIME (then {{NORTH}} JUMPS, {{SIMON}} JUMPS WITH HER, DEVIANT {{CONNOR}} WAS DESTROYED ON THE SHIP and {{CYBERLIFE}} WILL SEND A NEW {{CONNOR}}) / MADE IT (then {{CONNOR}} JUMPS, {{SIMON}} and {{NORTH}} JUMPS WITH HIM, {{CONNOR}} ESCAPED WITH {{JERICHO}}’S PEOPLE). nodes.title: At the grave
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, alone at {{Carl}}’s grave. There is no one to answer you. What do you tell him?

options.text: HEARTFUL: tell him you are lost, and that everything you touch turns to dust.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “I’m lost, {{Carl}}… I just wanted us to live in peace, but… everything I touch just turns to dust.”

options.text: MOURNFUL: tell him how much you miss him, and the home you had.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “I miss you, {{Carl}}… You can’t know how much I miss you… I’d give anything for us to be able to roll back the clock… I had a home, I had a loving father… We were happy... I was happy... and I didn’t even know it…”

options.text: REGRETFUL: wonder whether he would still be alive if you had defended yourself against {{Leo}}.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “You always said that living was about making choices… So what if I chose to defend myself against {{Leo}}? Maybe you could still be alive… Maybe a lot of things could’ve been different. Unless all of this was just meant to happen…”

options.text: REFLECTIVE: tell him he never said that freedom would cost so much.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “You said I should never let anyone tell me who I was… But you didn’t say that there was such a high price to pay for it… That freedom wasn’t a gift, that it was a fight, but… I don’t know. Maybe that’s what you were trying to tell me…”
